:class:ObservationNoiseWrapper for a batched brax / playground stack (above its VmapWrapper, as build_env_from_id builds it). Its step takes no key: the wrapper's own lives in the state's info, tiled over the envs (row 0 is read), and is split at every reset and step.

docs.title: init_norm_info
docs.text:
init_norm_info(batch_size, obs_shape, returns=False)

Initialise running stats with leading axis batch_size.

The leading axis is redundant (online_normalize collapses it on every update, so rows carry identical values) but it is load-bearing for env-side callers: env-side stats live inside the env state pytree, which Brax's VmapWrapper vmaps over the n_envs axis. Shrinking the stats to (1, *) would break that vmap with a mismatched-axis error. Agent-side callers should pass batch_size=1 instead (see init_agent_obs_norm).

docs.title: ajax.environments.obs_norm
docs.text:
Agent-side running observation normalization.

Lives inside CollectorState.obs_norm_info so stats are part of agent_state and thread through naturally. Normalization is applied at every actor/critic apply_fn boundary; stats are updated only at collection time (online interaction and BC dataset prep). The replay buffer stores RAW augmented observations so changing stats don't poison old samples; we re-normalize at sample time.

Why agent-side and not env-wrapper-side: when augment_obs_with_expert_state is on, the expert_state (PID integrators etc.) is appended AFTER the env step, in the collector. The env wrapper can't see those dims, so its running stats don't cover them. Agent-side normalization wraps the full augmented vector.

docs.title: init_agent_obs_norm
docs.text:
init_agent_obs_norm(obs_dim)

Initialise running stats for an obs vector of size obs_dim.

Stats are stored with leading shape 1 (not n_envs): online_normalize reduces the per-env axis on every update so all envs would share the same scalar stats anyway, and apply_obs_norm only needs the per-feature mean/var. The size-1 leading axis preserves broadcasting against batched obs (*, obs_dim) while saving an n_envs× memory factor on every checkpoint and vmap broadcast.

docs.title: update_obs_norm
docs.text:
update_obs_norm(obs, info, raw_columns=0)

Update running stats with obs and return (normalized_obs, new_info).

obs shape: (n_envs, obs_dim). When info is None the call is a no-op (returns input unchanged) so call sites can stay unconditional. The leading raw_columns stay raw (see online_normalize).

docs.title: apply_obs_norm
docs.text:
apply_obs_norm(obs, info)

Normalize obs using existing stats (no update). Used at every actor/critic apply_fn site that consumes obs sampled from the buffer or carried by the eval scan, so stats updates stay localised to the collection sites. Falls back to raw obs while the running stats are still empty (count == 0), avoiding a divide-by-≈0 at step 1 before any update.

The statistics cover the agent's own observation, the leading columns; what is appended after it stays raw: the expert's action (interaction.augment_obs) and a critic's action, already in action units, as the env's raw_columns keep a PID's terms raw.

docs.title: ajax.environments.system_class
docs.text:
System classes: distributions over environment parameters.

A system class is a distribution p(S) over the dynamics of an environment, represented as a distribution over its EnvParams. It is the object that turns one environment into a family of environments for domain randomisation, meta-learning and in-context control (Busetto et al. 2024, "One controller to rule them all", arXiv:2411.06482).

Sampling returns batched params: every leaf carries a leading axis of size n, one entry per parallel environment. :func:ajax.environments .interaction.reset / :func:~ajax.environments.interaction.step detect that leading axis and vmap over it (gymnax only: brax envs do not take per-step params). APG, DreamerV3 and TDMPC2 train on them; the agents of the shared loop compile them as a static argument and refuse them when built (ActorCritic.supports_batched_env_params).

docs.title: SystemClass
docs.text:
Base class: a distribution over EnvParams.

Subclasses implement :meth:sample. The nominal params are kept so callers can always fall back to the reference system (evaluation on the nominal plant, curriculum stage 1, ...).

docs.title: UniformPerturbation dataclass
docs.text:
UniformPerturbation(nominal, fields, scale=0.05)

Bases: SystemClass

Independent uniform relative perturbation of selected parameter fields.

Each listed field p is drawn as p * (1 + U(-scale, scale)), independently per field and per sampled system (a vector or matrix field is scaled by one factor per system); every other field stays at its nominal value. This is the meta-dataset construction of Busetto et al. 2024 (there: scale=0.05 on the 19 evaporator constants).

fields must name attributes of the nominal EnvParams; a typo raises at construction rather than silently sampling nothing.

docs.title: env_params_is_batched
docs.text:
env_params_is_batched(params)

True when params carries one system per env along a leading axis.

A batched params (from :meth:SystemClass.sample or :func:broadcast_env_params) has every leaf with the same leading axis. An unbatched one always has at least one rank-0 leaf (gymnax's max_steps_in_episode at minimum), even when other fields are vectors or matrices (e.g. a plant's state-space model), so "any leaf has rank >= 1" would misclassify those.

docs.text:

Replicate an unbatched params n times along a new leading axis.

Used to run a single nominal system through the batched code path (e.g. a fixed system during the first curriculum stage). Every leaf (scalar, vector or matrix) gets the new leading axis; an already batched params is returned unchanged.

docs.title: ajax.environments.model_reference
docs.text:
Model-reference tracking tasks on top of any gymnax environment.

Model-reference control (Busetto et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.06482, §2) asks a controller to make a plant's measured output y_k follow the output y^d_k of a reference model M driven by a user reference r_k. This module turns any gymnax env into such a task:

  • :class:StepReference is the reference distribution p(R): piecewise-constant random steps of random amplitude and duration.
  • :class:LinearReferenceModel is a discrete-time linear M (x_{k+1} = A x_k + B r_k, y^d_k = C x_k + D r_k); the paper's first-order model is :meth:LinearReferenceModel.first_order.
  • :class:ModelReferenceWrapper exposes the controller's view of the problem: observation [e_k, u_{k-1}] (tracking error and previous input, optionally followed by the raw plant observation) and reward -||y^d_k - y_k||^2, so the undiscounted return is the negative closed-loop matching cost of eq. (9) and the paper's M-RMSE is sqrt(-return / horizon).

Every operation is plain jnp so the wrapper is differentiable when the inner env is (see :mod:ajax.environments.differentiable), and it composes with :mod:ajax.environments.system_class batched params because the wrapper is per-env (Ajax vmaps reset/step).

docs.title: StepReference
docs.text:
Random piecewise-constant references r_{[0, N-1]}.

Each segment holds a value drawn uniformly in [min_value, max_value] for a duration drawn uniformly in [min_duration, max_duration] steps (both inclusive), independently per output. The paper's evaporator case uses values in [20, 25] % and durations in [20, 50] s at 1 s sampling over N = 100.

docs.title: sample
docs.text:
sample(rng)

One reference sequence, shape (horizon, n_outputs).

docs.title: LinearReferenceModel
docs.text:
Discrete-time linear reference model M.

x_{k+1} = A x_k + B r_k, y^d_k = C x_k + D r_k with A: (nx, nx), B: (nx, ny), C: (ny, nx), D: (ny, ny).

docs.title: first_order classmethod
docs.text:
first_order(
    a=0.4286, b=0.7143, c=0.5669, d=0.2914, n_outputs=1
)

Diagonal first-order model, one independent channel per output.

Defaults are the paper's eq. (12): x_{k+1} = 0.4286 x_k + 0.7143 r_k, y^d_k = 0.5669 x_k + 0.2914 r_k (unit DC gain).

docs.title: init_state
docs.text:
init_state(y0, r0)

State whose output equals the plant's initial output.

The paper initialises x^M_0 at the plant's initial condition so the desired trajectory starts where the plant starts. Solves C x = y0 - D r0 in the least-squares sense.

docs.title: ajax.environments.pid_terms
docs.text:
The error terms a PID controller acts on, carried in the observation.

A PID controller computes u_t = Kp e_t + Ki I_t + Kd D_t from the tracking error e_t = target_t - current_t, its integral I_t and its difference D_t. :class:PIDTermsWrapper puts (e_t, I_t, D_t) in front of a gymnax env's observation, so a policy reading them stays a function of the observation: every agent (replay or on-policy, with or without memory) trains on the wrapped env unchanged, and training and evaluation, which step the same wrapped env, see the same terms. The PID policy (:class:ajax.modules.pid_actor.PIDPolicy) reads them there.

The terms are the discrete-time PID's with sampling period dt (backward-difference form, as in Astrom & Hagglund, Advanced PID Control, 2006, cited from memory, unverified)::

I_t = clip(I_{t-1} + dt * e_t, -integral_limit, integral_limit),  I_{-1} = 0
D_t = (e_t - e_{t-1}) / dt,                                       D_0 = 0

The clip is clamping anti-windup (integral_limit=None: no clip). Every episode starts afresh, the auto-reset ones included: the integral restarts from dt * e_0 and the difference from 0, so no term carries over from the previous episode.

The wrapper declares the terms raw (raw_obs_columns): Ajax's observation normalisers leave them in the env's units, so gains acting on them are a PID's, and normalise the rest of the observation as usual.

docs.title: ajax.environments.differentiable
docs.text:
Differentiable closed-loop rollouts (backpropagation through the simulator).

The collectors in :mod:ajax.environments.interaction wrap every env step in stop_gradient: RL agents treat the environment as a black box. This module is the opposite path, for analytic policy gradient methods that differentiate an objective through the dynamics themselves (Busetto et al. 2024's in-context controller, APG/SHAC-style trainers, ...):

  • :func:with_transition_gradients configures a (possibly wrapped) gymnax env so its transitions keep gradients. gymnax >= 1.0 detaches them by default and only some envs support the opt-in (Pendulum, MountainCarContinuous, PointRobot, Reacher, Swimmer at the time of writing); unsupported envs raise instead of silently training on zero gradients.
  • :func:closed_loop_rollout runs a fixed-horizon closed loop between a stateful policy and the env with no stop_gradient anywhere, so jax.grad of any function of the returned :class:Rollout flows through the policy, the environment, and the policy's carry across time (BPTT over the whole horizon).

Gymnax only: brax/playground envs take no per-step params and have their own (MJX) gradient story.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
Time-major closed-loop trajectory, leaves shaped (T, B, ...).

obs[t] is what the policy saw at step t, action[t] what it applied, reward[t] / done[t] / next_obs[t] the env's response. resets[t] is the episode-start flag the policy was given at step t (True at t=0 and after a done). info is the env's per-step info dict with every leaf stacked over time (e.g. a tracking wrapper's desired output), for metrics that need more than the reward. policy_action[t] is the policy's own action, before an action_map mapped it onto the env (None without one).

docs.title: ajax.environments.utils.agent_action_to_env
docs.text:
agent_action_to_env(action, env, env_params=None)

Map an agent action in [-1, 1] to the env's action bounds.

Every Ajax env step carrying an agent's or an expert's action calls it: every continuous agent acts in [-1, 1] (squashed or not), whatever the env's box. action is [n_envs, *action_shape]. Continuous actions are clipped to [-1, 1] and, on every dimension of the Box with finite bounds [low, high], mapped affinely onto them: c + h * clip(a, -1, 1), with centre c = (high + low) / 2 and half-range h = (high - low) / 2 (CleanRL's action_bias and action_scale). This is DreamerV3's ClipAction + NormalizeAction (a dimension with an infinite bound keeps the clipped action) and TD-MPC2's action scaling. For [-1, 1] bounds -- every brax / playground env, gymnax envs like MountainCarContinuous -- the map is exactly the clip, even when the bounds are traced; gymnax Pendulum's torque is [-2, 2]. Per-env (batched) gymnax params (ajax.environments.system_class) give per-env bounds: env e's action is mapped with its own system's bounds. Discrete actions pass through. Replay stores the agent's raw action, not this one. :func:env_action_to_agent is the inverse.

docs.title: ajax.environments.utils.env_action_to_agent
docs.text:
env_action_to_agent(action, env, env_params=None)

Map an action in the env's bounds to agent units, [-1, 1].

The inverse of :func:agent_action_to_env on the env's box, (a - c) / h, with the same action layout and per-env bounds. It does not clip: an action outside the box stays outside [-1, 1]. It is the identity on [-1, 1] boxes, on a dimension with an infinite bound and on discrete actions.

docs.title: ajax.environments.utils.ExpertInAgentUnits
docs.text:
ExpertInAgentUnits(expert, env, env_params=None)

An expert written in env units, read in agent units ([-1, 1]).

What the expert returns -- expert(obs), a stateful expert(state, obs)'s action, step_with_gains's action -- goes through :func:env_action_to_agent's map, unclipped. init_state, learnable_fields, anchor_gains and step_with_gains exist exactly when the expert's do (hasattr still tells a stateful expert). It hashes by identity, for jit's static arguments.

Its bounds are one (A,) box read from concrete params, also inside jit (static params): a stateless expert is also vmapped over single observations, where per-env bounds would broadcast its action. Per-env boxes that differ raise.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text: An extension adds a research feature to any agent whose loop folds the phases it uses. The user guide shows how to use them and Writing an extension how to add one.

docs.title: ajax.extensions.base
docs.text:
The Extension framework — composable research features for any agent.

An :class:Extension is a research feature (expert guidance, observation augmentation, online behavioural cloning, target modifiers, exploration schemes, instrumentation, …) that attaches to any agent without bloating the agent's own file. It implements only the lifecycle phases it touches; an agent's training loop folds every extension through each phase, in list order.

docs.title: Design contract
docs.text:
• Static. Extensions are plain Python objects passed as static arguments to the jitted training step, so the fold unrolls at trace time (a Python for over a fixed tuple — no dynamic dispatch). Every extension must therefore be hashable: the default id-based hash is fine for a one-off instance; a @dataclass(frozen=True) is preferred for instances carrying config, so the JIT cache is reused across equivalent runs.
  • State lives in the pytree. An extension never stores mutable state on self — only frozen config. Anything that changes during training is a pytree returned by :meth:Extension.init_state and carried in BaseAgentState.ext_state (one entry per extension; the default () means stateless, zero overhead).
  • No-op by default. Every phase method has a default that is the identity / 0.0 / {} / unchanged-state, so an extension is exactly as invasive as the phases it overrides, and an empty :class:ExtensionStack is genuinely zero-cost.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
init_state build the extension's pytree state (once, on fresh init) pretrain one-shot, before the training loop (MC/BC pre-training) on_target transform the TD / value target critic_loss extra additive critic-loss term (summed over extensions) actor_loss extra additive actor-loss term (summed over extensions) action override the collection-time action (None = defer; the last non-None proposal in the stack wins) eval_action override the evaluation-time action (same rule) transform_action make the executed action a function of the policy's and the expert's (residual RL), in collection, the losses and evaluation post_update hook after the update step (φ-refresh, schedules, …) eval_metrics extra metrics, merged into the eval log

on_target, critic_loss and actor_loss may return (value, metrics) instead of their value: metrics, a dict of scalars named <extension>/<metric>, is logged with the update's own metrics (the last update's, or the mean over the update's epochs and minibatches, as the agent logs its own). Two extensions logging one name raise.

docs.title: Phase batches
docs.text: The batch dict of a phase holds the keys :data:PHASE_BATCH_KEYS lists on every agent that folds it; an agent may add its own (read its fold call), and an extension raises on a key it needs and does not find, rather than return a no-op. gamma is None for an average-reward agent, dones is where the target cut the bootstrap and targets the target, held constant; the critic (DQN's and PQN's q_state) and the actor come at the differentiated parameters. The replay agents' raw_observations is None in a run without an expert, whose replay does not keep them. a_expert is the agent's expert_policy's action at each row, stored at collection from the expert's state along the trajectory; None without one.

docs.title: ExtensionContext
docs.text:
Shared context handed to every extension phase.

step and rng are traced; total_steps is static so it can drive Python-level decisions (e.g. schedule lengths) at trace time. The pretrain phase of a run on ajax.agents.loop.TrainLoop also gets its static env_args and, off-policy, its update(agent_state, experience) -> (agent_state, aux) and replay buffer, so an extension can run the agent's own update; each is None where the run has none.

docs.title: ajax.extensions.expert
docs.text:
Expert-guidance research features as composable :class:Extensions.

  • :class:OnlineBC — value-weighted decaying BC loss term.
  • :class:ImitationLoss — plain BC loss term towards the expert.
  • :class:ResidualPolicy — execute clip(a_expert + scale·a_pi).
  • :class:JSRLCurriculum — per-episode expert→learner handoff.
  • :class:ExpertValueMetrics — the critic at the expert's actions, logged.

Each extension carries only frozen config on self; the maths are the functions below. The expert is SAC's expert_policy: OnlineBC, ResidualPolicy and JSRLCurriculum read the expert action SAC computes. ImitationLoss holds its own expert, and reads the actions the agent stored when that expert is the agent's.

docs.title: OnlineBC dataclass
docs.text:
OnlineBC(
    bc_coef=1.0, critic_warmup_frac=0.15, name="online_bc"
)

Bases: Extension

Online, value-weighted, warmup-decaying behavioural-cloning term.

A bc_coef · w(s) · ||μ_θ(s) - a_expert||² penalty (:func:compute_online_bc_loss) that decays to zero once the training fraction exceeds critic_warmup_frac. It reads the actor's mean action (pi_mean), the expert's action (a_expert, which SAC puts in its actor-loss batch) and the observations from the batch, and the frozen expert critic phi with its value range (expert_critic_params, expert_v_min, expert_v_max) and the critic phi is applied with from the agent's state, which :class:MCPretrain fits (refused without it). The expert's action is the agent's expert_policy's, so an agent without one refuses it (requires agent_expert); it raises on a batch without a_expert (an agent other than SAC). Until phi* exists the term is 0.

docs.title: ImitationLoss dataclass
docs.text:
ImitationLoss(
    expert_policy,
    coef=1.0,
    q_filter=False,
    anneal_frac=None,
    target="expert",
    alpha=None,
    reads_stored_expert=False,
    buffer=None,
    action_scale=None,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    name="imitation_loss",
)

Bases: Extension

Behavioural-cloning regulariser: coef · mean((μ(s) - a_E(s))²) / 4.

Same form as the actor-side BC term of TD3+BC (Fujimoto & Gu, 2021), with a frozen expert's action as the target: μ(s) is the actor's mean action (pi.mean(), which is TD3's deterministic action), a_E(s) the expert's action, held constant: its call on the raw observation, or, when it is the agent's expert_policy, the action collection stored from its tracked state (which a stateful expert, a PID with its integral, needs). The mean runs over batch and action dims; / 4 maps the squared distance of two actions in [-1, 1] to [0, 1]. Unlike :class:OnlineBC the term is unweighted and needs no pre-trained expert critic.

q_filter=True counts only the rows where the critic rates the expert's action above the policy's (:func:q_filter_weight, at μ(s)) and still divides by every row, as the paper's fixed λ2 = 1/N_D does: the Q-filtered BC of Nair, McGrew, Andrychowicz, Zaremba and Abbeel (ICRA 2018, Sec. IV-C, eq. 8). Deviations: replay rows labelled with the expert's action, not a demonstration buffer (the replay's expert flags would restore it); coef on the BC term, not the paper's λ1 = 1e-3 on the RL term and λ2; the policy's mean action and the minimum over the agent's critics (TD3's actor reads its first, REDQ's the mean of its ensemble), not DDPG's one critic. The filter needs a Q critic, which SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC and AVG put in their actor-loss batch (critic_state); a state-value critic (PPO, APO) cannot rate an action. It refuses :class:ResidualPolicy, whose critic reads the executed action. imitation/q_filter_frac logs, at each evaluation, the share of a replay batch the filter keeps (every agent but AVG, which keeps no replay).

With anneal_frac the term is multiplied by a weight falling linearly from 1 to 0 at that fraction of training (:func:anneal_weight), as in kickstarting (Schmitt et al., 2018, Kickstarting Deep Reinforcement Learning, arXiv:1803.03835, eqs. 2-3), whose distillation weight on the teacher decays so the student ends on its own RL loss. Deviations from kickstarting: a squared error on the mean action instead of the cross-entropy between the teacher's and the student's policies (the expert is deterministic: it gives an action, not a distribution); a linear schedule set by anneal_frac instead of the weights population-based training tunes. None keeps the weight at 1.

target="replay" clones the replayed rows' own actions (actions, which SAC, TD3, REDQ and ASAC put in their actor-loss batch) instead of an expert's: logged data needs no expert, and expert_policy may be None. alpha makes the actor loss TD3+BC's (Fujimoto and Gu, 2021), λ · (the agent's own) + coef · mean((μ(s) - a)²) with λ = alpha / mean|Q_1(s, μ(s))| (:func:td3bc_lambda), the actions compared in the env's units and without the / 4: the term adds (λ - 1) times the agent's own loss (agent_loss in its actor batch), already counted. On TD3, whose own loss is -mean Q_1, that is the paper's -λ mean Q + mean((π(s) - a)²); anneal_frac and the filter act on the cloning part only. With both, on TD3, a transition dataset trained offline (train_offline) and normalize_observations=True (the dataset's statistics, sqrt(var + 1e-8) in place of the reference's std + 1e-3), it is TD3+BC.

TD3, REDQ, ASAC, APO, SAC and PPO put pi_mean and raw_observations in their actor-loss batch, and all but PPO (which takes no expert) the stored a_expert; an agent whose batch has no pi_mean (a discrete-action policy) raises at trace time.

docs.title: ResidualPolicy dataclass
docs.text:
ResidualPolicy(scale=1.0, name='residual_policy')

Bases: Extension

Residual RL (Johannink et al. 2019).

The executed action is clip(a_expert + scale·a_pi, -1, 1): SAC's action pipeline applies :meth:transform_action at collection (its warmup samples uniformly), and the actor's policy gradient, the TD-target bootstrap and evaluation flow through the same transform. Its presence alone turns residual RL on, with SAC's expert policy; transform_action is a phase only SAC runs, so the other agents refuse it.

docs.title: JSRLCurriculum dataclass
docs.text:
JSRLCurriculum(
    episode_length=1000,
    decay_frac=0.5,
    name="jsrl_curriculum",
)

Bases: Extension

True JSRL per-episode handoff (Uchendu et al. 2023).

While step_in_episode < H_t the expert acts; otherwise the learner does. H_t decays linearly from episode_length to 0 over the first decay_frac fraction of training.

The :meth:action phase owns the per-episode substitution. It reads post_warmup_action and expert_action off the SAC action pipeline's batch dict (the same dict :class:EDGEExploration and :class:~ajax.extensions.target_mods.ValueBox use) and per-env step_in_episode off agent_state.collector_state; the SAC pipeline still owns the step_in_episode increment/reset (in :func:collect_experience). It writes _jsrl_use_expert back, which the pipeline reads to flag the steps the expert took.

Evaluations log the guide horizon H_t (jsrl/horizon) and the share of envs the expert drove on the last collection step (jsrl/expert_frac).

Substitute the expert action while step_in_episode < H_t.

docs.title: ExpertValueMetrics dataclass
docs.text:
ExpertValueMetrics(
    buffer=None,
    expert_policy=None,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    name="expert_value_metrics",
)

Bases: Extension

The critic at the expert's actions, logged at each evaluation, on a replay batch: value/q_expert_mean, the mean of min_k Q_k(s, a_E); value/q_gap, that minus the same at the batch's actions (above 0: the critic rates the expert above what was done); and, once :class:~ajax.extensions.pretrain.MCPretrain has fitted φ*, value/phi_star_q_gap_ood, the mean |min_k Q_φ*(s, a_E) - min_k Q(s, a_E)|.

One replay batch per evaluation pays for them, not a critic pass (two with φ*) per update for three logged numbers. a_E is the expert's action stored at collection. A replay agent with an expert_policy (SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC) binds its replay buffer, its expert and its observation augmentation.

docs.title: residual_action_transform
docs.text:
residual_action_transform(actions, a_expert, scale=1.0)

Residual RL: executed action is clip(a_expert + scale * a_pi, -1, 1).

The critic was trained on (s, executed_action) tuples, so the policy gradient must flow through Q(s, executed_action), not Q(s, a_pi). scale follows Johannink et al. 2019; values < 1 keep the initial behaviour close to the expert when the policy is randomly initialised.

The Q-filter of Nair et al. 2018 (eq. 8), (batch, 1): 1 where the critic's ensemble minimum rates the expert's action above the policy's, min_k Q_k(s, a_E) > min_k Q_k(s, π(s)), else 0; held constant.

docs.title: td3bc_lambda
docs.text:
td3bc_lambda(critic_state, observations, pi_mean, alpha)

TD3+BC's lambda = alpha / mean|Q_1(s, pi(s))|, held constant, with Q_1 the first critic, the one TD3's actor follows (sfujim/TD3_BC@8791ad7, TD3_BC.py:141-143: lmbda = alpha / Q.abs().mean().detach(), actor loss -lmbda * Q.mean() + mse_loss(pi, action)).

docs.title: ajax.extensions.pretrain
docs.text:
One-shot pre-training research features as composable :class:Extensions.

CloningPretrain, MCPretrain and BellmanPretrain run once, before the training loop (the pretrain phase, skipped on resume); PhiRefresh refreshes MCPretrain's critic during training.

  • :class:CloningPretrain — behaviour cloning of the actor on an expert's rollouts.
  • :class:MCPretrain — regress a frozen expert critic on Monte-Carlo returns, then (optionally) lightly nudge the online critic toward it.
  • :class:BellmanPretrain — Bellman-bootstrapped critic pre-training on the expert buffer.
  • :class:PhiRefresh — periodic self-consistent refresh of the frozen expert critic during training (the post_update phase).
  • :class:PriorData — a transition dataset in the replay, and the agent's own updates on it before acting.

docs.title: MCPretrainAux

docs.title: PretrainLosses
docs.text: A pretraining fit's first and last loss, kept in its extension's state for the evaluations' log. NaN before the fit, when it takes no step, and in a run resumed from a checkpoint saved before they were kept (added_fields, :func:ajax.checkpoint.restore_into).

docs.title: CloningPretrain dataclass
docs.text:
CloningPretrain(
    expert_policy,
    n_steps=100000,
    epochs=10,
    batch_size=64,
    skip_actor=False,
    reset_log_std=False,
    reset_actor_head=False,
    env_args=None,
    actor_optimizer_args=None,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    augment_obs_with_expert_state=False,
    use_train_frac=False,
    name="cloning_pretrain",
)

Bases: Extension

Behaviour cloning of the actor on an expert's rollouts, before training.

Rolls expert_policy out for n_steps steps per env, observing as the agent does, then fits the actor to its actions on observations standardised with the dataset's statistics (:func:ajax.agents.cloning.pre_train: epochs passes in batches of batch_size, at the actor's learning rate). The agent's observation statistics start from the dataset's. skip_actor leaves the actor as initialised; after cloning, reset_log_std puts its log-std (head or parameter) back at its initial values and reset_actor_head also its output head (the mean layer, or a PID actor's gains). Evaluations log the mean loss of cloning's first and last epoch (cloning/first_loss, cloning/last_loss).

The fields after reset_actor_head are the agent's context, filled by :meth:bind_to_agent (SAC, REDQ, TD3 and APO do).

docs.title: MCPretrain dataclass
docs.text:
MCPretrain(
    expert_policy,
    n_mc_steps=10000,
    n_mc_episodes=100,
    n_steps=5000,
    use_online_light=True,
    online_light_steps=500,
    online_light_lr_scale=0.1,
    env_args=None,
    network_args=None,
    critic_optimizer_args=None,
    num_critics=2,
    gamma=None,
    reward_scale=None,
    use_train_frac=False,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    expert_state_aug_dim=0,
    use_phi_refresh=False,
    name="mc_pretrain",
)

Bases: Extension

Monte-Carlo critic pre-training.

Regresses a frozen expert critic φ* on unbiased MC returns from expert rollouts, persists φ* + the value range v_min/v_max on the agent state, and — when use_online_light is set — applies a weak supervised nudge of the online critic toward φ* to reduce seed-to-seed variance at initialisation.

Building φ* needs the agent's env, critic network and optimiser config, gamma and reward_scale: the fields after the hyperparameters, which the agent fills through :meth:bind_to_agent (only SAC does). φ* trains with that optimiser config as it is, so the agent's weight_decay (like its gradient clipping and learning- rate schedule) also decays φ* while it fits the MC returns. use_phi_refresh keeps φ*'s optimiser state for a :class:PhiRefresh in the same stack. Evaluations log the value range (mc_pretrain/v_min, mc_pretrain/v_max) and the fit (mc_pretrain/first_loss, mc_pretrain/last_loss, mc_pretrain/q_expert_mean: :class:MCPretrainResults).

docs.title: bind_to_agent
docs.text:
bind_to_agent(**agent_context)

Copy the agent's context (env_args, network_args, critic_optimizer_args, num_critics, gamma, reward_scale, use_train_frac, augment_obs_with_expert_action, expert_state_aug_dim) onto a new instance, and keep φ*'s optimiser when the stack (extensions) holds a :class:PhiRefresh.

docs.title: pretrain
docs.text:
pretrain(agent_state, ext_state, ctx)

Build the frozen expert critic φ* and persist it on agent_state: a fresh critic regressed on unbiased MC returns sets expert_critic_params / expert_v_min / expert_v_max, then (use_online_light) the online critic is nudged toward it. The fit's results are the extension's state.

Raises ValueError when the agent did not bind its context.

docs.title: BellmanPretrain dataclass
docs.text:
BellmanPretrain(
    n_steps=5000,
    buffer=None,
    gamma=None,
    reward_scale=None,
    recurrent=False,
    update_value_fn=None,
    update_target_fn=None,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    name="bellman_pretrain",
)

Bases: Extension

Bellman-bootstrapped critic pre-training.

n_steps critic updates on the replay buffer before training, which then holds the agent's expert prefill. Bootstraps from an untrained critic, so the pre-trained values are biased (:class:MCPretrain regresses unbiased returns instead); kept for ablation parity. Evaluations log the critic loss of its first and last update (bellman_pretrain/first_loss, bellman_pretrain/last_loss).

The fields after n_steps are the agent's context, filled by :meth:bind_to_agent (only SAC does).

bind_to_agent(**agent_context)

Copy the agent's buffer, gamma, reward_scale, recurrent and critic updates (update_value_fn, update_target_fn). It requires agent_expert: without one the buffer holds no expert prefill to pre-train on.

pretrain(agent_state, ext_state, ctx)

Pre-train the critic and keep its losses; raises ValueError when unbound.

docs.text:
PhiRefresh(
    expert_policy,
    interval=500,
    steps=20,
    buffer=None,
    gamma=None,
    reward_scale=None,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    reads_stored_expert=False,

)

Bases: Extension

Periodic self-consistent refresh of the frozen expert critic.

Every interval steps, run steps self-consistent Bellman updates on expert-flagged buffer transitions, keeping φ* aligned with the live data distribution. Requires :class:MCPretrain (which creates the refreshable φ*; refused without it).

buffer, gamma and reward_scale come from the agent through :meth:bind_to_agent (only SAC binds them); unbound, post_update raises ValueError.

docs.title: bind_to_agent
docs.text:
bind_to_agent(**agent_context)

Copy the agent's buffer, gamma, reward_scale and observation augmentation, and whether its expert is the agent's (:func:reads_stored_expert_actions).

docs.title: PriorData dataclass
docs.text:
PriorData(dataset, offline_updates=0, name='prior_data')

Bases: Extension

Prior data in the replay, and the agent's own updates on it before acting (offline-to-online RL).

Adds dataset's rows to the agent's replay, where they stay (:func:ajax.buffers.dataset.fill_replay), and to its observation and reward normalisers, each row counted once as collection counts its own; then runs offline_updates of the agent's update on that replay: its critic, actor and target steps and its extensions' loss terms, but no post_update between them. offline_updates=0 is RLPD's prior data in the replay (Ball et al. 2023) without its symmetric sampling. Ajax's warm-up acts uniformly: pair it with learning_starts=0.

Needs the replay and update an off-policy loop hands the pretrain phase (pretrain_context): any agent but SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC and DQN refuses it when built.

docs.text:
pretrain_critic_mc(
    agent_state,
    expert_critic_state,
    expert_policy,
    mode,

    gamma,

)

Pre-train critic using Monte Carlo returns from expert trajectories.

Unlike Bellman pretraining (bootstraps from an untrained critic → biased), MC returns G_t = Σ γ^k r_{t+k} are unbiased estimates of V^expert(s). The critic starts with accurate Q(s, a_expert) near the target from step 1.

Collection strategy: single call with n_mc_steps * n_mc_episodes // n_envs timesteps. The n_envs parallel environments reset to different initial states on each episode boundary, giving the same state-space coverage as separate per-seed rollouts — without any mapping over traced keys (which fails inside the outer vmap over seeds). Total transitions ≈ n_mc_steps * n_mc_episodes regardless of n_envs.

(agent_state, frozen_expert_params, obs_batched, action_batched,

Type Description Tuple[Any, FrozenDict, Array, Array, MCPretrainAux, LoadedTrainState]

MCPretrainAux, expert_critic_state_trained)

Periodic self-consistent φ refresh using expert-flagged buffer transitions. augment: φ reads observations augmented with SAC's expert actions; ext's expert gives the action at s' (expert_next_actions).

Target: r + γ * min_k Q_φ(s′, π(s′)) — φ* supervises its own bootstraps. Non-expert transitions are masked out, so the gradient comes only from (s, a_expert, r, s') rows where EDGE fired the expert action.

docs.title: ajax.extensions.target_mods
docs.text:
TD-target modifier research features as composable :class:Extensions.

These reshape the SAC Bellman target before it enters the critic loss (the on_target phase):

  • :class:IBRL — add the positive gap γ(1-d)·max(Q_expert - Q_policy, 0) so the value function matches an argmax action-selection policy.
  • :class:LCBGatedBootstrap — soft-blend the policy and expert TD targets by an LCB-scored sigmoid gate.
  • :class:CriticBlend — warmup-decaying blend of the Bellman target with the frozen expert critic's.
  • :class:MCVarianceCorrection — replace high-ensemble-variance Bellman targets with the MC-pretrained oracle.
  • :class:ValueBox — value-threshold expert action override during collection (the action phase).

The batch argument to on_target is the dict SAC's update_value_functions builds: observations, actions, next_observations, rewards (unscaled), reward_scale, dones, rng_key, q_preds, gamma, raw_next_observations (the environment's own next observations, which an extension's expert reads: SAC keeps them when an extension carries an expert) and recurrent.

docs.title: IBRL dataclass
docs.text:
IBRL(expert_policy, reads_stored_expert=False, name='ibrl')

Bases: Extension

IBRL bootstrap (Hu, Mirchandani and Sadigh, Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning, 2023).

Adds γ(1-d)·max(min Q_target(s', a_expert') - min Q_target(s', a_π'), 0) to the Bellman target so the value function is consistent with an argmax(Q_expert, Q_policy) action-selection rule.

Replace high-variance Bellman targets with the MC oracle.

Where the inter-critic variance exceeds threshold the Bellman target is swapped for the MC-pretrained expert critic's estimate. Requires :class:MCPretrain (refused without it).

docs.title: ValueBox dataclass
docs.text:
ValueBox(name='value_box')

Bases: Extension

Value-threshold expert-action override.

During collection, override the policy action with the expert's whenever the frozen-expert value V_expert(s) exceeds a curriculum threshold that ramps from v_min to v_max over training. Requires :class:MCPretrain (which supplies phi*, v_min and v_max; refused without it).

The :meth:action phase reads the SAC action pipeline's per-step dict (env_action, expert_action, the action of SAC's expert_policy, at which it also measures the expert's value, and observations, the critics' input, augmented when it is) and the box bounds off the agent state (so a resumed run keeps them), and writes in_value_box, entry_bonus and box_entry back into the dict for the pipeline to record on the transition. An entry ends the agent's episode: the expert's value, paid as the bonus, replaces the bootstrap, whatever its sign. The override (:func:box_action_override) comes after the warmup / post-warmup choice (action_slot).

Evaluations log the threshold (value_box/threshold), the share of envs inside the box and the share the expert drove on the last collection step (value_box/in_box_frac, value_box/expert_frac); the bounds are :class:MCPretrain's (mc_pretrain/v_min, mc_pretrain/v_max).

docs.title: ajax.extensions.adversarial
docs.text:
Adversarial imitation as a composable :class:Extension.

  • :class:AdversarialReward — GAIL's discriminator reward.

docs.title: Discriminator
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Logits of "an expert's" for an (observation, action) row.

docs.title: AdversarialReward dataclass
docs.text:
AdversarialReward(
    demonstrations,
    n_updates=2,
    learning_rate=0.001,
    architecture=("32", "relu", "32", "relu"),
    name="gail",
)

Bases: Extension

GAIL (Ho and Ermon, NeurIPS 2016): the policy learns from a reward a discriminator gives, trained to tell its rollouts from the expert's demonstrations. Following HumanCompatibleAI/imitation@e5ef188 (algorithms/adversarial/gail.py and common.py): each rollout's rewards become -log(1 - D(s, a)) from the current discriminator (- logsigmoid(-logits)), then the discriminator takes n_updates steps of binary cross-entropy, the demonstrations labelled 1, on the rollout's rows and as many demonstration rows drawn uniformly. The environment's own reward is not used. The discriminator reads the action the env executes, clipped to [-1, 1] in agent units (:func:~ajax.environments.utils.agent_action_to_env), as the reference records it (its BufferingWrapper sees the action SB3 steps the env with, clipped to the box). Its 32-32 ReLU network starts as torch's nn.Linear and steps by torch's Adam (learning rate 1e-3), the reference's BasicRewardNet and optimiser. Deviations: the discriminator reads (s, a) unnormalised, without the reference examples' running normalisation; its generator batch is the whole rollout, the reference's demo_batch_size rows of its last one; PPO stands in for the paper's TRPO, as in the reference. Logs gail/reward, gail/disc_loss and the shares of expert and rollout rows it classifies right, gail/expert_acc and gail/policy_acc.

rows()

docs.title: ajax.extensions.offline
docs.text:
Offline-RL critic regularisers as composable :class:Extensions.

  • :class:ConservativeQ — CQL(H)'s conservative critic term.
  • :class:CalQL — the same term, its policy-action values floored at the data's Monte-Carlo returns (Cal-QL).
  • :class:TargetBC — ReBRAC's penalty on the target's next actions.

docs.title: ConservativeQ dataclass
docs.text:
ConservativeQ(
    alpha=5.0, n_actions=10, name="conservative_q"
)

Bases: Extension

CQL(H)'s critic term (Kumar, Zhou, Tucker and Levine, NeurIPS 2020, eq. 4), in the importance-sampled form of the authors' code (aviralkumar2907/CQL@d67dbe9, d4rl/rlkit/torch/sac/cql.py:234-264, min_q_version 3)::

alpha * mean( logsumexp_j [Q(s, a_j) - log density(a_j)] - Q(s, a) )

over the critics and the batch, with a the row's action and the a_j n_actions uniform actions in [-1, 1]^A and n_actions of the policy at s and at s', all scored at s. It pushes the critic down on actions away from the data's and up on the data's. The reference sums each critic's Bellman loss and term; Ajax's critics share one mean squared error, so the term is the mean over them, at the same ratio. It needs a policy with a density: a deterministic one (TD3's) is a point mass, whose samples are copies of one action and whose density is undefined. Deviations from the reference's SAC: its target keeps SAC's entropy term (the reference's deterministic_backup drops it). Logs cql/term and cql/gap, the logsumexp minus the data's value.

docs.title: floor
docs.text:
floor(q, batch)

The policy actions' values as the term reads them (CalQL floors them); no metrics.

docs.title: CalQL dataclass
docs.text:
CalQL(alpha=5.0, n_actions=10, name='cal_ql')

Bases: ConservativeQ

Cal-QL (Nakamoto, Zhai, Singh, Mark, Ma, Finn, Kumar and Levine, NeurIPS 2023): :class:ConservativeQ's term with the policy actions' values floored at the row's Monte-Carlo return to go before the logsumexp (nakamotoo/Cal-QL@ac6eafe, JaxCQL/conservative_sac.py:227-240), so the critic is pushed down no further than the data's own return. The return to go is the transition dataset's (return_to_go), at its gamma, in the env's reward units: the agent's gamma and a reward_scale of 1 match it. Deviation: the reference computes a collected episode's returns when it ends; collected rows here keep -inf, no floor. Also logs calql/bound_frac, the share of policy actions at s whose value the floor raised.

docs.title: TargetBC dataclass
docs.text:
TargetBC(beta=1.0, name='target_bc')

Bases: Extension

ReBRAC's critic penalty (Tarasov, Kurenkov, Nikulin and Kolesnikov, NeurIPS 2023; tinkoff-ai/ReBRAC@694385b, src/algorithms/rebrac.py: 134-144): the bootstrap less beta times the squared distance from the next actions the target scored (TD3's smoothed next_actions) to the dataset's next action a' (next_action)::

y -= gamma (1 - d) beta sum_i (next_actions_i - a'_i)^2

A row whose a' is unknown (an episode's last row, a collected one: NaN) keeps its target. Logs target_bc/penalty, the mean penalty, and target_bc/known_frac, the share of rows with an a'.

docs.title: ajax.extensions.exploration
docs.text:
Exploration research features as composable :class:Extensions.

EDGE (Expert Decayed Guided Exploration) substitutes the expert action for the policy action during collection, gated by a value comparison that decays over training. :class:EDGEExploration selects one of six gates with gate: "fixed" / "argmax" / "boltzmann" (value-gap gates) or "lcb" / "argmax_lcb" / "thompson" (quality-aware gates); the gate maths are the functions below.

The SAC action pipeline pre-computes the per-step quantities every gate needs (policy_action, expert_action, observations, ...) and passes them through the obs argument as a dict, as the batch dict of the on_target / actor_loss phases. The extension picks an action (or returns None to defer); the pipeline owns the bookkeeping (is_expert_flag, buffer_action, expert-state threading). Gate randomness is threaded through obs["gate_rng"] (read and overwritten in place), the pipeline's own stream, not the framework's per-extension rng split (stack._keys).

docs.title: EDGEExploration dataclass
docs.text:
EDGEExploration(
    gate="fixed",
    decay_frac=0.3,
    tau=1.0,
    fixed_prob=0.5,
    lcb_beta_init=1.0,
    lcb_beta_decay_k=2.0,
    lcb_temperature=1.0,
    lcb_asymmetric=False,
    epsilon_floor=0.0,
    name="edge_exploration",
)

Bases: Extension

Expert Decayed Guided Exploration during collection.

gate selects the substitution rule (see module docstring). The other fields:

  • decay_frac — value-gap gates decay to 0 over this fraction.
  • tau — Boltzmann temperature on the value gap.
  • fixed_prob — substitution probability for the fixed gate.
  • lcb_beta_init / lcb_beta_decay_k — LCB pessimism schedule.
  • lcb_temperature — softmax temperature of the LCB / Thompson gate.
  • lcb_asymmetric — LCB on the expert arm, UCB on the policy arm.
  • epsilon_floor — minimum policy-pick probability (Thompson).

The expert is SAC's expert_policy: the gate compares the action it gave the pipeline with the policy's. Evaluations log the share of envs the expert drove on the last collection step (edge/live_expert_frac) and the gate's schedule: edge/beta for the LCB gates, edge/decay for the fixed, argmax and Boltzmann gates (the Thompson gate has none).

docs.text:

Apply the configured EDGE gate to substitute the policy action.

obs is the SAC action pipeline's per-step dict (the module docstring): policy_action, expert_action, observations (the critics' input, augmented with the expert-action dims under augment_obs_with_expert_action), critic_params and critic_state (the frozen expert critic if MC pretraining ran, else the live critic), post_warmup_action and gate_rng.

Side effects: writes _edge_use_expert back into obs for the pipeline's is_expert_flag bookkeeping, and updates obs["gate_rng"] for any downstream gate.

lcb_beta(step, total_steps, init, decay_k)

The LCB pessimism init (1 - t / T)^decay_k, annealed over the run (t / T clipped to [0, 1], T at least 1).

docs.title: lcb_score
docs.text:
lcb_score(q, beta)

min Q - beta (max Q - min Q) over the ensemble axis: the critics' disagreement as epistemic uncertainty, penalised.

docs.title: edge_compute_value_gap
docs.text:
edge_compute_value_gap(
    obs,
    policy_action,
    expert_action,
    critic_state,

)

Compute Q(s,pi*) - Q(s,pi). Positive means expert is still better.

Returns (gap, q_policy) — q_policy is reused by the Boltzmann gate.

docs.title: edge_compute_decay
docs.text:
edge_compute_decay(timestep, total_timesteps, decay_frac)

Linear decay: 1 -> 0 over decay_frac of training.

decay_frac=0.0 means never decay (gate stays active for full training).

docs.title: edge_argmax_gate
docs.text:
edge_argmax_gate(gap, decay, rng)

Deterministic: use expert whenever gap > 0 and decay > 0.

Returns (use_expert_mask, unchanged_rng).

docs.title: edge_boltzmann_gate
docs.text:
edge_boltzmann_gate(gap, decay, rng, q_policy, tau)

Adaptive: p = decay * sigmoid(gap / (tau * |Q|)).

Returns (use_expert_mask, updated_rng).

docs.title: edge_fixed_gate
docs.text:
edge_fixed_gate(gap, decay, rng, fixed_prob)

Fixed probability: p = decay * fixed_prob.

Returns (use_expert_mask, updated_rng).

docs.title: edge_lcb_scores
docs.text:
edge_lcb_scores(
    obs,
    policy_action,
    expert_action,
    critic_state,
    critic_params,
    beta,
    asymmetric=False,
)

Each candidate's score (score_expert, score_policy): its :func:lcb_score, the critics' disagreement penalising uncertain (OOD) candidates; the gate then compares the two.

asymmetric scores the policy arm optimistically instead (UCB, max Q + beta (max Q - min Q)), so the gate hands control to the policy where its critic is uncertain, which is where fresh on-policy Bellman anchors help most; the expert arm keeps its LCB, staying conservative about following an unreliable expert. Symmetric LCB over-penalises the policy exactly where it explores beyond the expert's tube.

docs.title: edge_lcb_argmax_gate
docs.text:
edge_lcb_argmax_gate(score_expert, score_policy, rng)

Deterministic argmax gate over LCB scores.

use_expert = score_e > score_p.

Compared to edge_lcb_gate (softmax), this collapses the gate to a hard threshold while preserving the LCB scoring (mu - beta*sigma) so the (gating form, scoring rule) ablation can vary one axis at a time. Used by the argmax_lcb corner of the 2x2.

docs.title: edge_lcb_gate
docs.text:
edge_lcb_gate(score_expert, score_policy, rng, temperature)

Stochastic Boltzmann gate over LCB scores.

p(use_expert) = sigmoid((score_e - score_p) / temperature).

Hard threshold (argmax) creates a self-fulfilling expert preference: expert always wins → buffer all expert → critic never learns Q for policy actions → expert keeps winning. The stochastic version ensures policy occasionally gets sampled, breaking the inertia.

Temperature → 0 recovers argmax; → ∞ recovers uniform mixing.

docs.title: edge_compute_thompson_stats
docs.text:
edge_compute_thompson_stats(
    obs,
    policy_action,
    expert_action,
    critic_state,
    critic_params,
)

Per-action Q mean / std across critic ensemble: (mu_e, sigma_e, mu_p, sigma_p).

docs.title: edge_thompson_gate
docs.text:
edge_thompson_gate(
    mu_e,
    sigma_e,
    mu_p,
    sigma_p,
    rng,
    temperature=1.0,
    epsilon_floor=0.0,
)

Thompson-sampling gate, with optional epsilon floor on policy picks.

Treat each candidate's Q as Gaussian(mu, (temperature * sigma)^2), draw one sample per side, pick whichever is larger. Equivalent to p(use_expert) = Phi((mu_e - mu_p) / (T * sqrt(sigma_e^2 + sigma_p^2))) in expectation, but stochastic per-step (which is what we want for exploration: the gate itself injects noise rather than deferring to a fixed rule).

Symmetric: high uncertainty on either side widens the gate, never biasing it. Confident estimates dominate. With both sigmas → 0 we recover deterministic argmax.

epsilon_floor: with this probability, force the policy regardless of the Thompson outcome. Required when the expert dominates by many sigmas (Phi -> 1 -> Thompson never picks the policy -> the critic never sees policy actions in its updates -> Q for policy actions stays stale -> the gate can never flip even if the policy improves). Set carefully on brittle envs: too high crashes the agent, too low starves the policy of evaluation data. ~0.001-0.05 is a sane range.

docs.title: ajax.extensions.ensemble
docs.text:
Critic-ensemble research features as composable :class:Extensions.

  • :class:KernelRepulsion — SVGD-style function-space repulsion between the critics of an ensemble (the critic_loss phase).

docs.title: KernelRepulsion dataclass
docs.text:
KernelRepulsion(coef=0.1, name='kernel_repulsion')

Bases: Extension

coef times :func:q_kernel_repulsion of the critics on the critic-loss batch, added to the critic loss (REDQ's SVGD variant).

It reads the batch every replay agent's critic step passes (observations, actions, critic_params, critic_state), so it costs one more ensemble forward. Feedforward critics only: agents with memory reject extensions, so repulsion with recurrent memory is unsupported.

docs.title: q_kernel_repulsion
docs.text:
q_kernel_repulsion(q_preds)

The mean RBF kernel between the critics' Q-functions on a batch.

q_preds is (num_critics, batch, ...); each critic's outputs form one feature vector. The bandwidth follows the median heuristic (Liu & Wang 2016, SVGD), held constant so the kernel adapts to the current spread without a confounding gradient; minimising the mean kernel pushes the critics apart in function space.

docs.title: ajax.extensions.instrumentation
docs.text:
EVarEst measurement / instrumentation as composable :class:Extensions.

The measurement code of EVAREST's evarest/rl/, foldable into any Ajax agent (SAC, DQN, REDQ, TD3 off-policy; PPO, PQN, APO, AVG on-policy): extensions=[ConditioningMetrics(), BiasVoreDecomposition(...), ...].

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
• :class:ConditioningMetrics — eval_metrics phase, plasticity diagnostics (srank, dormant fraction, feat / weight L2 norms). Reads the agent's replay buffer (off-policy) OR agent_state.last_rollout (on-policy with expose_recent_rollout), auto-detected.
  • :class:BiasVoreDecomposition — eval_metrics phase, EVarEst bias^2 / Var(residual) / MSE / |bias| decomposition of the critic objective. Mirrors the math in EVAREST's loss.py / mechanism.py.
  • :class:BiasVorePenalty — critic_loss phase, the EVarEst critic objective itself. penalty(alpha) = ((1-2alpha)/alpha) * Var(q_preds - target_q) added on top of the agent's vanilla MSE.

Without a measurement batch (no replay buffer, no last_rollout yet) the eval-metric extensions emit no metrics rather than wrong numbers. The maths are intentionally kept identical to the EVAREST sources.

docs.title: ConditioningMetrics dataclass
docs.text:
ConditioningMetrics(
    buffer=None,
    on_policy_batch=256,
    critic_loc="auto",
    concat_action="auto",
    name="conditioning_metrics",
)

Bases: Extension

Plasticity diagnostics on a state batch sampled from the agent's visited-state distribution.

Reads the critic's encoder features: * critic_loc='critic' + concat_action=True ⇒ Q(obs,act) ensemble critic on critic_state. * critic_loc='critic' + concat_action=False ⇒ V(obs) ensemble critic on critic_state. * critic_loc='actor' ⇒ Q-network on actor_state (DQN, PQN), penultimate features read via the encoder_features sow.

'auto' (the default for both) reads them from the networks, never from the agent's name or the batch source: the critic branch when critic_state's network is an ensemble critic (it exposes apply_encoder_ensemble), the actor branch otherwise; on the critic branch, the action is concatenated when the critic's parameters were built on the observation and action (:func:_takes_action).

Pass buffer=agent.buffer for off-policy agents whose buffer object isn't on the agent state itself; on-policy agents must set BaseAgentConfig.expose_recent_rollout=True.

docs.title: BiasVoreDecomposition dataclass
docs.text:
BiasVoreDecomposition(
    buffer=None,
    on_policy_batch=256,
    gamma=0.99,
    reward_scale=1.0,
    value_target_fn=None,
    name="bias_vore_decomposition",
)

Bases: Extension

EVarEst bias^2 / Var(residual) / MSE / |bias| decomposition.

Ports the math from EVAREST loss.py / mechanism.make_evarest_decomposition_metrics. The residual is reconstructed from the agent's current critic on a measurement batch sampled the same way :class:ConditioningMetrics samples (replay buffer for off-policy, last_rollout for on-policy).

By default it is the critic's one-step TD residual under the current policy, prediction - (reward_scale * r + gamma (1 - d) next), with the critic read from the networks (:func:_critic_kind):

  • Q(s, a) ensemble: next = min_i Q_i(s', a') - alpha log pi(a'|s'), a' ~ pi(s'), alpha the agent's temperature if it has one, else 0;
  • V(s) ensemble: next = min_i V_i(s');
  • Q-network: next = max_a' Q(s', a').

The bootstrap uses the critic's current parameters: whether and how an agent keeps a target network (SAC does, AVG and PQN do not) is its own business, as are GAE, Q(lambda) and average-reward targets. Pass value_target_fn to measure against an agent's exact target.

docs.title: BiasVorePenalty dataclass
docs.text:
BiasVorePenalty(
    alpha=0.5,
    coeff_override=None,
    loss_scale=1.0,
    name="bias_vore_penalty",
)

Bases: Extension

EVarEst critic objective as a critic_loss extension.

Ports the additive form of EVAREST's :func:make_evarest_loss / :func:make_evarest_ppo_loss / :func:make_evarest_td_loss. The agent's vanilla critic loss already contains MSE = bias^2 + Var(residual); this extension adds the eq. (6) extra penalty term:

penalty(alpha) = ((1 - 2 alpha) / alpha) * Var(q_preds - target_q)

so the total objective becomes MSE + ((1-2 alpha)/alpha) * Var(residual). alpha=0.5 ⇒ coeff 0 ⇒ identical to vanilla; alpha->0 is the AVEC limit (use a small alpha rather than zero). coeff_override lets callers fix the coefficient directly (e.g. to disable the extra penalty entirely without recomputing alpha). It rebuilds the residual the agent's MSE term sees from the critic_loss batch: observations, targets and the critic (critic_params and critic_state, with actions for a Q-critic; DQN's and PQN's q_state and actions), and raises on a batch without them rather than add 0.

docs.title: srank
docs.text:
srank(feats, delta=0.01)

Kumar et al. (2021) effective rank.

Smallest k whose top-k singular values capture >= 1-delta of the total spectral mass. feats is the (batch, d) feature matrix.

docs.text:

A unit is dormant when its mean-|activation| score, normalised by the layer mean, is <= tau. feats is the (batch, d) post- activation feature matrix.

docs.title: setup_environment
docs.text:
setup_environment(
    env,
    env_params,
    num_episodes,
    norm_info,
    gamma,
    action_repeat=1,
    episode_length=None,
)

The training env's stack, rebuilt for evaluation (gymnax or brax).

Ajax's own layers come off (:func:~ajax.environments.create.strip_ajax_wrappers) and go back on as training composed them (:func:~ajax.environments.create.add_ajax_wrappers): the clip to a continuous action space's bounds, the observation normaliser frozen at norm_info (None: no normaliser) and applied to the observations only where training applied it, rewards never normalised. The task under them -- the user's wrappers, the flattening -- is kept as trained on (gymnax).

brax / playground tasks are rebuilt from their id with num_episodes parallel envs. episode_length (simulator steps) and action_repeat are the training env's; the defaults are None -> the env's native episode length, falling back to 1000, and repeat 1. gymnax envs do not support action_repeat > 1.

    actor_state, recurrent, continuous

Return a function mapping (obs, done, hidden) → (action, entropy, hidden).

In recurrent mode the hidden state is an explicit input/output so the eval loop can thread it through its carry (the live carry on actor_state belongs to the training envs and has the wrong batch size here). Non-recurrent mode passes hidden through untouched.

docs.title: step_environment
docs.text:
step_environment(
    mode,
    env,
    env_params,
    recurrent,
    actor_state,
    continuous,
    expert_policy=None,
    train_frac=None,
    eval_action_transform=None,
    agent_state=None,
    pid_gain_policy=False,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    augment_obs_with_expert_state=False,
    value_estimate=None,
    command=None,
    norm_info=None,
)

Return a pure function stepping the evaluation (an :class:_EvalCarry).

The expert acts in agent units (:class:ExpertInAgentUnits), as every action here; the executed one is mapped onto the env's bounds (:func:agent_action_to_env), as in collection.

pid_gain_policy: when True, the actor output is interpreted as PID gain modulation: env_action = expert.step_with_gains(state, obs, anchorexp(ln10a)).

augment_obs_with_expert_action: when True, the actor receives [env_obs, expert_action] as input. The expert is queried statefully (matching training) so the policy sees the same augmented obs at eval that it saw during training.

value_estimate: the critic's estimate at the actor's input and the action collection stores, each step: the executed action in agent units, the actor's (the gains') under pid_gain_policy.

command: a command-conditioned actor's (see :func:evaluate): the actor reads command.actor_input(obs, c), and each step's reward, in the agent's units (norm_info, :func:normalised_reward), and end update c.

docs.title: step_environment_expert
docs.text:
step_environment_expert(
    mode, env, env_params, expert_policy
)

Step function for the expert's own rollout, called as the agent's rollout calls it (:func:step_environment): a stateful expert (one with init_state) as expert_policy(state, obs) -> (action, state), a stateless one as expert_policy(obs) -> action, in agent units and mapped onto the env's bounds. A discrete expert's action index comes as an (n, 1) column, as a replay keeps it; the env takes (n,).

docs.title: evaluate
docs.text:
evaluate(
    env,
    actor_state,
    num_episodes,
    rng,
    env_params,
    recurrent=False,
    gamma=0.99,
    norm_info=None,
    avg_reward_mode=False,
    expert_policy=None,
    train_frac=None,
    eval_action_transform=None,
    max_eval_steps=None,
    agent_state=None,
    pid_gain_policy=False,
    augment_obs_with_expert_action=False,
    augment_obs_with_expert_state=False,
    eval_expert_policy=None,
    value_estimate=None,
    command=None,
)

Evaluate the actor's deterministic policy on num_episodes episodes; with expert_policy (the training expert, which builds the actor's input) the expert's return too, that of eval_expert_policy when given, on the same episodes (the same reset and key). The experts speak env units: they are read in agent units here (:class:ExpertInAgentUnits; an agent's are already).

command evaluates a command-conditioned actor (UDRL's desired return and horizon): command.initial(agent_state, num_episodes) is each episode's first command, the actor reads command.actor_input(obs, c), and command.update(c, reward, done) follows each step, the reward in the agent's units, normalised as in training: the units of its targets.

Returns the mean return, entropy, average reward (avg_reward_mode), value bias (value_estimate), episode length and expert's return, each NaN without what it needs. The value bias is the mean over the evaluated steps of the critic's estimate (:class:ValueEstimate) minus the discounted return realised from the step, in the critic's units: the rewards normalised as in training (:func:normalised_reward) and scaled. A recurrent critic's memory is not run here: NaN then.

docs.title: evaluate_policy
docs.text:
evaluate_policy(
    env_args, policy_fn, init_carry_fn, num_episodes, key
)

Mean return and mean length of one episode in each of num_episodes envs.

The evaluation protocol of the agents that own their collection (the world-model agents, DESIGN §5.4), for a stateful policy with the row collector's protocol policy_fn(carry, obs, is_first, key) -> (action, carry, extras) (extras ignored):

  • the env is rebuilt through :func:setup_environment with num_episodes parallel envs and the training action_repeat and episode length; actions go through :func:ajax.environments.utils.agent_action_to_env, as in the row collector, so train and eval act on the env identically (the env's clip to its bounds is then a no-op);
  • the envs are reset with key (the same reset-key derivation as :func:evaluate, so both see the same initial states for one key);
  • the policy starts from init_carry_fn(num_episodes) (a zero carry) with is_first set on the first step only;
  • every env runs exactly one episode: a scan over the episode length in agent steps (:func:ajax.environments.utils.agent_episode_length) with rewards and lengths masked after each env's first done.

Preconditions (they raise): the training env does not normalise observations or rewards (the rebuild is the raw env, see :func:ajax.environments.row_collector.check_unnormalized_env), and env_params describes one system (per-env, batched params cannot be rebuilt with num_episodes envs; evaluate a nominal system instead).

docs.title: ajax.checkpoint
docs.text:
Checkpoint save/restore for Ajax agents.

Serializes the pytree data of a BaseAgentState (arrays, counters, and other leaves) while discarding non-data fields such as optax GradientTransformation closures and flax apply_fn callables. Those closures are rebuilt at load time by re-initializing a skeleton state from the same agent config; the loaded data is then grafted onto the skeleton via flax.serialization.from_state_dict.

Typical resume flow (resume in tests/probing/runs.py runs it): skeleton = agent.train(seed=seeds, n_timesteps=0) # init only if checkpoint_exists(path): skeleton = restore_into(skeleton, path) final = agent.train(..., initial_state=skeleton, ...) save_checkpoint(final, path)

docs.title: restore_into
docs.text:
restore_into(skeleton, path)

Load path and graft its data onto skeleton.

skeleton is a freshly-initialized agent state with the same structure as the saved one. The optimizer transformations and apply functions come from skeleton; only the pytree data (params, optimizer mu/nu/count, buffer arrays, rngs, counters) is replaced.

docs.title: Networks and modules
docs.text: The actor and critic networks, Squash, the tanh wrapper over any policy distribution, the pluggable memory block, the PID policy and the blocks the world models share. See Networks and Memory.

docs.title: CNNSpec
docs.text:
Bases: NamedTuple

CNN encoder architecture: conv stack + projection width.

CNNSpec() is :class:CNNEncoder's default architecture. Each kernel_sizes / strides entry may be an int (square) or an (h, w) tuple. A NamedTuple -> hashable, so it is safe as a flax module field and as a :class:NetworkConfig field. padding is flax's nn.Conv padding; layer_norm puts a LayerNorm after every convolution and the projection, before its ReLU; kernel_init names every layer's initializer as :func:~ajax.networks.utils.dense reads it, "torch_linear" drawing kernel and bias uniform in +-1/sqrt(fan_in) (torch's and Torch7's default); None is flax's lecun_normal with zero biases.

docs.title: CNNEncoder
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Conv encoder for image observations packed flat as (H*W*C + extra_dim,).

The flat layout (rather than native NHWC) keeps Ajax's existing collector and command-augmentation paths working unchanged: extra trailing scalar dims (e.g. UDRL's (d_r, d_h) command) are concatenated to the embedding AFTER the convolutions, so the conv stack only sees the image.

The image is assumed to be stored in NHWC order: a Flatten wrapper in user code must transpose a stack-first array (T, H, W) into (H, W, T) before flattening so reshape(H, W, C) recovers the right layout.

docs.title: Actor
docs.text:

The stochastic policy of SAC, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, PPO, APO and UDRL: a Normal head for continuous actions (:class:Squashed bounds it), a Categorical one for discrete. Expert guidance acts at the loss level, not in the architecture, which keeps the policy unconstrained.

docs.title: ajax.networks.distributions
docs.text:
Policy distributions shared by the agents.

:class:Squash bounds any continuous policy to (-1, 1) with tanh (:func:squash also takes a :class:Deterministic one). The functions below it read any policy, squashed or not, so callers need not check which they hold.

docs.title: Deterministic
docs.text:
Tiny distrax-compatible wrapper for deterministic policies (TD3's).

Exposes .mean() so existing code (the policy loss, the target action computation, the ImitationLoss extension) keeps working without branches. A pytree of its action, as distrax distributions are of their parameters (a replayed bootstrap gathers its steps, recurrent.actor_dist).

docs.title: log_prob
docs.text:
log_prob(x)

For BC pretraining: a delta distribution's log-density is +∞ at x=action, -∞ elsewhere. We use the negative-MSE proxy so that maximizing log_prob is equivalent to MSE-minimizing the actor toward the target action. Shape: (..., action_dim) -> (..., action_dim) (per-dim, summed by caller).

docs.title: Squash
docs.text:
Squash(distribution)

Bases: Transformed

tanh of a policy distribution, its latent: any distrax distribution (a Block spans its event dimensions, if it has any).

Exact: sampling and log-probabilities. log_prob(action) inverts tanh, finite only while |action| < 1, which float32 loses once the latent sample passes about 9; :meth:log_prob_from_raw reads the latent sample itself and stays finite.

Not exact, as neither has a closed form: :meth:mean is tanh of the latent's mean, the deterministic action, not the mean of the squashed action; :meth:entropy is sampled.

docs.text:
log_prob_from_raw(raw)

The log-probability of tanh(raw), from the latent sample raw (no arctanh, so finite at saturation).

The squashed action's entropy, estimated as brax does: the latent's entropy plus the tanh log-det-Jacobian at one latent sample drawn with seed. Unbiased, and its gradient reaches the mean; the latent's entropy alone grows without bound in its scale.

docs.title: TorchLinear
docs.text:
Bases: Module

A dense layer that starts as torch's nn.Linear does: its kernel and its bias each uniform in ±1 / sqrt(fan_in).

torch 1.5.1 (torch/nn/modules/linear.py:79-84, at its v1.5.1 tag) draws the weight with kaiming_uniform_(a=sqrt(5)), whose bound sqrt(3) * sqrt(2 / (1 + a**2)) / sqrt(fan_in) is 1 / sqrt(fan_in) (torch/nn/init.py:61-69, :322-327), and the bias with the same bound. A layer, not an initializer: a flax bias initializer never sees the fan-in. Its parameters are a Dense layer's, at the same path.

Each member is its own network in the references, clipped alone (ASAC: BobMak/asac @4b68862, darer/Models.py:299-301).

docs.text:
parse_activation(activation)

Parse an activation name, or pass an activation callable through.

"silu" is x * sigmoid(x) (DreamerV3's activation, Table 4 of arXiv:2301.04104v2). "mish" is x * tanh(softplus(x)) (TD-MPC2's activation, Sec. 3.1 of arXiv:2310.16828v2; torch nn.Mish).

docs.title: parse_function_string
docs.text:
parse_function_string(s, context=None)

Split "name" / "name(expr)" into (name, value of expr).

A string that does not start with an identifier (a letter or _), such as "0.5" or "-1.0", is evaluated as a whole and returned as (None, value). One that does but is neither form, such as "orthogonal(2.0" or "np.sqrt(2)", raises ValueError rather than being read as a bare name.

docs.title: trunc_normal_fan_in
docs.text:
trunc_normal_fan_in(scale=1.0)

Fan-in truncated normal: DreamerV3's weight initializer.

DreamerV3 (arXiv:2301.04104v2; danijar/dreamerv3@2411f7d, dreamerv3/nets.py:842-848, :870, fans :873-884; dreamerv3_spec 1.5) initialises every Linear, BlockLinear and Conv kernel as::

W = scale * 1.1368 * sqrt(1 / fan_in) * TruncatedNormal(-2, 2)

with a unit-sigma normal truncated at +-2 and scale the layer's outscale. This is variance_scaling(scale**2, "fan_in", "truncated_normal"): flax divides by the exact standard deviation of the truncated unit normal, 0.87962566, where DreamerV3 multiplies by the rounded 1.1368. Drawn with the same key the two kernels differ by the constant factor 1.13684723 / 1.1368, a residual relative difference of 4.16e-5 (tested; deviation D23 in docs/world_models/deviations.md). Both give Std[W] = scale / sqrt(fan_in), and flax's fan-in matches the reference for every kernel rank >= 2: shape[-2] * prod(shape[:-2]), so a BlockLinear kernel (g, I/g, U/g) gets the full input width I.

scale = 0 gives an all-zero kernel (DreamerV3's reward and value heads).

docs.title: ajax.networks.memory
docs.text:
Pluggable memory (recurrent) modules for actor/critic networks.

Every memory architecture unifies behind one interface, operating on time-major sequences (T, B, features) with per-step reset flags (T, B):

  • init_carry(config, rng, batch_size) -> carry returns the recurrent state as a pytree (always a tuple with one entry per layer).
  • __call__(carry, x, resets) -> (new_carry, y) runs the cell over the whole sequence, isolating episodes wherever resets[t] is set, and returns the final carry plus the per-step outputs (T, B, hidden).

Step-wise inference (collection, evaluation) is the same code path with T=1, so training and acting can never diverge. The step-vs-sequence equivalence tests in tests/networks/test_memory.py are the acceptance harness for every kind.

Carries are zero at initialization for every supported kind; callers rely on this to build fresh carries with zeros_carry_like (e.g. at eval time or for replayed sequences).

Kinds and their compute/memory profile:

  • "gru" / "lstm": nn.scan over the classic cells — sequential in T, carry is O(hidden) per env.
  • "transformer": sliding-window causal self-attention. Training runs FULL PARALLEL attention over the chunk (no scan) with an episode-segment mask; acting keeps a rolling cache of the last window - 1 embeddings per layer, so per-step memory is O(window * hidden) and constant in episode length.
  • "mamba": selective state-space (S6-style) block. Training runs a parallel associative_scan over T; the carry is the SSM state plus a small causal-conv tail — RNN-sized memory with transformer-like training parallelism.

The transformer and mamba outputs end with a LayerNorm, as their references' pre-norm stacks do; the GRU and LSTM outputs are the cells' own.

docs.text:
flatten_carry(carry)

Pack a carry pytree into one (batch, D) float array.

Used to write per-step actor carries into the replay buffer (R2D2-style stored-state replay): flashbax schemas hold flat arrays, not pytrees. Every leaf keeps its leading batch axis; the trailing dims are flattened and concatenated in jax.tree leaf order. Reversible via :func:unflatten_carry given any same-structure template. Bool leaves (e.g. the transformer cache's validity flags) are cast to float and recovered by dtype from the template.

docs.title: gate_block_orthogonal
docs.text:
gate_block_orthogonal(n_gates)

One gate's kernel as torch's nn.init.orthogonal_ leaves it on a GRU's or LSTM's stacked (n_gates * H, fan_in) weight: a (fan_in, H) block of a random orthogonal (fan_in, n_gates * H) matrix, of std 1/sqrt(max(n_gates * H, fan_in)). Ni et al. start every GRU and LSTM weight so, with zero biases (pomdp-baselines @e7c19c3 policies/models/recurrent_actor.py:70-74, recurrent_critic.py:64-68; Memory-RL @c9b8b39 policies/seq_models/rnn_vanilla.py:23-31), where flax's per-gate kernels have std 1/sqrt(fan_in) (lecun_normal) and 1/sqrt(H) (orthogonal). Each gate draws its own matrix, so the gates are independent, where torch's are jointly orthogonal.

docs.title: ajax.modules.pid_actor
docs.text:
PID policies: an actor that is a PID controller with learned gains.

The actor acts on the error terms (e, I, D) that :class:ajax.environments.pid_terms.PIDTermsWrapper puts first in the observation; its pre-squash action, per action dimension a, is::

u_a = sum_j Kp[a, j] e_j + Ki[a, j] I_j + Kd[a, j] D_j

Passing a :class:PIDPolicy as actor_architecture selects it in any continuous-action agent (SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, PPO, APO). Two kinds of gains:

  • gains="fixed": the gains are the actor's parameters, a linear map with no bias and no hidden layer, so the trained policy deploys as a plain (saturated) PID with the gains :func:pid_gains reads off it, in normalised units (below) (Lawrence et al. 2022, "Deep reinforcement learning with shallow controllers: an experimental application to PID tuning", cited from memory, unverified).
  • gains="observation": an MLP predicts the gains from the observation (gain scheduling); with a constant network it is the fixed policy.

Each agent's own output rules apply to u as to any actor's mean: SAC, REDQ, ASAC and AVG squash it with tanh, TD3 too (deterministic); APO takes tanh(u) as its mean (its tanh_mean) and samples around it unsquashed, PPO around u (unless squash=True). Like every action, u is in agent units, [-1, 1], mapped onto the env's box [low, high] (:func:ajax.environments.utils.agent_action_to_env): the deployed controller is c + h * sat(u), with centre c = (high + low) / 2, half-range h = (high - low) / 2 and sat the agent's tanh or clip to [-1, 1]. The gains are therefore normalised: they map the error terms to agent units, and a PID in the env's units has gains h * K (small-signal, tanh near 0) and offset c; zero gains command the box's centre (no control on a symmetric box). The stochastic agents explore with a learned, state-independent log-std, clipped to the agent's log_std_bounds (PPO's and APO's default: no clip). Gains start at zero. Observation normalisation (env- or agent-side) leaves the terms raw, as the wrapper declares them, so the gains act on the errors in the env's units; the gain network of gains="observation" reads the rest normalised.

{"kp", "ki", "kd"} of a fixed-gain PID actor, each (..., action_dim, n_errors) (leading axes, e.g. seeds, kept).

They are normalised gains, from the errors to agent units [-1, 1]: on an env box [low, high] the env-unit gains are (high - low) / 2 times these (the module docstring), equal on a [-1, 1] box.

docs.title: ajax.modules.pid_head
docs.text:
PID output head: a stateful, learnable PID layer on a network's output.

Busetto et al. 2024 (arXiv:2411.06482, §4.1) close their in-context controller with a PID layer: the transformer emits a signal z_k and the applied input is

u_k = K_P z_k + K_I sum_{j<=k} z_j + K_D (z_k - z_{k-1})

with three learnable gains. The integral term promotes zero steady-state error on step references, and the authors report faster training. This is NOT :mod:ajax.modules.pid_actor (a PID policy acting on the observation's tracking-error terms): here the PID acts on the network's own output, so it needs a carry (integral and previous signal) like a memory cell.

Interface mirrors :class:ajax.networks.memory.MemoryCell: time-major (T, B, n) inputs with (T, B) reset flags, initialize_carry, and __call__(carry, z, resets) -> (new_carry, u); step-wise use is the T=1 case of the same code path.

docs.title: PIDOutputHead
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Learnable PID on a time-major signal z; see the module docstring.

Attributes:

Name Type Description n_outputs int

signal width n (one gain triple per channel; the paper's single-input case is n_outputs=1).

use_p bool

enable the proportional term; a disabled term has no parameter. With only use_p and kp_init=1 the head is the identity at initialisation. use_i and use_d likewise enable the integral and derivative terms.

anti_windup float | None

pre-squash output magnitude beyond which the integral stops accumulating in the saturating direction (conditional integration, the textbook anti-windup). None disables it. With a downstream tanh bound, a value of about 3 (where tanh is within 0.5 % of its rail) is a sensible choice: it stops the integral from winding up while the applied input is pinned, so the loop does not overshoot when it comes off the rail.

docs.text:
__call__(carry, z, resets)

z: (T, B, n), resets: (T, B) -> (new_carry, u (T, B, n)).

A reset at step t clears the integral and the previous signal before z_t is consumed, so u_t is computed as at the start of an episode.
