docs.title: ajax.networks.blocks
docs.text:
Dense layers and normalised MLP shared by DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2.

Both world-model agents build every network from the same hidden layer, Dense -> Norm -> Activation with the bias kept, and differ only in its configuration:

  • DreamerV3 (arXiv:2301.04104v2 Table 4, "RMSNorm + SiLU"; danijar/dreamerv3@2411f7d:dreamerv3/nets.py:367-403 MLP, :594-635 Linear, :724-758 Norm, :816-884 Initializer): RMSNorm with epsilon 1e-4 and a learnable scale only, SiLU, kernels from the fan-in truncated normal, output layers scaled by outscale (0 for the reward and value heads, 0.01 for the policy).
  • TD-MPC2 (arXiv:2310.16828v2 Sec. 3.1 and App. A, "LayerNorm + Mish", 1 % dropout after the first linear layer of each Q-function; nicklashansen/tdmpc2@5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/layers.py:85-122 NormedLinear and mlp, common/init.py:4-17 weight_init): LayerNorm with epsilon 1e-5 and a learnable scale and shift, Mish, dropout between the first Linear and its norm, kernels from N(0, 0.02^2), final weights of the reward and Q heads zeroed.

flax's defaults match neither paper (epsilon 1e-6, and LayerNorm's fast variance E[x^2] - E[x]^2, off by ~0.2 on mean-1000 unit-variance inputs where torch's two-pass variance is within 1e-4), so :class:NormedMLP sets them explicitly. Statistics are computed in float32: DreamerV3 at 2411f7d computed the RMS in its bf16 compute dtype, and Ajax runs these agents in float32 throughout (deviation D4 in docs/world_models/deviations.md). Output layers and heads are composed by the agents with :func:linear.

docs.title: NormedMLP
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Stack of layers hidden layers Dense -> [Dropout] -> Norm -> Act.

Every layer has width units. Dropout (inverted, rate dropout) is applied only after the Dense of the first layer and only when deterministic is False, using the 'dropout' RNG stream (TD-MPC2 layers.py:120, dropout*(i==0)). There is no output layer: compose one with :func:linear. Use :meth:dreamerv3 and :meth:tdmpc2 for the papers' configurations.

Attributes:

Name Type Description act Union[str, ActivationFunction]

activation or activation name (see parse_activation).

norm Literal['layer', 'rms']

"rms" (scale only) or "layer" (scale and shift, exact two-pass variance).

norm_eps float

epsilon added to the mean square or variance.

kernel_init Union[str, InitializationFunction]

initializer or initializer name of the Dense kernels.

dropout float

dropout rate of the first layer; 0 disables it.

docs.title: dreamerv3 classmethod
docs.text:
dreamerv3(layers, units, **module_kwargs)

DreamerV3's MLP trunk: RMSNorm(eps 1e-4) and SiLU, fan-in init.

nets.py:390-391 applies layers x Linear(units, act='silu', norm='rms') with winit: normal and fan in (configs.yaml:113-129, nets.py:600-601); RMSNorm's default epsilon is 1e-4 (nets.py:728).

docs.title: tdmpc2 classmethod
docs.text:
tdmpc2(layers, units, dropout=0.0, **module_kwargs)

TD-MPC2's hidden NormedLinear layers: LayerNorm(eps 1e-5) and Mish.

layers.py:85-100 (Linear -> Dropout -> LayerNorm -> Mish, torch LayerNorm epsilon 1e-5) and init.py:7-9: torch's trunc_normal_(std=0.02) truncates at the absolute bounds +-2, i.e. 100 standard deviations, so it is N(0, 0.02^2), hence "normal(0.02)"; jax's truncated_normal(0.02) would cut at +-0.04 and shrink the standard deviation to 0.0176. TD-MPC2 sets dropout=0.01 for the Q-functions only.

__call__(x, deterministic=None)

Apply the trunk to x [..., in]; returns [..., units].

docs.text:
linear(
    features,
    kernel_init,
    bias_init="zeros",
    outscale=1.0,

docs.title: ajax.distributional
docs.text:
Symlog transforms and two-hot discrete regression (DreamerV3, TD-MPC2).

Both world-model agents predict rewards and values as a categorical distribution over fixed bins and train it with a cross-entropy against a two-hot target: the scalar target is spread over its two neighbouring bins by linear interpolation. The papers share the idea but not the details, and the details matter for fidelity:

  • DreamerV3 (Hafner et al., arXiv:2301.04104v2, Eqs. 9-12 and p.18; paper-era code danijar/dreamerv3@2411f7d) places 255 bins at symexp(linspace(-20, 20, 255)) (dreamerv3/nets.py:462-466), interpolates the raw target between them and predicts the expectation of the raw bins (dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:210-274).
  • TD-MPC2 (Hansen et al., arXiv:2310.16828v2, Sec. 3.1 and Table 8; paper-era code nicklashansen/tdmpc2@5f6fade) places 101 bins at linspace(-10, 10, 101) in symlog space, interpolates clip(symlog(y), -10, 10) between them and predicts symexp(E_p[bins]) (tdmpc2/common/math.py:5-9, 66-95).

In raw space both bin sets are symexp(linspace(-limit, limit, n)); they differ in the bin count, the limit and the space in which the target is interpolated and the expectation taken. :class:TwoHot captures exactly these three parameters. For the same target the two interpolation spaces give different weights even on identical bins (y = 1 on DreamerV3's bins: upper weight 0.3827 in raw space, 0.4015 in symlog space), and symexp(E[b]) != E[symexp(b)], so neither can be simplified into the other.

Both bin sets are built by mirroring their negative half, so the middle bin is exactly 0 and the bins are exactly antisymmetric. The expectation is DreamerV3's symmetric sum over mirror bins, written so that uniform probabilities give exactly 0 in eager and in jitted code alike: a zero-initialised head predicts 0 (:meth:TwoHot.decode).

Fidelity, tested against literal ports of both references (tests/world_models/reference_impls.py), with the float32-level departures registered as deviations D22 (DreamerV3) and T24 (TD-MPC2) in docs/world_models/deviations.md:

  • The bins are the float32 roundings of their float64 values, computed once with numpy, so they are the same constants in eager and jitted code and on every backend. The references evaluate the same expressions in float32 on the device: DreamerV3's jnp bins differ from these by up to 1.3e-6 relative (mostly float32 linspace rounding near 0), TD-MPC2's torch.linspace bins by up to 4.8e-7 (its middle bin is -1.5e-7, not 0).
  • Given the same bins, :meth:TwoHot.encode and :meth:TwoHot.loss are bit-identical to DreamerV3's code run op by op, and :meth:TwoHot.decode is within 3 eps E_p|b| of it (eps the float32 machine epsilon), eagerly and under jax.jit.
  • TD-MPC2 encodes with a floor formula on its uniform grid. The generic interpolation used here is equal in exact arithmetic, and in float32 the more accurate of the two (within 2e-6 of the exact weights, against up to 8.6e-6 for the floor formula, whose positions near 100 have an ulp of 7.6e-6); they agree to 1.1e-5. TD-MPC2's naive expectation is matched within eps (1 + 6 E_p|b|) in symlog space (4.8e-6 at most; the eps term is its exp(|x|) - 1 rounding near 0), and its F.log_softmax (max subtracted first) within 3 eps (max|logits| + loss).

docs.title: TwoHot dataclass
docs.text:
TwoHot(num_bins, limit, transform)

Two-hot discrete regression over symlog-spaced bins.

Frozen and hashable, so it can be a jax.jit static argument or a field of a frozen module config. Use the paper constructors :meth:dreamerv3 and :meth:tdmpc2 rather than the raw fields.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default num_bins int

number of bins n; odd and at least 3, so that the middle bin is 0 and the symmetric summation pairs every bin.

required limit float

the bins span [-limit, limit] in symlog space, i.e. [-symexp(limit), symexp(limit)] in raw space. Only symmetric ranges are representable.

required transform Literal['identity', 'symlog']

the space in which targets are interpolated and the expectation is taken. "identity" (DreamerV3): raw space, the bins are symexp(linspace(-limit, limit, n)). "symlog" (TD-MPC2): symlog space, the bins are linspace(-limit, limit, n), the target is symlog(y) and the prediction is symexp of the expectation.

required

All methods compute in float32 and return float32.

docs.title: dreamerv3 classmethod
docs.text:
dreamerv3(num_bins=255)

DreamerV3's symexp_twohot: raw-space bins and interpolation.

Bins symexp(linspace(-20, 20, num_bins)) (range about ±4.85e8), raw targets, raw-space expectation (2411f7d:dreamerv3/nets.py:462-466, jaxutils.py:210-274; bins: 255 in configs.yaml).

docs.title: tdmpc2 classmethod
docs.text:
tdmpc2(num_bins=101, limit=10.0)

TD-MPC2's two_hot: symlog-space bins and interpolation.

Bins linspace(-limit, limit, num_bins) in symlog space (step 0.2 by default, raw range about ±22025), target clip(symlog(y), -limit, limit), prediction symexp(E_p[bins]) (5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/math.py:66-95). TD-MPC2's config has separate vmin: -10 and vmax: +10 (config.yaml:48-50); the range must be symmetric here, which every TD-MPC2 config is: limit = vmax = -vmin (deviation T24).

docs.title: bins
docs.text:
bins()

The [num_bins] bin locations in the interpolation space.

Built as DreamerV3 builds its bins (nets.py:464-466): the negative half linspace(-limit, 0, (n + 1) // 2) (mapped by symexp for the identity transform) concatenated with its negated mirror, so bins[n // 2] == 0 and bins == -bins[::-1] exactly. The half is computed in float64 with numpy and rounded to float32 once, so the bins are trace-time constants, identical in eager and jitted code (deviations D22, T24; module docstring).

docs.title: encode
docs.text:
encode(y)

Two-hot weights [..., num_bins] for scalar targets y [...].

DreamerV3's algorithm (2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:257-271; dreamerv3_spec Algorithm D) applied to the transformed target: linear interpolation between the neighbouring bins b_below <= y < b_above; a target outside the bin range puts all its mass on the edge bin; a target equal to a bin puts all its mass on that bin. On TD-MPC2's uniform symlog grid this equals, in exact arithmetic, its floor formula k = floor((y - vmin) / step), t[k] = 1 - o, t[k + 1] = o after clip(y, vmin, vmax) (5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/math.py:72-77): a clipped target lands exactly on the edge bin. See the module docstring for the float32 agreement (deviation T24).

docs.title: decode
docs.text:
decode(logits)

Predicted scalars [...] from logits [..., num_bins].

inverse_transform(E_p[bins]) with p = softmax(logits) and the expectation summed symmetrically over mirror bins, as DreamerV3 does (2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:226-243; paper p.18) so that a zero-initialised head predicts exactly 0. DreamerV3 sums p_m b_m + sum_i (p_i b_i + p_j b_j) over the mirror pairs (i, j). Under jax.jit XLA contracts each pair into a fused multiply-add, which skips the rounding of one of the two products, so the pairs no longer cancel: on DreamerV3's bins the reference code then gives a constant at zero logits that depends on the compiled program (-0.17 to +0.16 on CPU) and, once the logits move, noise of std about 0.085 on every prediction, enough to slow the actor's early entropy decline (deviation D22). With b_m = 0 and b_i = -b_j exactly, the same sum is sum_j (p_j - p_i) b_j; the difference is exactly 0 for mirror-equal p before any multiplication, so the result is exactly 0 however the operations are fused. It stays noise-free only while the outer logits are bitwise mirror-symmetric, which depends on the compiled program: the outer bins (up to 4.85e8 on DreamerV3's bins) hold about 1/255 of the mass early on, so last-ulp differences between mirrored logits move the prediction by 1e-2 to 1e-1. A naive jnp.sum of p * bins gives 2.0 on DreamerV3's bins (CPU).

docs.title: loss
docs.text:
loss(logits, y)

Soft cross-entropy -sum(w * log_softmax(logits), -1), shape [...].

The log-probabilities are logits - logsumexp(logits) as in DreamerV3 (2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:272-274); TD-MPC2's F.log_softmax (5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/math.py:5-9) subtracts the max first, the same up to float32 rounding (deviation T24). The weights w = encode(y) are stop-gradiented. In both references the callers pass targets that carry no gradient (DreamerV3 agent.py:257 replay data, :349-350 and :371-373 log_prob(sg(...)); TD-MPC2 tdmpc2.py:201-202 and :231-233, TD targets under torch.no_grad, and replay rewards at :257); Ajax makes that explicit. There is no reduction over the batch; callers apply each paper's own weighting and averaging.

docs.title: symlog
docs.text:
symlog(x)

sign(x) * log(1 + |x|), elementwise and dtype-preserving.

DreamerV3 Eq. 9 (2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:76-77); TD-MPC2 5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/math.py:48-54 writes log(1 + |x|), equal to rounding. As in both references the derivative at exactly 0 is 0 (sign'(0) = sign(0) = 0); the limit from either side is 1.

docs.title: symexp
docs.text:
symexp(x)

sign(x) * (exp(|x|) - 1), the inverse of :func:symlog.

DreamerV3 2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:80-81; TD-MPC2 5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/math.py:57-63 (exp(|x|) - 1).

docs.title: ajax.normalizers
docs.text:
Percentile-range scale normalisers (DreamerV3 retnorm, TD-MPC2 RunningScale).

Both world-model agents divide a quantity by a running estimate of the spread between its 5th and 95th percentiles, floored at 1, so that the actor's learning signal is invariant to the reward scale without amplifying small returns. The papers describe the same idea ("an EMA of the 5-95 percentile range, floored at 1"), but the two implementations differ, and each normaliser below reproduces its own reference:

  • :class:ReturnNormalizer, DreamerV3's return normaliser (arXiv:2301.04104v2 p.6 and Eq. 7, Table 4; Moments(impl='perc', rate=0.01, limit=1.0) at danijar/dreamerv3@2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxutils.py:301-395, configs.yaml:141): separate EMAs of the 5th and 95th percentiles, both starting at 0, no bias correction; the floor is applied when the scale is read, max(1, hi - lo). Bit-identical to the reference run op by op.
  • :class:RunningScale, TD-MPC2's Q normaliser (arXiv:2310.16828v2 Sec. 3.1, Table 8; nicklashansen/tdmpc2@5f6fade:tdmpc2/common/scale.py:4-45): one EMA starting at 1 of the range floored before averaging, S <- lerp(S, max(1, p95 - p5), tau). Equal to the reference up to float32 rounding of the EMA (deviation T25 in docs/world_models/deviations.md).

Clamping before or after the EMA, and starting at 0 or 1, give different scales on the same data (ranges alternating 0 and 3: 1.5075 vs 2.0050). Both EMAs are optax.incremental_update.

In both references the statistics are updated before the scale is read in the same training step, so the current batch already counts: DreamerV3 agent.py:329 (retnorm(ret, update)), TD-MPC2 tdmpc2.py:188-189 (update then divide). Percentiles are jnp.percentile with linear interpolation over all elements of the stop-gradiented float32 input; TD-MPC2's sort-and-interpolate _percentile (scale.py:23-35) is the same formula, and it always receives a (B, 1) batch, so "all elements" is "over the batch". Neither normaliser passes gradients.

docs.title: ReturnNormalizer
docs.text:
Bases: Replaceable

DreamerV3 return normaliser state; see the module docstring.

lo and hi are the EMAs of the 5th and 95th percentiles of the returns. Use as norm = norm.update(returns) followed by norm.scale() in the same step (update, then read). DreamerV3 divides advantages by the scale and does not subtract the offset lo.

Attributes:

Name Type Description lo, hi

float32 scalars, both 0 at :meth:create.

rate float

EMA rate, 0.01 (decay 0.99).

limit float

floor of the scale, 1.0.

docs.text:

Initial state: lo = hi = 0 (jaxutils.py:319-321).

lo and hi are two arrays, not one aliased twice, so that a state holding the normaliser can be donated to a jitted function.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
update(x)

Fold the percentiles of all elements of x into the EMAs.

lo <- (1 - rate) lo + rate P5(x), hi likewise with P95 (jaxutils.py:356-359). No bias correction. optax.incremental_update adds the same two products in the other order, which is exact: floating-point addition commutes.

docs.title: scale

max(limit, hi - lo), stop-gradiented (jaxutils.py:382-386).

docs.text:

TD-MPC2 running Q scale state; see the module docstring.

Use as scale = scale.update(q) then q / scale.scale() in the same step (update before divide), with q the (B, 1) batch of t = 0 policy-loss Q values (tdmpc2.py:188-189).

Name Type Description value Array

the float32 scale S, 1 at :meth:create; always >= 1.

rate float

EMA rate tau, 0.01 (TD-MPC2 reuses the target-network tau).

Initial state: S = 1 (scale.py:9).

docs.text:
update(x)

S <- (1 - rate) S + rate max(1, P95(x) - P5(x)) (scale.py:37-40).

The range is floored at 1 before it enters the average, so S never drops below 1. torch's lerp_ computes S + rate (v - S), the same average up to float32 rounding (deviation T25).

docs.title: Training loop
docs.text: The agents share one loop, TrainLoop: it collects experience, waits for learning_starts, folds the extensions, evaluates, logs and resumes the same way for every agent. An agent supplies only its init and update. Architecture explains how the pieces fit.

docs.title: ajax.agents.loop
docs.text:
The training loop the agents share.

An agent's make_train builds a :class:TrainLoop and hands it what makes the agent its algorithm: how to initialise its state and how to update it. The loop owns everything else, the same for every agent::

fresh run:  state = init(key), then every extension's initial state
            and one-shot pretraining
resumed:    state = the checkpointed state
iterate:    collect one step per env (off-policy) or a rollout (on-policy)
            if timestep >= learning_starts (on-policy: always):
                state, aux = update(state, experience)
                fold the extensions' post_update
            else:
                aux = the update's metrics, filled with NaN
            evaluate and log every log_frequency steps

An off-policy agent that acts, trains and evaluates its own way (the world models: a planner or a filtered latent acts through the row collector, a train ratio schedules the updates) supplies those steps too, and the loop runs them in the same order (:meth:TrainLoop.off_policy)::

iterate:    state, experience = collect(state, tick)
            repeat n_updates(tick, state) times:
                state, _ = update(state, experience)
                fold the extensions' post_update
            evaluate and log every evaluation.every ticks

A replay agent given a dataset trains offline instead (:meth:TrainLoop.offline)::

fresh run:  the replay and the normalisers start from the dataset
iterate:    state, aux = update(state, None)   # no environment step
            fold the extensions' post_update
            evaluate and log every log_frequency updates

The result is :func:ajax.perf_utils.build_resumable_train's jitted train(key, index, initial_state, resume_from_state), which :meth:ajax.agents.base.ActorCritic.train vmaps over seeds. It returns (state, None) without a logging config, the evaluation not even traced (tracing alone rebuilds the evaluation env). With one it evaluates every log_frequency steps, whether or not a backend (W&B, TensorBoard) records the logs, and returns (state, evaluations): every logged key's values at the evaluations, in order, padded to the most a call makes with -1 (integer leaves, the timestep) and NaN. They are written into rows the scan carries, not stacked per iteration, which would cost seeds x iterations memory.

docs.title: off_policy
docs.text:
off_policy(
    init,
    update,
    learning_starts=0,
    *,
    recurrent=False,
    expose_rollout=False,
    after_collect=None,
    collect_kwargs=None,
    eval_kwargs=None,
    collect=None,
    n_updates=None,
    evaluation=None,
    num_ticks=None,
)

Train on one environment step per env per iteration (a tick).

Each tick collects a step (uniform actions before learning_starts), applies after_collect(agent_state, transition) when given, then from learning_starts runs update(agent_state, transition), then evaluates the actor (:meth:evaluate_and_log). expose_rollout keeps the step on agent_state.last_rollout as a T = 1 rollout. The budget is :attr:budget // n_envs ticks.

An agent acting, training and evaluating its own way (the module docstring) supplies those steps: collect replaces the collection and the arguments configuring it; n_updates(tick, agent_state) updates (of the absolute, unbatched tick: a train ratio, a burst; or of the collected state: the env steps the tick took) replace the learning_starts gate (:meth:repeat_update); evaluation replaces the actor's evaluation (:meth:evaluate_every); num_ticks the budget.

With :attr:offline_data it trains offline instead (:meth:offline).

docs.title: offline
docs.text:
offline(
    init, update, buffer, recurrent=False, eval_kwargs=None
)

Train on :attr:offline_data alone, with no environment step.

A fresh run's replay and normalisers start from the dataset's rows (:func:seed_replay). Each tick runs update(agent_state, None) on that replay, folds post_update and counts the update in the collector's timestep: the schedules run over the updates, and the evaluations (:meth:evaluate_and_log) come every log_frequency updates and log the updates done as their timestep. The budget is :attr:budget updates.

    n_steps,
    *,
    recurrent=False,

    collect_kwargs=None,

)

Train on an n_steps rollout per env per iteration.

Each iteration collects the rollout from the state start (:func:collect_experience with collect_kwargs), then runs update(agent_state, rollout, start) and folds post_update; expose_rollout keeps the rollout on agent_state.last_rollout. The budget is :meth:n_rollouts; the last one may reach past the call's end, and evaluates there when the horizon is further.

critic_step(

    batch,

    value_loss,

A replay agent's critic step on batch (a :class:Transition).

Folds the extensions' on_target into target_q (held constant), then steps the critic down value_loss(params, target_q) -> (loss, aux) plus their critic_loss terms. rewards, dones (where the bootstrap is cut), gamma (None for an average-reward agent) and reward_scale are what the target used; key, split between the two folds, is one the agent draws nothing else on. target_extras joins the on_target batch (TD3's smoothed next actions). Returns the stepped critic state, aux, the gradients' norm (:func:gradient_step) and the two folds' metrics.

docs.title: ajax.perf_utils
docs.text:
Shared JAX-pure performance helpers for Ajax agents.

Patterns the perf audits found across agents (PERFORMANCE_LOG.md), written once so a fix lands in one place instead of in every agent's train_*.py.

docs.title: build_resumable_train
docs.text:
build_resumable_train(
    *,
    init_fn,
    make_scan_fn,
    num_updates,
    resume_transform=None,
    carry_out=None,
)

Build the canonical init-or-resume + lax.scan inner train fn.

Every Ajax agent shares this skeleton, written once here so it cannot drift between agents: build a fresh agent_state with init_fn (its one-shot initialisation included, so a continued run does not re-run it) or, with resume_from_state=True, reuse the initial_state handed in from a checkpoint; then jax.lax.scan the per-iteration body num_updates times, its input the iteration index. Each agent's make_train keeps its own setup (networks, optimisers, action pipeline, logging) and hands the pieces over.

The returned train function has the signature

train(key, index=None, initial_state=None, resume_from_state=False,
      iteration_offset=0, shared=None)

and is jitted with resume_from_state static (the init-fresh vs load-from-checkpoint branch is dead-code-eliminated) and initial_state donated: XLA reuses the incoming agent-state buffers on the resume path, saving one agent state of peak memory (donating None, the init path, is a no-op).

The scan input is the iteration index iteration_offset + arange(num_updates): a resumed run passes the number of iterations already done so the body sees absolute iteration indices and every schedule computed from them (seed phase, update bursts, static resets, logging cadence) continues instead of restarting. A passed offset is a traced scalar (one compilation serves every offset) and must be unbatched -- pass it through jax.vmap with in_axes=None -- so the index, and every predicate derived from it, stays unbatched under the seed vmap. The default (the Python int 0, not passed) adds nothing to the program.

shared is an optional pytree the body reads but never carries -- an offline dataset, say -- handed to make_scan_fn as the keyword argument shared (only when it is not None, so builders that do not take it are unchanged). Pass it through the seed vmap with in_axes=None: it then enters the compiled program once, as an argument shared by every seed. Closing over it instead would bake it into the program as a constant (HLO bloat, a recompilation per dataset), and a batched argument would copy it per seed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default init_fn Callable[[Any, Any], Any]

(key, index) -> agent_state. Builds a fresh agent state. Called only on the fresh-init path. index is the per-seed index (or None); agents that don't need it simply ignore it.

required make_scan_fn Callable[..., Callable[..., Tuple[Any, Any]]]

a builder (agent_state, resume_from_state, key, index) -> body of the per-iteration body (carry, x) -> (carry, aux), invoked once at trace time, after init/resume is resolved, so the body can be finished from the resolved state, branch on whether this is a resume, or use the per-call key / per-seed index or the shared input (passed as shared= when given).

required num_updates int

number of scan iterations (static int).

required resume_transform Callable[[Any, Any], Any] | None

optional one-shot (agent_state, key) -> agent_state applied on the resume path only (e.g. re-initialising the optimizer for a new curriculum stage while keeping the learned parameters).

None carry_out Callable[[Any, Any], Any] | None

optional (agent_state, index) -> out, the initial value of an output the body writes into as it goes (in place) instead of stacking one per iteration. The body then maps ((agent_state, out), x) to ((agent_state, out), None) and train returns the final (agent_state, out).

None

docs.title: final_aux_scan
docs.text:
final_aux_scan(body, init_carry, length, xs=None)

Run lax.scan and expose only the final-step aux from the body.

Replaces the common idiom

carry, ys = jax.lax.scan(body, init, xs, length=length)
last_aux = jax.tree.map(lambda x: x[-1], ys)

with a carry-only variant that never materializes the leading scan axis on device for the aux. Critical under vmap-over-seeds because the discarded ys dimension would otherwise grow as [seeds, length, *aux_shape] purely to be thrown away.

The body maps (carry, x) -> (new_carry, aux), aux a pytree of arrays (any structure).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default xs Any

optional pytree of per-step inputs; if None, the body receives None as x each step (matches scan semantics).

None

Returns:

Type Description

(final_carry, last_aux) where last_aux is the body's

return value on the final iteration only.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
This page explains how Ajax is put together: where the code lives, how a call to agent.train() becomes one compiled program, what the shared training loop does for every agent, and where extensions, evaluation and logging plug in. Read it before changing an agent or the loop. To add an agent or an extension, follow Contributing and Writing an extension.

Three ideas shape the code:

  • A run is one compiled program. Initialisation, every training iteration, the evaluations and the logging calls are traced once and run inside jax.lax.scan. Seeds are a jax.vmap over that program, so eight seeds cost one compilation.
  • An agent is its algorithm. Collecting experience, the warm-up before learning starts, evaluating, logging and resuming are written once, in the shared loop. An agent's folder holds the paper's maths and little else.
  • Research features are extensions. An agent accepts its own hyperparameters plus extensions=(). A feature such as behaviour cloning before training or an extra loss term is an Extension folded into the loop, not a keyword on the agent. The exceptions left are expert_policy (SAC, TD3, REDQ, AVG, APO), SAC's options that reach its network's input, collection or action pipeline, which extensions do not reach yet, and TD3's action_pipeline for a downstream project.

docs.title: The package
docs.text:
src/ajax/
├── __init__.py          the 14 exported agents; configures the compile cache on import
├── agents/
│   ├── base.py          ActorCritic: environment and network setup, extensions=, train(); run_config
│   ├── loop.py          TrainLoop, the shared loop; critic_step and gradient_step
│   ├── recurrent.py     replay buffers and R2D2-style sequence replay for memory=
│   ├── cloning.py       the behaviour-cloning loss and fit that CloningPretrain runs
│   └── <AGENT>/         one package per agent (below)
├── extensions/          Extension, ExtensionStack and the shipped extensions
├── environments/
│   ├── create.py        build an env from an id (gymnax, Brax, MuJoCo Playground), add Ajax's layers
│   ├── interaction.py   collect_experience: act, step, store, count
│   ├── utils.py         env helpers; the [-1, 1] action map; ExpertInAgentUnits
│   ├── obs_norm.py      agent-side running observation normalisation
│   ├── row_collector.py the world models' collector: one row per env per tick
│   ├── differentiable.py  closed-loop rollouts you can backpropagate through (APG)
│   └── model_reference.py, system_class.py, pid_terms.py   tracking tasks, parameter distributions, PID error terms
├── networks/            actor and critic networks, memory blocks, Squash, the world models' layers
├── modules/             the PID actor and PID output head
├── buffers/             replay buffers (flashbax)
├── logging/             LoggingConfig; the W&B and TensorBoard worker
├── log.py, evaluate.py  when to evaluate and log; the evaluation episodes
├── perf_utils.py        build_resumable_train: init or resume, then one jitted scan
├── state.py             BaseAgentState, CollectorState and the configuration dataclasses
├── checkpoint.py        save_checkpoint, restore_into
├── wrappers.py          env wrappers: normalisation, action clip, auto-reset, observation noise
├── deprecation.py       warn_inert, for keywords on their way out
├── schedule.py          a warm-up and cosine learning-rate schedule
├── distributional.py, normalizers.py   symlog, two-hot and return scales (DreamerV3, TD-MPC2)
└── _compile_cache.py    the persistent JAX compile cache

Each agent package src/ajax/agents/<AGENT>/ holds:

File What it holds <AGENT>.py the public class: the paper's hyperparameters and extensions=; its make_train and train_kwargs train_<AGENT>.py the algorithm, and a make_train that hands its initialisation and update to TrainLoop state.py <AGENT>State and <AGENT>Config core.py (SAC, PPO, TDMPC2) the maths that descendants import instead of copying

The lineage is explicit: ASAC, REDQ and AVG import SAC's core.py; APO imports PPO's; the multi-task TD-MPC2 imports TD-MPC2's. A fix to the parent's maths reaches every descendant. Some agents keep further modules of their own (SAC's action_pipeline.py, TD-MPC2's planner.py).

docs.title: Names that moved, keywords that went
docs.text:
A few names now live where their layer is. The old paths are gone, removed once no downstream project used them rather than kept as aliases.

Was Is ajax.agents.obs_norm ajax.environments.obs_norm ajax.agents.SAC.utils.SquashedNormal, then ajax.networks.distributions.SquashedNormal(loc, scale) ajax.networks.distributions.Squash(distrax.Normal(loc, scale)) NormalizationInfo in ajax.agents.AVG.utils and .state RunningMoments in ajax.agents.AVG.state ajax.plane.get_mode jax.default_backend() the _obs_noise_sigma hook on an env ObservationNoiseWrapper in ajax.wrappers

The keywords below went in October 2026; passing one now raises TypeError.

Keyword Agents Instead pre_train_n_steps, actor_cloning_epochs, actor_cloning_batch_size, actor_cloning_lr, skip_actor_pretrain, reset_log_std_after_bc, reset_actor_head_after_bc SAC, TD3, REDQ, APO extensions=(CloningPretrain(expert, n_steps=..., epochs=..., batch_size=..., skip_actor=..., reset_log_std=..., reset_actor_head=...),), at the actor's learning rate pid_actor_config SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, PPO, APO actor_architecture=PIDPolicy(...) action_scale SAC nothing: SAC never read it, and every continuous action is mapped onto the env's bounds use_expert_guidance SAC nothing: it only switched on diagnostics; ExpertValueMetrics logs the critic's view of the expert reward_shaping_fn, use_vtrace_gae PPO nothing: neither ever ran actor_kernel_init, critic_kernel_init, encoder_bias_init PPO, APO nothing: no run set them; encoder_kernel_init, actor_bias_init, critic_bias_init and PPO's mean_kernel_init stay n_epochs, bc_loss_type UDRL n_updates_per_iter; the loss is the log-likelihood

Every agent is importable from the top level, TD3 and UDRL included: from ajax import TD3.

docs.title: From agent.train() to a compiled program
docs.text:
agent = SAC("Pendulum-v1", extensions=(...))     ActorCritic.__init__
  ├─ self.config = run_config(locals(), name)     what the loggers will record
  ├─ prepare_env                                  the env (episode_length, action_repeat), its params, Ajax's layers
  ├─ EnvironmentConfig, NetworkConfig, OptimizerConfig
  ├─ ExtensionStack(extensions) + checks          phases, buffer fields, experts, phi*: raise here
  └─ experts read in agent units                  ExpertInAgentUnits, the agent's and the extensions'

agent.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=..., logging_config=..., initial_state=...)
  ├─ get_make_train()(env_args, ..., total_timesteps, logging_config)
  │    └─ make_train                              train_<AGENT>.py, with train_kwargs and the extensions
  │         ├─ TrainLoop.create(...)              budget, extensions, logging
  │         └─ loop.off_policy(init, update, ...) or loop.on_policy(...)
  │              └─ build_resumable_train(...)    jitted train(key, index, initial_state, ...)
  ├─ jax.vmap over seeds                          one program, every seed
  └─ block_until_ready, stop the logging worker
returns (state, evaluations)                      every leaf has a leading seed axis

ActorCritic in agents/base.py does the work every agent needs at construction. It builds the environment (prepare_env, which every agent hands episode_length and action_repeat), groups the static settings into frozen configuration dataclasses, and wraps the extensions in an ExtensionStack. It rejects silent misconfigurations early: memory= on an agent whose supports_memory is false, an extension implementing a phase the agent never folds, an extension reading a replay field the agent does not store, a stateful expert called without its state, and an extension reading the frozen expert critic phi* in a stack that never fits it.

train then calls the agent's make_train (bound by get_make_train() to the agent's own train_kwargs and its extensions) with the run's settings. The result is a jitted function of one seed's key. train maps it over the seeds with jax.vmap and waits for the result.

The whole run is a single pytree, so this example's state carries both seeds:

import jax

from ajax import PPO

agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_envs=2, n_steps=64)
state, out = agent.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=512)

print(out)                                # None: no logging config, no evaluation
print(type(state).__name__)               # BaseAgentState: the whole run, one pytree
print(state.collector_state.timestep)     # [640 640]: env steps, every env counted
print(jax.tree.leaves(state.actor_state.params)[0].shape[0])  # 2: the seed axis
print(agent.config["algo_name"], agent.config["n_steps"])     # PPO 64: the run config

The timestep reads 640, not 512, because an on-policy run always makes one rollout more than the budget holds (see the loop shapes).

docs.title: The run config
docs.text: Every agent builds its run config the same way, as the first line of its constructor: self.config = run_config(locals(), self.name). run_config keeps the constructor's arguments, drops self, __class__ and any names passed in exclude (TDMPC2MultiTask leaves out its dataset and evaluation envs), and adds algo_name. DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 then add the settings they resolve from those arguments. With a LoggingConfig, train merges agent.config into logging_config.config, which is what W&B and TensorBoard record for the run.

docs.title: Agent units and env units
docs.text: Every continuous agent acts in [-1, 1], whatever the env's action box. Every env step maps the action onto the box (agent_action_to_env in environments/utils.py: c + h * clip(a, -1, 1) with c the box's centre and h its half-width), so on gymnax Pendulum's [-2, 2] torque the agent reaches the full range. Replay stores the agent's own action. An expert is written in env units and is read through ExpertInAgentUnits, which maps its answer into agent units with the inverse map (env_action_to_agent, unclipped): the agent's expert_policy and every expert an extension holds (its expert_fields) are converted once, at construction. Replay, losses and extensions see one unit.

docs.title: The shared training loop
docs.text:
TrainLoop in agents/loop.py owns everything that is the same for every agent. An agent supplies two functions:

  • init(key) -> agent_state: a fresh state. One-shot pre-training, such as behaviour cloning, is an extension's (CloningPretrain), on a key the loop splits off.
  • update(...) -> (agent_state, aux): one update. aux holds the update's metrics as flax dataclasses nested exactly one level (TD3's AuxiliaryLogs(policy=..., value=...) is logged as value/critic_loss and so on).

The loop does the rest, in this order on every iteration:

fresh run:  state = init(key), then fold_init: each extension's initial state, then its pretrain
resumed:    state = the state passed in
iterate:    collect one step per env (off-policy) or a rollout (on-policy)
            if timestep >= learning_starts (on-policy: always):
                state, aux = update(state, experience)
                fold the extensions' post_update
            else:
                aux = the update's metrics, filled with NaN
            evaluate and log every log_frequency steps

Because this order lives in one place, a fix to it (when the evaluation runs, which key an extension draws, how a resumed run continues) reaches every agent at once. The probes check it end to end: a planted fault that runs post_update before the update instead of after is caught (see Testing).

docs.title: Three iteration shapes
docs.text:
Shape Agents One iteration Budget loop.off_policy(init, update, aux_cls, learning_starts, ...) SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, DQN one step per env (a tick); from learning_starts on, one update(state, transition) budget // n_envs ticks loop.on_policy(init, update, n_steps, ...) PPO, APO, PQN an n_steps rollout per env from the state start, then update(state, rollout, start) budget // (n_envs * n_steps) + 1 rollouts loop.off_policy(..., collect=, n_updates=, evaluation=) DreamerV3, TDMPC2 the agent's own collect(state, tick), then n_updates(tick, state) updates (a train ratio, a burst), then the agent's own Evaluation budget // n_envs ticks, or num_ticks

Before learning_starts, the off-policy shape acts uniformly at random and logs the update's metrics as NaN, which the logger drops. The on-policy shape passes start to the update so that a recurrent agent can replay its rollout from the memory carries it began with.

Three agents use the loop's parts without one of these shapes. UDRL runs its own iteration (a segment, its replay, its command statistics, the updates) on TrainLoop.train, and evaluates its command-conditioned policy every log_frequency steps through an Evaluation. APG and the offline TDMPC2MultiTask call build_resumable_train themselves, with the loop's fresh_state and its post_update fold.

Two helpers serve the replay agents: gradient_step(train_state, loss_fn), one optimiser step, and critic_step(...), a replay critic step that folds the extensions' on_target and critic_loss phases. Both also return the gradients' global norm, before the optimiser clips them. TD3, REDQ, ASAC and AVG use critic_step; SAC builds its own critic step, with the same folds.

docs.title: Agent state
docs.text:
Everything that changes during training lives in one flax dataclass, the agent state. Nothing changes on the Python objects. This is what lets a run be one scan (the state is the carry), lets seeds be one vmap (the state gains a leading axis), and makes a checkpoint a matter of saving that pytree.

BaseAgentState in state.py holds:

Field What it holds rng the training key; every random draw splits it actor_state, critic_state flax TrainStates with target parameters, memory carries and the observation normaliser's statistics collector_state the environment state, last observation and episode flags, the replay buffer, timestep, the rolling episodic return, a stateful expert's internal state eval_rng the evaluations' key, split apart from rng and never advanced: evaluation n draws from fold_in(eval_rng, n) n_updates, n_logs counters; n_logs gates the evaluations and numbers them ext_state one entry per extension, () without extensions last_rollout the latest rollout, kept only when the agent is asked to expose it

Agents subclass it: SoftACState adds SAC's temperature and is shared by SAC, ASAC, REDQ and AVG; the world models carry their model and replay. collector_state.timestep counts environment steps over all parallel environments (one collection step on four environments adds four). The learning_starts gate, the logging cadence and the training fraction all read it.

Static settings stay out of the state. EnvironmentConfig, NetworkConfig, OptimizerConfig and the agent's <AGENT>Config are frozen and passed as static arguments, so they fix shapes and Python-level decisions at trace time. Extensions are static for the same reason: they must be hashable and must never change after construction.

docs.title: Extensions in the loop
docs.text:
Each phase the stack folds is one method of ExtensionStack, fold_<phase>, and an agent makes one call to it where the phase applies (SAC's action pipeline dispatches action itself). The call builds the ExtensionContext (step, rng, total_steps), runs the extensions in the order given, reads (and, for pretrain and post_update, writes) agent_state.ext_state, and returns the result. On an empty stack it returns its input unchanged (a loss term is 0.0) without building anything, so an agent without extensions traces nothing extra and never guards a fold.

Call Where it is made fold_init (each init_state, then each pretrain) fresh_state, fresh runs only (a resumed state already carries both) fold_post_update after every update: the loop's maybe_update, repeat_update and on_policy; APG, UDRL and TDMPC2MultiTask in their own iterations fold_eval_metrics at every evaluation, merged into the logged metrics (compose_eval_metrics in log.py) fold_on_target, fold_critic_loss in the agent's critic step; critic_step for TD3, REDQ, ASAC and AVG fold_actor_loss in the agent's actor step the action phase SAC's action pipeline only, with an expert policy

fold_on_target, fold_critic_loss and fold_actor_loss return their value and the metrics the phases returned beside theirs; the agent carries them out of its loss as an aux and logs them, in its AuxiliaryLogs' extensions field, under their own names.

The first three are the loop's own (LOOP_PHASES: pretrain, post_update, eval_metrics); an agent lists those plus the phases its update folds in supported_extension_phases, and construction rejects any other. Each fold gets a key of its own, split from one the agent draws nothing else on, so an extension never shares randomness with the agent's own draws.

Writing an extension covers the phases in detail.

docs.title: Evaluation and logging
docs.text:
Three modules share the work:

  • log.py decides when. evaluate_and_log evaluates once every log_frequency environment steps, counted against n_logs, and never past the run's horizon. Agents with their own Evaluation (the world models, APG, UDRL) use maybe_eval_and_log, gated on the scan index. Every evaluation draws fresh keys (evaluation_keys: split(fold_in(eval_rng, n_logs)), one key for the episodes, one for the extensions' metrics), the same per seed from one run to the next and apart from training.
  • evaluate.py runs the episodes: num_episode_test episodes with the deterministic action, reporting the mean return, the episode length, the policy's entropy and, for the discounted agents with a critic (SAC, TD3, REDQ, AVG, DQN, PQN, PPO), the value bias (Eval/mean bias: the critic's estimate minus the discounted return realised from each evaluated step, in the critic's units). With an expert it also rolls the expert out on the same episodes at each evaluation and reports its return.
  • logging/wandb_logging.py records. LoggingConfig names the backend (use_wandb, use_tensorboard) and the cadence. The compiled program hands each evaluation's metrics to a host callback, which forwards them to a separate worker process that writes to Weights & Biases or TensorBoard. The worker starts only when a backend is enabled.

What train returns follows from the logging config:

  • No LoggingConfig: no evaluation is traced at all (tracing alone would rebuild the evaluation environment), and train returns (state, None). APG returns its per-update metrics in place of None.
  • A LoggingConfig: the run evaluates whether or not a backend records it, and returns (state, evaluations): every logged key's values per seed and evaluation. The values are written into rows the scan carries, not stacked per iteration, which would cost seeds x iterations memory. Rows a call does not fill hold -1 (the timestep) or NaN.

Two details keep the gates correct under the seed vmap. The counters a gate reads (the timestep, n_logs, the scan index) stay unbatched, so jax.lax.cond stays a real branch and evaluates only on logging iterations; a batched predicate would turn it into a select that runs the evaluation on every iteration. And the logging callback checks its flag itself (gated_log_callback), so it fires only on real evaluations in either lowering.

docs.title: Resuming
docs.text:
perf_utils.build_resumable_train builds every agent's jitted train(key, index, initial_state, resume_from_state). On a fresh run it calls init; on a resumed one it takes the state passed in, whose buffers XLA reuses (the argument is donated).

ActorCritic.train(initial_state=state) continues a run. It checks that every seed stands at the same timestep, evaluation count and update count (shared_counters; only an agent declaring per_seed_update_counts, TD-MPC2 in its episodic mode, may differ in updates, and keeps them batched), keeps those counters unbatched, and trains from that timestep to timestep + n_timesteps (the loop's end_timestep). Every schedule (the training fraction, the extensions' total_steps, the exploration, the logging's end) runs to the run's horizon, train's total_timesteps (by default the call's end; the loop's total_timesteps), so a resumed run continues where it stopped instead of restarting its schedules, and a run whose calls are all told its horizon follows the schedules of one call. Agents whose schedules depend on the absolute tick (the world models) also pass an iteration offset. A run split in two, on a new agent instance, ends in the state one uninterrupted call reaches (tests/agents/test_resume_contract.py). checkpoint.py saves a state's arrays to disk and grafts them back onto a fresh skeleton; see Checkpoints and resuming. A state class that deletes a data field lists it in its removed_fields, a ClassVar[frozenset[str]]: checkpoints saved with the field then restore without it. A saved field that its class neither has nor lists still fails to restore. A class that gains a float field lists it in its added_fields: checkpoints saved before it restore it as NaN.

docs.title: Keywords on their way out
docs.text:
A public keyword is removed in two steps (CLAUDE.md, rule 10, "expand, then contract"): first the new form is added and downstream projects move to it, then the old one goes. A keyword that no longer does anything but that callers still pass stays accepted meanwhile, and says so with ajax.deprecation.warn_inert: a FutureWarning for each such keyword set to something other than None, pointing at the caller's line and giving the reason.

import warnings

from ajax import SAC

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    SAC("Pendulum-v1", jsrl_curriculum=True)  # SAC counts episode steps itself
print([str(w.message) for w in caught if w.category is FutureWarning])
# ["SAC's jsrl_curriculum has no effect and will be removed: SAC counts each
#   env's steps in its episode when an extension reads them (JSRLCurriculum)."]

Today it covers SAC's jsrl_curriculum (SAC now counts episode steps whenever an extension reads them) and LoggingConfig's horizon, which nothing reads. Keywords whose downstream callers have moved are removed outright, without a warning.

docs.title: Compilation
docs.text: import ajax points JAX at a persistent compile cache (~/.cache/ajax/jax_compile_cache, or AJAX_JAX_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR; one subdirectory per CPU, Python, JAX and jaxlib version; AJAX_NO_COMPILE_CACHE=1 turns it off). A second process with the same shapes and code loads the compiled program instead of compiling it. JAX never caches a program that contains a host callback, so a run with a LoggingConfig recompiles in each new process. CI restores the cache each job left on the last push to main. Performance has the numbers.

docs.title: Contributing to Ajax
docs.text: This guide is for changing Ajax: where the code lives, how an agent trains, how to add an agent or an extension, and how the tests check them. To use Ajax, read the README. CLAUDE.md holds the checks a change must pass and the refactoring rules; this guide does not repeat them.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text: Install as the README says, then run uv run pre-commit install once, so ruff and mypy check every commit. Prefix commands with uv run, or activate .venv.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
Architecture gives the overview. These are the pieces every agent shares:

src/ajax/
├── agents/base.py       ActorCritic: environment and network setup, extensions=, train()
├── agents/loop.py       TrainLoop, the shared loop; critic_step and gradient_step
├── agents/recurrent.py  replay buffers and R2D2-style sequence replay for memory=
├── agents/cloning.py    the behaviour-cloning loss and fit (CloningPretrain's)
├── extensions/base.py   Extension, ExtensionStack, ExtensionContext, the phases
├── environments/interaction.py  collect_experience: act, step and store
├── perf_utils.py        build_resumable_train: initialise or resume, then one jitted scan
├── log.py, evaluate.py  when to evaluate and log; the evaluation episodes
├── state.py             BaseAgentState, BaseAgentConfig, the configuration dataclasses
└── checkpoint.py        save_checkpoint, restore_into

Agent anatomy. Each folder src/ajax/agents/<AGENT>/ holds <AGENT>.py, the public class (the paper's hyperparameters and extensions=; it names its make_train and fills train_kwargs, which get_make_train() binds); train_<AGENT>.py, the algorithm and a make_train that hands its initialisation and update to TrainLoop; and state.py, <AGENT>State and <AGENT>Config. SAC, PPO and TDMPC2 also have a core.py: the maths their descendants import instead of copying (ASAC, REDQ and AVG from SAC; APO from PPO; TDMPC2MultiTask from it).

docs.title: The shared training loop
docs.text:
The agents share one loop, TrainLoop, so collecting experience, waiting for learning_starts, applying the extensions, evaluating, logging and resuming work the same way everywhere and are fixed in one place. An agent supplies only its algorithm:

  • init(key) -> agent_state: a fresh state. One-shot pretraining (behaviour cloning) is an extension's, on a key the loop splits off.
  • update(...) -> (agent_state, aux): one update. aux holds the metrics as flax dataclasses nested exactly one level, as TD3's AuxiliaryLogs(policy=..., value=...), logged as value/critic_loss; the logger expects that shape.

and picks one of two iterations:

  • loop.off_policy(init, update, aux_cls, learning_starts, ...) (SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, DQN): each iteration collects one step per environment, then, from learning_starts, runs update(agent_state, transition) and folds the extensions' post_update. Before learning_starts the actions are uniform and the metrics are aux_cls filled with NaN, which the logger drops.
  • loop.on_policy(init, update, n_steps, ...) (PPO, APO, PQN): each iteration collects an n_steps rollout per environment from the state start, then runs update(agent_state, rollout, start) and folds post_update. A recurrent agent replays the rollout from start's memory.

The loop does the rest: init and the extensions' initial state and pre-training (ExtensionStack.fold_init) on a fresh run, the given state on a resumed one, then the iterations in build_resumable_train's jitted scan, evaluating and logging every log_frequency steps (with eval_metrics).

Continuous agents act in [-1, 1]; never scale to the env's bounds yourself. Every Ajax env step maps the action onto them (agent_action_to_env), and ActorCritic reads an expert, written in env units, in the same [-1, 1] (ExpertInAgentUnits): replay, losses and extensions see one unit.

The world models (DreamerV3, TDMPC2) also give off_policy their own collect(agent_state, tick), n_updates(tick, agent_state) (such as a train ratio) and Evaluation. UDRL runs its own iteration on TrainLoop.train; APG and the offline TDMPC2MultiTask call build_resumable_train themselves, with fresh_state and the post_update fold.

ActorCritic.train runs the seeds at once (jax.vmap). With a LoggingConfig it returns (state, evaluations), each logged key's values per seed and evaluation, kept whether or not a backend (use_wandb, use_tensorboard, the only case that starts the logging worker) records them. Without one it does not evaluate and returns (state, None); APG returns every update's metrics instead. initial_state=state continues a run.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
An extension is a research feature (an expert to learn from, an exploration rule, an extra loss term, a measurement) that plugs into any agent without changing it, so an agent's surface stays its algorithm's hyperparameters plus extensions=() (see CLAUDE.md, "Extensions are self-contained"). The extensions guide lists the ones Ajax ships.

An extension is a frozen dataclass subclassing Extension. It holds its own settings and overrides only the phases it touches; the other phases keep their defaults, which change nothing. An agent folds its ExtensionStack through a phase in list order, mostly with a stack.fold_<phase>(...) helper (fold_init, fold_on_target, fold_critic_loss, fold_actor_loss, fold_post_update, fold_eval_metrics) that builds the ExtensionContext (step, rng, total_steps) and threads the extensions' state. On an empty stack a helper changes nothing (a loss term is 0.0), so an agent without extensions traces nothing extra and never guards a fold.

Phase What it does Folded today by init_state(agent_state, rng) returns the extension's state ((): none) every agent, fresh runs only pretrain(agent_state, ext_state, ctx) one-shot step before training every agent, fresh runs only on_target(agent_state, ext_state, batch, target, ctx) transforms the TD or value target SAC, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, TD3, DQN, PQN, PPO, APO critic_loss(agent_state, ext_state, batch, ctx) adds a term to the critic loss SAC, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, TD3, DQN, PQN, PPO, APO actor_loss(agent_state, ext_state, batch, ctx) adds a term to the actor loss SAC, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, TD3, PPO, APO, APG, UDRL action(agent_state, ext_state, obs, rng, ctx) overrides the collection action (None defers) SAC with an expert_policy, for extensions with an action_slot eval_action(agent_state, ext_state, obs, rng, ctx) overrides the evaluation action no agent yet post_update(agent_state, ext_state, ctx) runs after each update every agent eval_metrics(agent_state, ext_state, rng, ctx) adds metrics to each evaluation every agent

tests/probing/test_extensions.py checks the phases on the agents with test-only extensions of known effect, and that an extension implementing a phase the agent does not fold is rejected.

Every agent lists the phases it folds in supported_extension_phases: the shared loop's LOOP_PHASES (pretrain, post_update, eval_metrics, in ajax.agents.loop) plus those its update folds; the base class's default is empty. An extension implementing any other phase is rejected when the agent is built instead of being silently ignored.

What changes during training lives in agent_state.ext_state (one entry per extension), never on self: extensions are static arguments of the compiled program, so they stay hashable and unchanged. An extension that needs what the agent builds (environment, network config, buffer, discount) overrides bind_to_agent(**agent_context) to return a new instance holding it, as MCPretrain does; SAC, TD3, REDQ, APO and DreamerV3 call it. The batch a phase receives is a dictionary: the keys every agent puts in it are listed in ajax/extensions/base.py; read the agent's fold call before relying on any other.

docs.title: Adding an agent
docs.text:
Boilerplate goes in the shared code; the algorithm goes in one file, so a reader can follow train_<AGENT>.py like the paper's pseudocode. Lineage rule: an agent descending from another (REDQ from SAC) imports the parent's maths from its core.py. Use critic_step (a replay critic step) and gradient_step (an optimiser step) from agents/loop.py rather than writing your own.

These templates for an agent FOO follow the replay agents TD3 and REDQ; an on-policy agent follows APO instead (no buffer, loop.on_policy).

1. state.py. BaseAgentState already holds the random key, the actor, critic and collector states, the update count and the extensions' state. A replay agent's config extends RecurrentReplayConfig, a BaseAgentConfig for sequence replay; kw_only lets fields without defaults follow others.

@partial(struct.dataclass, kw_only=True)  # Partial from jax.tree_util
class FOOState(BaseAgentState):
    """FOO carries only actor + critic + collector."""


@partial(struct.dataclass, kw_only=True)
class FOOConfig(RecurrentReplayConfig):
    gamma: float
    learning_starts: int = 100
    reward_scale: float = 1.0

2. train_FOO.py. The paper's maths, then make_train. The critic step goes through critic_step, which folds on_target and critic_loss; its keywords are what the target used (dones: where it cut the bootstrap, as TD3's batch.terminated):

def update_value_functions(agent_state, batch, agent_config, extension_stack, total_timesteps):
    key, rng = jax.random.split(agent_state.rng)
    target_q = compute_foo_td_target(agent_state, key, batch, agent_config)  # the paper's target

    def value_loss(params, target_q):  # -> (loss, aux)
        return value_loss_function(params, agent_state.critic_state, batch.obs, batch.action, target_q)

    critic_state, aux = critic_step(
        agent_state, batch, target_q, value_loss, extension_stack, key, total_timesteps,
        rewards=batch.reward, dones=batch.terminated,
        gamma=agent_config.gamma, reward_scale=agent_config.reward_scale,
    )
    return agent_state.replace(rng=rng, critic_state=critic_state), aux


def make_train(
    env_args, actor_optimizer_args, critic_optimizer_args, network_args, buffer,
    agent_config, total_timesteps, num_episode_test,
    run_ids=None, logging_config=None, start_timestep=0, extensions=(),
):
    loop = TrainLoop.create(
        env_args, total_timesteps, num_episode_test, run_ids, logging_config, extensions,
        start_timestep=start_timestep,
    )

    def init(key):
        return init_FOO(key, env_args, actor_optimizer_args, critic_optimizer_args, network_args, buffer)

    def update(agent_state, _transition):
        # The step just collected is in the buffer: FOO samples it from there.
        return update_agent(agent_state, buffer, agent_config, loop.stack, total_timesteps)

    return loop.off_policy(
        init, update, AuxiliaryLogs, agent_config.learning_starts,
        collect_kwargs={"buffer": buffer},
    )

update_agent samples a batch (sample_replay), takes the critic step, then the actor step, whose loss adds extension_stack.fold_actor_loss(...), and returns the state with an AuxiliaryLogs of both steps' metrics. ActorCritic.train calls make_train with the keyword names above (start_timestep when it resumes a run), so keep them. Split a random key for the extensions only under if stack:, so an agent without extensions keeps its random stream.

3. FOO.py.

class FOO(ActorCritic):
    """FOO (Author et al., year) for continuous action spaces; defaults as in the paper."""

    name: str = "FOO"
    # The phases the loop folds, plus those FOO's update folds.
    supported_extension_phases: frozenset = LOOP_PHASES | {
        "on_target", "critic_loss", "actor_loss"
    }
    make_train = staticmethod(make_train)  # ActorCritic.get_make_train binds it

    def __init__(
        self, env_id: str | EnvType, n_envs: int = 1, gamma: float = 0.99,
        buffer_size: int = int(1e6), batch_size: int = 100, learning_starts: int = int(1e4),
        extensions: Sequence[Extension] = (),
    ) -> None:
        self.config = run_config(locals(), self.name)  # what train() logs with the run
        super().__init__(env_id=env_id, n_envs=n_envs, extensions=extensions)
        self.agent_config = FOOConfig(gamma=gamma, learning_starts=learning_starts)
        self.buffer = make_replay_buffer(
            self.agent_config, n_envs, self.network_args.memory, buffer_size, batch_size
        )
        # make_train's own keywords, beyond those every agent's takes.
        self.train_kwargs = {"buffer": self.buffer}

Do not add a keyword for a feature (use_critic_blend=True, ...): it belongs on an extension. Set supports_memory = True only once the agent trains with memory=; until then ActorCritic rejects it.

4. Export and document. Import it in src/ajax/__init__.py, add it to __all__, and add a row to the README's agent table.

5. Tests and benchmark. tests/agents/FOO/: the maths on hand-computed values. tests/agents/test_agent_contract.py: a row, so FOO builds, refuses what it cannot act in and folds extensions on tiny runs. tests/probing/: presets in agents.py, then the cases that fit (test_framework.py fails while an exported agent has none). tests/agents/test_agent_pins.py: a tiny run's fingerprint, so a later restructuring can show it changed nothing. benchmarks/agent_bench.py: an entry in AGENTS and a baseline (see Performance).

docs.title: Adding an extension
docs.text:
Add an extension, never a flag or a keyword on an agent.

  1. Pick the phases from the table and check that the agents you target fold them. If one does not, adding the fold to that agent is a change of its own, and the agent still must not know about your extension.
  2. Write the dataclass in src/ajax/extensions/<topic>.py, its settings as fields. This one counts updates and logs the count; it runs as is:
from dataclasses import dataclass

import jax.numpy as jnp

from ajax import PPO
from ajax.extensions.base import Extension
from ajax.logging.wandb_logging import LoggingConfig


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UpdateCounter(Extension):
    """Counts the updates and logs the count at each evaluation."""

    name: str = "update-counter"

    def init_state(self, agent_state, rng):
        return jnp.asarray(0)

    def post_update(self, agent_state, ext_state, ctx):
        return agent_state, ext_state + 1

    def eval_metrics(self, agent_state, ext_state, rng, ctx):
        # A float: the steps that do not evaluate log NaN in its place.
        return {"Counter/updates": ext_state.astype(jnp.float32)}


agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_steps=128, extensions=(UpdateCounter(),))
logging = LoggingConfig(config={}, log_frequency=1024, use_wandb=False)
state, evaluations = agent.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=4096, logging_config=logging)
print(state.ext_state[0])  # the updates each seed made: [9 9]
print(evaluations["Counter/updates"])  # per seed, at each evaluation: [2. 4. 6. 8.]
  1. Test it in tests/extensions/: the feature fires and does what its paper says (a metric appears, a term moves the loss the right way).

Callable hooks. A few Optional[Callable] keywords predate extensions and stay: TD3's action_pipeline (AjaxExperiments' TD3 variants), DQN's td_target_fn and td_loss_fn and PQN's td_loss_fn (Double DQN and Huber, which their agents' tests run). tests/modules/test_hook_composition.py pins them. Add none.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Two kinds of tests check the code, each answering its own question (Testing is the full guide):

  • Unit tests (tests/<area>/, tests/agents/<AGENT>/) check one component against an exact contract, with no learning. Where agents or extensions share a contract, the test is generic (tests/agents/test_*_contract.py, tests/extensions/test_phase_contract.py, ...): it runs every one of them, and a new one fails it until it joins.
  • Probing tests (tests/probing) train an agent briefly on a tiny generic environment whose answer is known, and check only what learning shows: the right value, the right action, the right count.

A convention that differs from a reference implementation (an ordering, a default, a constant) is for code review, not for a test. Pins record what a tiny run produces today, so a restructuring can show it changed nothing: tests/agents/test_agent_pins.py (tiny runs' fingerprints), tests/extensions/test_sac_extensions_equivalence.py and tests/test_downstream_api.py (the names downstream projects import). Slow tests (@pytest.mark.slow) are the long trainings.

The tests come in two tiers. The fast tier is the tests not marked slow, which every pull request must pass (CI runs the probing harness's own checks and tests/conformance in jobs of their own). A fast test may run a tiny training, but at most 128 gradient steps and about 30 s: tests/conftest.py times each test, counts its gradient steps (the larger of the agent's update count and each train state's step) and lists the tests past either line at the end of the run (AJAX_FAST_MAX_UPDATES, AJAX_FAST_MAX_SECONDS). For now it only reports. A test past the lines belongs in tests/probing, or is marked slow. The slow tier is everything that trains: tests/probing, which tests/conftest.py marks slow, and the tests marked slow elsewhere. Until the fast tests catch what the probes catch, pull requests also run the slow tests, the probes and the conformance tests (below).

Every directory of tests/ that holds Python files is a package (an empty __init__.py; tests/test_repo_hygiene.py checks it), so tests import shared helpers by their full name: from tests.agents.extension_stubs import CounterExt. The benchmark scripts the tests import are on the path through pythonpath in pyproject.toml.

uv run pytest --collect-only -q   # everything imports and collects
uv run pytest tests/agents/TD3    # the tests of what you changed
uv run pytest -m "not slow" -n auto   # the fast tier, a worker per core
make ci   # what CI runs: ci-precommit, ci-test, ci-slow, ci-probe, ci-conformance, docs

The make targets hide the GPU (CPU_ENV) so tests never compete with a running experiment; elsewhere set JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu while a GPU is busy.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs on CPU for every pull request and push to main: Pre-commit; Tests (three shards: the tests not marked slow, probing excluded, under coverage, a pytest-xdist worker per vCPU, at XLA's optimisation level 0 since these programs are tiny; the last shard runs whatever the first two do not name, so a new test file always runs); Coverage (the shards combined, at least 70%); Slow tests (without coverage, which would lengthen them); Probing (five shards by recorded duration, without the families out of the gate, below); Conformance (each agent's training step against its original implementation); Docs (the documentation site, mkdocs build --strict). Lint and Test, the one check branch protection requires, passes only when all of them passed. Pre-commit, Tests, Coverage, Conformance and Docs run on GitHub's arm64 runners, which all come on one CPU model, so a job finds main's compile cache (JAX keys it by the CPU); Slow tests and Probing run on x86, the platform most users train on.

The Slow tier workflow (slow.yml) runs everything that trains (pytest -m slow: tests/probing, marked slow by tests/conftest.py, and the tests marked slow elsewhere) in six shards by recorded duration (--shard I/N, tests/.durations, make durations): daily on main when main changed, by hand, and on a pull request each time the label run-slow-tier is added. A red run on main opens an issue, and bisects the merges since the last green run when that is cheap.

A probe family leaves the pull-request gate once the fast tests catch every fault its catalogue lists (tests/probing/faults/<family>.jsonl). Each such fault's fast field names the fast tests that catch it, measured by planting the fault in a scratch copy and running the fast tests that execute its lines (uv run python -m tests.fault_catches SCRATCH FAMILY). The families out of the gate are listed in faults.OUT_OF_THE_GATE, and ci.yml's Probing job ignores their files; tests/probing/test_framework.py checks both. They still run in the slow tier. Out so far: resuming a split run (test_p4_split_run.py) and memory (test_memory.py).

docs.title: The probing tests
docs.text:
A unit test checks a contract; it cannot show that an agent learns what it should. A probe trains an agent on a tiny problem whose answer is known exactly (a value, a best action, a count) and compares what it learned with the right answer and named wrong ones (a discount applied twice), so a failure names the mistake.

envs.py builds the tiny problems, agents.py holds each agent's presets (pinned by DIGEST), runs.py trains every seed in one compiled program, readouts.py reads values and actions off a trained agent and oracles.py computes the right and wrong answers. In verdict.py, a Query is a reading's right and named wrong answers and a Case adds the budget and tolerances; a check trains seeds 0-7: 7 or more within tolerance pass, 4 or fewer fail, otherwise seeds 8-15 run and 13 of 16 must pass. faults.py and faults/<module>.jsonl plant known bugs in a scratch copy of the source, each naming the tests that must catch it. The test_*.py modules group the cases by subject (value chains, episode ends, bookkeeping, extensions, memory, world models, resuming a split run); test_framework.py tests the harness. A planted fault quotes the source it edits, so any change under src/ajax can break one: such a change runs tests/probing/test_framework.py locally before the push (text and collection only, no training).

A new case's budget and tolerances come from calibration on seeds no check uses (uv run python -m tests.probing.verdict ladder|choose|certify ...; verdict.py describes the procedure); then its module's ANSWER_DIGEST is re-pinned. A known bug stays visible as a strict xfail naming the defect, never as a looser tolerance. The directory is capped at 7,000 lines.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
CLAUDE.md ("Performance no-regression guardrail") sets the rule; here is the check. benchmarks/agent_bench.py times a fixed run per agent; --compare fails when one is slower than --tol (10% by default) against a baseline. Capturing requires --out, so a quick check never overwrites the baseline.

export JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu
uv run python benchmarks/agent_bench.py --only TD3 --out benchmarks/my_change.jsonl
uv run python benchmarks/agent_bench.py --compare benchmarks/agent_baseline.jsonl benchmarks/my_change.jsonl

docs.title: Dependencies and releases
docs.text:
Ajax is a library: pyproject.toml says which versions work, and uv.lock fixes the ones CI and development use. Users' installers never read the lock.

  • Floors only. Each lower bound is the oldest version Ajax works with. Raise it when Ajax needs something newer or an older version is known to break, with a comment saying why. Add an upper bound only after a known break, with its reason, and remove it once Ajax is fixed.
  • The ranges are tested. The Compatibility workflow (compat.yml) runs the tests not marked slow every Monday, and on pull requests that change the dependencies, twice without the lock: at the newest versions allowed, on the newest Python, and with every direct dependency at its floor (uv sync --resolution lowest-direct), on the oldest.
  • The lock is refreshed monthly by Dependabot (dependabot.yml), the JAX stack in one pull request.
  • Python: 3.12 and newer, the versions JAX supports. A version goes when JAX drops it.
  • Releases. Versions follow semantic versioning; before 1.0, a breaking change (a raised floor, a removed keyword) bumps the minor version. A release is an entry in CHANGELOG.md and a vX.Y.Z tag on main, which downstream projects can pin. Public names change by expand then contract (CLAUDE.md, rule 10). Tags come only from the Release workflow (release.yml, by hand, with the version): it tags main's head once the slow tier has passed there, running it first if needed, then publishes that commit to PyPI as ajax-rl.

docs.title: Style
docs.text: Pre-commit (.pre-commit-config.yaml) runs on every commit and in CI: ruff lint with rules I F E W B C RUF ARG (ARG, unused arguments, is off under tests/), ruff-format (settings in pyproject.toml), and mypy on everything but benchmarks/, run in the project's environment (uv run mypy) so it sees jax and flax.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Speed is part of what a change must preserve. This page gives the rule, the benchmark that checks it, and where results are recorded. For how to make a training run fast as a user (seeds, environments, the compile cache), read Performance in the user guide. The benchmarks run on CPU; Ajax claims no GPU speed-up.

docs.title: The guardrail
docs.text:
The rule, from CLAUDE.md: any agent that becomes more than about 10% slower on the standardised benchmark run is investigated to its root cause before the change lands. Small deltas that are understood are written down in PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md. Benchmarks run on CPU by default, so they never compete with an experiment using the GPU. The benchmark is run by hand (Checking a change); CI only tests the script itself (tests/benchmarks).

A regression is not automatically a veto. The recurrent replay rework of October 2026 made SAC with memory 17-24% slower in exchange for exact bootstraps at time limits; the report records the cost, where it goes, the variants measured on the way and the owner's decision. What the rule forbids is a slowdown nobody has explained.

docs.title: The benchmark
docs.text:
benchmarks/agent_bench.py times a fixed training run for each agent:

  • The run. Discrete-action agents train on CartPole-v1, continuous ones on Pendulum-v1, with 4 environments for 8,000 steps, logging off. The environment, n_envs and the step count are pinned, and so is learning_starts=1000 for SAC, TD3, REDQ and ASAC, whose defaults (10,000) would outlast the run. Every other hyperparameter is the agent's default, so the benchmark follows the agent's own code path rather than a tuned configuration. tests/benchmarks/test_agent_bench.py checks that every entry updates within the run.
  • Presets and scenarios. Three agents cannot run that way and get a small documented preset in the script: APG trains on a Pendulum tracking task (it differentiates through the environment), and DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 run shrunken models that keep every code path. SAC has a second scenario, SAC/inverted_pendulum, a Brax task whose episodes terminate, for the auto-reset and terminal targets. The offline TDMPC2MultiTask is not benchmarked.
  • The measurement. For each agent the script first runs a 400-step warm-up (recorded as compile_s, compilation included), then three measured trials, each on a freshly built agent. A fresh agent traces and lowers its program again, and compiles it unless the compile cache holds it. So each trial records two times:
    • measured_s, the whole call, and steps_per_s, the 8,000 steps over it;
    • exec_s, the same time less the spans JAX reports for tracing, lowering and compiling (overlapping spans counted once), and exec_steps_per_s. This is the run's execution alone.

Each result is one JSON line per trial, tagged with the git commit and the JAX backend. --n-seeds N trains N seeds at once, the vmapped program experiments run; steps per second then count every seed's steps.

docs.title: The baseline
docs.text:
benchmarks/agent_baseline.jsonl is the reference a change is compared with. It holds the run of 2026-10-12: main at a8a13c2, macOS on Apple silicon, CPU only, the compile cache off (AJAX_NO_COMPILE_CACHE=1), the script's defaults (4 envs, 8,000 steps, one seed, three trials), 14 entries (every exported agent but TDMPC2MultiTask, plus SAC/inverted_pendulum). The report's section of that date gives the medians.

That baseline breaks with every earlier benchmarks/agent_*.jsonl file in two ways. Before it, SAC, TD3, REDQ and ASAC ran at their default learning_starts=10_000, past the end of the run, so their rows timed collection alone, with no update. And the earlier files have no exec_s. Do not compare against them.

docs.title: Checking a change
docs.text:
Measure both sides on the same machine, one after the other, with the same settings:

export JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu AJAX_NO_COMPILE_CACHE=1
# on main
uv run python benchmarks/agent_bench.py --only TD3 SAC --tag main --out /tmp/bench_main.jsonl
# on your branch
uv run python benchmarks/agent_bench.py --only TD3 SAC --tag branch --out /tmp/bench_branch.jsonl
uv run python benchmarks/agent_bench.py --compare /tmp/bench_main.jsonl /tmp/bench_branch.jsonl

--compare reads exec_steps_per_s when both files have it, and steps_per_s otherwise; it says which at the top. It prints each agent's median on both sides and the change, flags every agent slower than --tol (10% by default), and exits with code 1 when there is one. An agent present on one side only shows as MISSING or NEW (no baseline).

--out has no default: a capture without it stops with an error, so a quick check of one agent can never overwrite the recorded baseline. To compare with the baseline itself, capture on the same kind of machine and pass benchmarks/agent_baseline.jsonl as the first file of --compare.

docs.title: Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• They belong to the machine. Steps per second move with the CPU and with whatever else runs on it. The report's first DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 bench entries, run at a load average of 25 to 35, read 81 and 64-66 steps per second, against 275 and 245 for the whole run in the quiet baseline. Compare files measured on one machine, under similar load.
  • Execution, not compilation. exec_s leaves out tracing, lowering and compiling, which a fresh agent repeats in every trial: at the DreamerV3 preset tracing and lowering alone take about 15-20% of a trial.
