That is why --compare judges exec_steps_per_s. The compile cache still moves compile_s and measured_s, so use the same cache setting on both sides; the baseline was captured with it off.
  • Noise. Single runs swing; the report has seen 15% between identical runs under load, and UDRL's three baseline trials spread from 9,604 to 15,069 execution steps per second. Look at the medians, and repeat a measurement before calling a 10% change real.

docs.title: Recorded results
docs.text:
The benchmarks/*.jsonl files are the recorded results; keep scratch measurements outside the repository.

File What it holds agent_baseline.jsonl the current baseline (above) agent_refactor_before.jsonl, agent_refactor_after.jsonl the agents before (13, the since-deleted SafeSAC included) and after (12) the 2026 refactoring, at a1658d9 and 91ee10f, compile cache off; SAC, TD3, REDQ and ASAC timed collection only results.jsonl perf_bench.py scenarios, May 2026, on a GPU seed_scaling.jsonl, seed_scaling_p3d.jsonl the seed-scaling runs of the user guide's Performance page, May 2026, on a GPU

Older records (per-phase benchmarks, the compile-cache and bf16 experiments) were removed on 2026-10-12; git history has them before d05a9f2.

docs.title: Recording a result
docs.text: PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md is the summary: one dated section per change that moved the numbers. A section says what changed and why, how it was measured (the command, the machine, its load, the number of trials), the table of before and after, and the cause of each delta where it is known. PERFORMANCE_LOG.md is the running log of optimisation attempts, the reverted ones included, with the tricks worth reusing. A new baseline replaces agent_baseline.jsonl and gets its own section, saying how it breaks with the one before.

docs.title: Other measurement tools
docs.text: Script What it measures benchmarks/perf_bench.py SAC scenarios one process per measurement, splitting compile from steady-state time and recording peak GPU memory benchmarks/seed_scaling_report.py prints time per seed against the number of seeds, from benchmarks/seed_scaling.jsonl benchmarks/world_models/learning_checks.py whether an agent learns its task on CPU at a small preset (the world models' learning gates); hours long, run outside CI

docs.title: What keeps Ajax fast
docs.text:
Most of Ajax's speed comes from structure, not from tuning each line. A change that breaks one of these patterns usually shows up in the benchmark.

  • One program per run, seeds as a vmap. The report measured 28 times the single-seed throughput with 32 seeds on Pendulum, and 86 times with 100 seeds on Plane3DCircle: the wall time barely moves as seeds are added.
  • The persistent compile cache. Compilation dominated the start of a fresh process: with the cache, compile and warm-up fell by 77% on a warm process. A program containing a host callback is never cached, so a run with a LoggingConfig recompiles in each new process. CI restores each job's cache from the last push to main.
  • Nothing per-iteration piles up. The loop writes each evaluation's metrics into rows the scan carries instead of stacking metrics at every iteration; final_aux_scan in perf_utils.py keeps only an inner scan's last metrics.
  • Unbatched gates. Every predicate that decides whether to evaluate is built from values shared by all seeds, so jax.lax.cond skips the evaluation instead of computing it on every iteration (see Architecture).
  • Donated state. A resumed run's state is donated to the compiled program, which reuses its buffers instead of holding a second copy.
  • No scatters in hot loops on CPU. XLA runs a scatter one index at a time on CPU. The recurrent replay builds its bootstrap stream with one-hot selects; building it with scatters cost about 15% more on the transformer memory.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Ajax checks its code with two kinds of tests, and each answers a different question (the conformance checks, below, are a third, against an agent's original implementation):

  • Unit tests check one component against an exact contract, with no learning. Where agents or extensions share a contract, the test is generic: it runs every one of them, and a new agent or extension fails it until it joins.
  • Probes are tiny generic environments with known answers. An agent trains on one briefly, and the probe checks a capability of the whole agent: that it learns the right value, picks the right action, counts the right steps.

A convention that differs from a reference implementation (an ordering, a default, a constant) is a matter for code review only, not for a test.

The two kinds do not overlap. A unit test can show that a TD target takes a max rather than a mean; it cannot show that the trained agent's values come out right, which needs the target, the buffer, the episode-end handling, the optimiser and the network to work together. A smoke test that trains on CartPole and checks the return proves little either: a broken agent often still solves CartPole.

Beside them, pins record what a tiny run produces today, so that a restructuring can show it changed nothing.

docs.title: Where the tests live
docs.text:
Kind Where CI job Unit, one component tests/<area>/ (environments, networks, buffers, logging, ...), tests/agents/<AGENT>/ Tests Unit, generic contracts tests/agents/test_*_contract.py, tests/extensions/test_phase_contract.py, tests/extensions/test_no_silent_noop.py, tests/environments/test_wrapper_contract.py, ... (below) Tests, Slow tests Pins tests/agents/test_agent_pins.py, tests/agents/SAC/test_sac_parity.py, tests/extensions/test_sac_extensions_equivalence.py, tests/test_downstream_api.py Tests Slow anywhere, marked @pytest.mark.slow: the option matrix, the resume contract, long trainings Slow tests (and the Slow tier workflow) Probes tests/probing/ Probing (and the Slow tier workflow) Conformance tests/conformance/ (below) Conformance Learning checks benchmarks/world_models/learning_checks.py: a world model learns its task at a small preset; hours on a CPU, run before merging such an agent none

Every directory of tests/ that holds Python files is a package, so tests import shared helpers by their full name (from tests.environments.identity_env import IdentityEnv); tests/test_repo_hygiene.py checks it.

docs.title: The generic contract tests
docs.text:
These tests are written once and run over every agent, extension or wrapper that shares the contract. Each finds its subjects from the code (the exported agents, the subclasses of Extension, the signatures), so a new one cannot slip past: it fails a completeness check until it has a row. Several run on the identity task (tests/environments/identity_env.py), whose observation [t, c] says which step of which episode a row comes from: an episode with c > 0 terminates at t = 3, the others are truncated at t = 5.

Test The contract tests/agents/test_agent_contract.py every agent on the shared loop builds its configs on each action space it acts in and refuses the other; a default run keeps no extension state; a run of two seeds and two envs folds its extensions in step and adds their metrics to every evaluation; the measurement extensions find its critic by themselves; the run config drops the instance; the evaluation key is apart from the training key, and each evaluation draws fresh keys; a continuous agent acts on the env's whole box; episode_length and action_repeat reach the env tests/extensions/test_phase_contract.py for every agent and every phase it folds (on_target, critic_loss, actor_loss, post_update): each batch holds the keys PHASE_BATCH_KEYS documents; each fold gets a key of its own, never one the agent draws on; critic_loss gets the target on_target returned; a loss term moves the network it names, and that one only tests/extensions/test_no_silent_noop.py every extension implementing on_target, critic_loss or actor_loss raises on a batch without what it reads, rather than return its input or 0 tests/extensions/test_extension_phase_support.py each agent accepts exactly the phases it folds; a reader of phi* needs MCPretrain tests/agents/test_compatibility.py every extension and network option (memory, cnn) on every agent, as the agent is built: it builds, or it is refused for a capability the algorithm lacks, or it is a gap pinned with the work that closes it; the matrix is Compatibility, rewritten with AJAX_WRITE_COMPATIBILITY=1 tests/environments/test_wrapper_contract.py every Ajax env wrapper survives copy, deepcopy and pickle, and reports the episode-end flags each step raised, alone and in the stacks create.py builds tests/agents/test_transition_contract.py the transitions every agent hands on_target continue their own episode (a time-limited row's next observation is the final one, not the next episode's first), carry the flags the step raised, and carry the normalised rewards under reward normalisation tests/agents/test_expert_consumers.py every agent taking an expert_policy gives it the raw observation, and a stateful expert its state; the cloning dataset holds its actions in agent units; the evaluation's expert return is its closed form tests/test_evaluate.py, tests/extensions/test_instrumentation_extensions.py every output of the evaluation, and every metric of the measurement extensions, meets its closed form on a known rollout tests/agents/test_reward_normalisation.py every agent taking normalize_rewards hands the normaliser the discount it documents (none by default, reward_normalization_gamma when given) and reports its Train and Eval returns in the env's units (UDRL's Train return is a strict xfail: a known bug) tests/agents/test_carry_restart.py the recurrent actors of PPO, SAC, ASAC, REDQ and TD3 remember only their current episode, for every memory kind: the carry each acts with is the actor's run from a fresh carry over the episode's observations (the fast tier runs each agent once and each kind at least once, the other rows are slow; APG's controller has its own test in tests/agents/APG/test_episode_ends.py) tests/agents/test_option_smoke.py (slow) the option matrix: every pair of an agent's options, and every extension stacked into an agent that folds it, trains a tiny logged run that updates the policy and keeps every parameter finite tests/agents/test_resume_contract.py (slow) a run split in two, its second half on a new agent instance, ends in the state one uninterrupted call reaches, every leaf alike (floats to a relative 1e-5): every agent of the contract table and APG, with the normalisation it takes and with memory where it takes one, every call told the run's horizon so the schedules run as in one call (the world models' own tests hold theirs); fast, a two-call DQN run's epsilon at every step is the one call's

The option matrix and the resume contract train, so their main tests run in the slow tier; their completeness checks (every switch of a signature is in a row, every extension has a builder, every agent has a row) are fast and run with the other unit tests.

What each agent computes is tested in its own directory, tests/agents/<AGENT>/: GAE on a known trajectory, a loss's sign, a target on a hand-built batch, and that every configuration value reaches the code that runs. That last kind exists because of a real bug: PPO once treated num_minibatches=32 as 1, and its CartPole smoke test still passed (tests/agents/PPO/test_PPO_code.py).

docs.title: Pins
docs.text: The pins are change detectors, not truth. test_agent_pins.py compares a fingerprint of a tiny run (the sum of squares of each parameter tree, and the state of a test extension) with the one recorded, under a relative tolerance that absorbs the floating-point drift between CI's Linux x86 and macOS ARM. A behaviour-neutral change that moves a pin only by that drift re-records it; a change that moves the numbers on purpose re-records it in its own commit, saying why. test_downstream_api.py pins the names and keywords the downstream projects import, so that removing one is a deliberate step (CLAUDE.md, rule 10).

docs.title: Conformance checks
docs.text:
A conformance check runs one training step of an Ajax agent and of its original implementation from the same state, with the same random numbers, and compares the change each makes to every leaf of the state: parameters, optimiser moments, and for PQN the collected rollout and its targets. The tolerance comes from rounding alone: each side's float32 run against the same run in float64, times 10 (tests/conformance/submaps.py). A planted fault, such as TD3's target noise at 0.22 instead of 0.2, must fail the check.

Agent Original Test PQN purejaxql (JAX) tests/conformance/test_pqn_purejaxql.py TD3 sfujim/TD3 (PyTorch) tests/conformance/test_td3_sfujim.py TD3+BC sfujim/TD3_BC (PyTorch) tests/conformance/test_td3bc_sfujim.py REDQ watchernyu/REDQ (PyTorch) tests/conformance/test_redq_original.py AVG gauthamvasan/avg (PyTorch) tests/conformance/test_avg_original.py

The originals are vendored under benchmarks/reference/vendor. A PyTorch original runs in its own environment (benchmarks/reference/envs/torch) and records its states to disk; CI keeps those records between runs while the original, its recorder and that environment's lock stay the same (AJAX_CONFORMANCE_RECORDS). tests/conformance/kit.py holds the seams that make one step comparable without changing the code under test: a tape of the random draws, and the capture of an agent's update. A difference that is the original's convention or defect is registered with its reason (benchmarks/reference/refcmp_specs.py) and asserted by a test of its own; PQN's also appear in the reproduction specifications.

docs.title: Running tests locally
docs.text:
The full suite costs about an hour of CPU, so CI runs it on the pull request. Before pushing, run the cheap checks (CLAUDE.md, "Commit requirement"):

uv run pre-commit run --all-files            # ruff lint, ruff-format, mypy
uv run pytest --collect-only -q              # everything imports and collects
uv run pytest tests/agents/TD3               # the tests of what you changed
uv run pytest tests/probing/test_framework.py  # any change under src/ajax
uv run pytest tests/probing -k TD3           # a change to TD3's training: all its probe cells

Two of these are process rules. A change under src/ajax runs tests/probing/test_framework.py, which trains nothing: every planted fault quotes a line of the source, so any source edit can break one. A change to an agent's training runs all of that agent's probe cells (-k <Agent> over tests/probing).

make ci runs everything CI runs (ci-precommit, ci-test, ci-slow, ci-probe, ci-conformance, and docs, the strict build of this site). The make targets hide the GPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="", JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu), so tests never compete with an experiment running on it. Outside make, set JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu while a GPU is busy.

pyproject.toml registers one marker, slow, and runs pytest with --strict-markers, so a misspelt marker is an error rather than a test that silently runs in the wrong job.

docs.title: How CI splits the suite
docs.text:
The tests come in two tiers. The fast tier is the tests not marked slow, which every pull request must pass. A fast test may train, but for at most 128 gradient steps and about 30 s; tests/conftest.py lists the tests past either limit at the end of a run, without failing them yet. The slow tier is every test that trains: tests/probing (marked slow as it is collected, but for the harness's own checks) and the tests marked slow elsewhere. Contributing describes both.

.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on CPU for every pull request and every push to main:

Job What it runs Pre-commit ruff lint, ruff-format and mypy on every file Tests (3 shards) the tests not marked slow, probing and conformance excluded, under coverage, a pytest-xdist worker per vCPU, at XLA optimisation level 0, on arm64 runners. Shards 1 and 2 name directories; shard 3 runs everything else, so a new test file always runs somewhere Coverage the three shards' data combined; fails below 70% Slow tests -m slow, probing excluded, without coverage (its tracing would lengthen them) Probing (5 shards) tests/probing, in five shards by recorded duration (--shard I/5, tests/.durations), without the families out of the gate (faults.OUT_OF_THE_GATE: test_p4_split_run.py and test_memory.py), which run only in the slow tier Conformance tests/conformance: one training step of each agent that has a check against its original implementation (above) Docs mkdocs build --strict with the docs group alone: a broken link, a page left out of the navigation or a docstring naming a parameter the signature lacks fails it Lint and Test passes only when every job above passed; the one check branch protection requires

The Slow tier workflow (slow.yml) runs the slow tier in six shards: daily on main when it changed, by hand, and on a pull request each time the label run-slow-tier is added. A red run on main opens an issue and, when that is cheap, bisects the merges since the last green run. The Release workflow tags a version only once the slow tier has passed on main's head.

The test, slow, probing and conformance jobs restore Ajax's compile cache as the last push to main left it for that job, so a program a change leaves alone is loaded instead of compiled. A new push to a pull request cancels the run it supersedes. Nothing merges while any job is red; a failure that is pre-existing and unrelated to the change is called out explicitly instead of merged over.

docs.title: The probing framework
docs.text:
A probe trains an agent on a tiny Markov decision process whose answer is known exactly (a value, a best action, a count) and compares what the agent learned with the right answer and with the answers that named bugs would produce. When it fails, it says which mistake the agent's reading is closest to.

The directory tests/probing holds:

File Role envs.py Spec: a small episodic environment from its transition function, with gymnax auto-reset, a time limit and, on request, a record of the executed actions agents.py each agent's frozen probe presets, pinned by DIGEST, and make, which checks every override reached the agent runs.py trains every seed of a case in one compiled program, and caches the readings so the tests of one case share its training readouts.py reads values and actions off a trained agent, through the same paths training uses oracles.py the right answers, and the wrong ones under named faults, from each estimator's fixed point or a closed form verdict.py Query, Case, the two-stage verdict, calibration and answer digests faults.py, faults/*.jsonl the planted-fault catalogue and its runner test_*.py the cases, grouped by subject (below); test_framework.py tests the harness itself Module What it probes test_value_chains.py values and actions on short chains: max bootstrap and action indexing, discounting, entropy bonuses, normalisation, gradients through a transition (APG) test_episode_ends.py terminations against time limits, rollout ends, parallel environments out of step, reward scale, average reward test_bookkeeping.py what an agent counts, logs, stores, draws and executes: step counters, UDRL's commands, an expert's warm-up, a declared action box test_extensions.py every extension phase an agent claims to fold, through test-only extensions of known effect; the expert extensions' numbers test_memory.py a recurrent agent acts on what an episode showed it and restarts at the episode's end test_world_models.py answers reachable only through a learned model (TD-MPC2's horizon, multi-task twins, DreamerV3's imagination) test_p4_split_run.py a run checkpointed, restored and resumed equals the run never interrupted test_action_box.py a trained policy's deterministic action at either edge of, and inside, a box that overhangs [-1, 1] unequally, in env units, against each agent family's oracle (no entropy term, an auto-tuned or a fixed temperature)

docs.title: Known-answer cases
docs.text:
A Query names one reading, its right answer and the wrong answers that named faults produce. A Case adds the readings function, the training budget and the calibrated tolerances. This one, from test_value_chains.py, is a two-step chain: state s1 pays 0, 0.5 or 1 by action, and Q(s0) = 0.8 max_a Q(s1, a):

# doc: skip (an excerpt of tests/probing/test_value_chains.py; it needs the test package)
R3, G3 = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0), 0.8  # s1's rewards by action; the discount
Q_S0_WRONG = {"mean bootstrap (D01)": G3 * 0.5, "no discount": 1.0}

CASES["p0a-DQN"] = Case(
    "p0a-DQN",
    (*Q_S1, *(Query(f"Q(s0, a={a})", G3, Q_S0_WRONG) for a in range(3)), GREEDY),
    _three_run("DQN"),  # train, then read Q at both states and the greedy action
    2500,  # budget, in environment steps
    (0.026, 0.021, 0.033, 0.037, 0.032, 0.029, 0.02),  # one tolerance per query
    note="1250 qualified but 2 seeds of 3000-3031 read Q(s0) 0.047 off; cert 32/32",
)

The tolerance can never reach a wrong answer: it is at most half the gap to the nearest one, and at most 0.1. So a reading within tolerance is closer to the truth than to any named bug. A margin query asks only for the right sign by a margin, for readings such as the gap between two actions' values.

Some cases are exact rather than judged. The bookkeeping and split-run probes assert equalities (a counter, a logged timestep, a whole state) on two seeds trained in one program.

docs.title: The two-stage seed rule
docs.text:
Learning is noisy, so a judged case trains several seeds and counts how many land within tolerance:

  1. Train seeds 0-7 in one program. Seven or more within tolerance: pass. Four or fewer: fail.
  2. Five or six: train seeds 8-15 as well, and pass when 13 of the 16 are within.

A clear result costs one training; only an ambiguous one pays for a second. A precondition (a reading of the wrong shape, an override that did not reach the agent) raises RuntimeError, never AssertionError, so a strict xfail cannot absorb it.

docs.title: Calibration and certification
docs.text:
A case's budget and tolerances are measured, never guessed, and on seeds no check uses:

  1. Ladder. Read two blocks of 32 seeds (1000-1031 and 2000-2031) untrained and at a series of budgets.
  2. Choose. Pool the blocks and take the smallest budget at which twice the worst seed's error fits under the cap (the smaller of 0.1 and half the gap to the nearest wrong answer); that doubled error, at least 0.02, becomes the tolerance. For a margin query, half the weakest seed's margin must reach 0.25.
  3. Certify. Check the chosen budget and tolerances on a third block, 3000-3031, and record the result in the case's note.
uv run python -m tests.probing.verdict ladder test_value_chains p0a-DQN 1000 1250,2500,5000 a.json
uv run python -m tests.probing.verdict ladder test_value_chains p0a-DQN 2000 1250,2500,5000 b.json
uv run python -m tests.probing.verdict choose test_value_chains p0a-DQN a.json b.json
uv run python -m tests.probing.verdict certify test_value_chains p0a-DQN   # seeds 3000-3031

test_framework.py checks that every calibrated tolerance lies inside its gap.

docs.title: Answer digests
docs.text:
A calibration holds only for the configuration and the answers it was made on. Two digests pin both:

  • agents.DIGEST hashes every agent's probe presets.
  • Each scenario module's ANSWER_DIGEST hashes every query's right answer, wrong answers, tolerance and kind, to six decimals.

test_presets_and_answers_are_pinned fails when either moves. Change a preset or an answer only together with a fresh calibration, then re-pin the digest. To see what a module's digest covers:

uv run python -m tests.probing.verdict answers test_value_chains

docs.title: Planted faults
docs.text:
A probe that has never caught a bug has not shown it can. Each scenario module has a catalogue, faults/<module>.jsonl, with one line per fault:

{"id": "P0a-D01-DQN", "path": "agents/DQN/train_DQN.py",
 "old": "    max_q_next = jnp.max(q_next, axis=-1, keepdims=True)\n",
 "new": "    max_q_next = jnp.mean(q_next, axis=-1, keepdims=True)\n",
 "catches": ["test_value_chains.py::test_learns[p0a-DQN]"]}

path is under src/ajax; old must occur exactly once; catches lists every test node that fails with the fault planted. The runner copies the repository to a scratch directory, plants the fault there (your checkout is never modified), checks that Python imports the copy, and runs the listed nodes with the compile cache off. A non-zero exit means caught:

JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu uv run python -m tests.probing.faults /tmp/faults P0a-D01-DQN P0a-gather-up
# {'P0a-D01-DQN': 'caught', 'P0a-gather-up': 'caught'}

CI does not plant faults; test_framework.py runs test_every_planted_fault_applies_once_and_names_live_nodes, which checks that each old text still occurs once and that each listed node still exists. This is why a change under src/ajax runs test_framework.py before the push: when a change moves the code a fault edits, update the fault's line and run it again. The catalogue holds 209 faults across eight modules.

docs.title: Known defects
docs.text: A probe that finds a live bug keeps failing, visibly. The case gets a defect, which turns it into a strict xfail whose reason names the defect (LIVE defect: ...). When the bug is fixed, the xfail passes, strict mode fails the suite, and the annotation has to be removed. A known bug is never hidden by loosening a tolerance.

docs.title: Size budgets
docs.text: The framework is meant to stay readable. test_framework.py caps each file's length (CAPS) and the whole directory at 7,000 lines, and requires at least one case for every agent ajax exports.

docs.title: The bugs the probes target
docs.text:
The catalogue reads as a list of the classic ways reinforcement-learning code goes wrong without crashing:

Bug Example faults The bootstrap averages instead of maximising; the taken action's value, or the greedy action, is read at the wrong index P0a-D01-DQN, P0a-gather-up, P0a-greedy-up The discount is squared, replaced by 1 - gamma, or dropped the value-chain cases: at the probe discount 0.62 those wrong answers sit about 0.24 or more from the right one A time limit is treated as a termination; the reset observation replaces the episode's final one; truncation is dropped P6-PPO-OR, P6-RESET-OBS, P6-GYMNAX-TRUNC-DROPPED The reward scale is applied twice P5-S13, P5-REDQ-scaled-twice GAE runs forwards in time; the value bootstraps on the wrong observation; the configured lambda is ignored Q9-GAE-FORWARD, P09, Q9-PQN-LAMBDA The entropy term has the wrong sign or is missing; the tanh log-probability misses its Jacobian, in the policy or in the target P07, S-entropy-sign, S-no-jacobian, S-pre-tanh-target The observation normaliser is skipped in the target or at evaluation P1-sac-target-skips-agent-norm, P1-eval-skips-agent-norm TD3's target policy noise is not clipped T02 Parallel environments share one random key; the step counter counts collection steps, not environment steps B02, P9-shared-step-keys, B01 Every seed gets the same key B11 A recurrent memory is never reset at an episode start, or reset every step; the burn-in is too short P0b-never-restart, P0b-reset-every-step, Q2-short-burn A resumed run loses its random key, optimiser state, counter or buffer P4-rng, P4-optimizer, P4-counter, P4-buffer An extension's term has no gradient, its target is ignored, or post_update runs before the update P3-ppo-critic-term-no-gradient, P3-dqn-target-ignored, P3-post-update-first Logs go to the wrong run; the last evaluation is dropped W01, L01 A planner forgets its terminal value; a world model ignores the action Q12-terminal, Q13-action-cut An action consumer clamps to the env's [-1, 1], or reads actions in the other units (env for agent, or the reverse) box-executed-clamped, box-replay-env-units, box-TDMPC2-plan-clamped

docs.title: Adding a probe
docs.text:
1. Pick the module by subject, and write the environment as an envs.Spec: a transition function returning the next state, the reward and the termination flag.
  2. Write the queries. Give each reading its exact right answer and the wrong answers the bugs you are after would produce. Choose the problem's numbers so the wrong answers sit well apart from the right one: the tolerance can be at most half that gap.
  3. Write the readings with runs.readings(build, read): build makes the agent with agents.make (its probe preset plus your overrides), and read applies readouts to the trained state.
  4. Calibrate and certify as above, and record the budget, the tolerances and the certification in the case's note.
  5. Re-pin the module's ANSWER_DIGEST (and agents.DIGEST if you changed a preset). The failing pin test shows the new value.
  6. Plant the faults. Add a line per bug to faults/<module>.jsonl, run them with the fault runner, and keep only lines it reports as caught. A fault that survives means the probe is weaker than you thought.
  7. Mind the caps. If a file outgrows its cap, shorten the code before raising the cap.

A new agent needs probe presets in agents.py and at least one case; a new probe file joins a probing shard without any workflow change (a test missing from tests/.durations counts one second).

docs.title: Writing an extension
docs.text: An extension is a research feature that plugs into an agent's training loop without changing the agent: an expert to learn from, an extra loss term, a change to the TD target, a measurement logged at each evaluation. This page explains the contract an extension follows and walks through examples that run. Extensions in the user guide lists the ones Ajax ships.

docs.title: The rule: a feature is an extension, not a keyword
docs.text:
An agent's constructor accepts its algorithm's own hyperparameters plus extensions=(), and nothing else. The documented exceptions are expert_policy (SAC, TD3, REDQ, AVG, APO), whose return each evaluation logs and which SAC also learns from; SAC's options that reach its network's input, its collection or its action pipeline, which extensions do not reach yet (SAC); and TD3's action_pipeline, kept for a downstream project. Do not add to them. If a new feature seems to need a keyword on an agent (use_critic_blend=True, an expert's weight), write an extension instead. The agent must not know that any particular extension exists, and must not hold any extension's hyperparameters.

The reason is maintenance. Each feature written into an agent grows that agent's file and couples it to one paper. SAC once grew to about a hundred constructor keywords that way, before those features moved into extensions; behaviour cloning was the last to move (CloningPretrain). Kept separate, an extension works with every agent that folds its phases, and an agent's file stays readable as its paper's pseudocode.

docs.title: The contract
docs.text:
An extension subclasses Extension and follows six rules.

  1. A frozen dataclass. Write it as @dataclass(frozen=True), with its settings as fields. Extensions are static arguments of the compiled program, so they must be hashable and must never change. Two extensions with equal fields hash equal; an equivalent run on a new agent traces the same program again, which the persistent compile cache then loads instead of compiling (unless the run logs).
  2. State lives in the agent state. Anything that changes during training is a pytree returned by init_state and stored in agent_state.ext_state, one entry per extension. Never store it on self.
  3. Override only what you need. Every phase has a default that changes nothing (the identity, 0.0, {}, None). An extension is exactly as invasive as the phases it overrides, and an agent without extensions traces nothing extra.
  4. Self-contained. The agent passes context in; the extension decides what to do with it. When the extension needs something the agent builds (its replay buffer, its discount), it takes it through bind_to_agent, not through a new agent keyword.
  5. Raise on a missing operand. When a phase needs a batch key, or a value the agent should have bound, and does not get it, it raises a ValueError naming what is missing. It never returns its input or 0.0 instead: that would let an agent that does not pass the key silence the extension for a whole run.
  6. Declare what you read beyond the batch. A replay field the agent stores only on request, an expert, the frozen expert critic phi*: each has a class attribute or method (below), and the agent checks them when it is built.

docs.title: The phases
docs.text:
An agent folds its ExtensionStack through each phase in the order the extensions were given.

Phase Returns How several extensions combine Folded by init_state(agent_state, rng) the extension's state ((): none) one entry each every agent, fresh runs only pretrain(agent_state, ext_state, ctx) (agent_state, ext_state) in order, each sees the last one's agent state every agent, fresh runs only reward(agent_state, ext_state, batch, rewards, ctx) (rewards, ext_state, metrics): the rollout's new rewards in order, each transforms the last one's rewards PPO, after each rollout, before its targets on_target(agent_state, ext_state, batch, target, ctx) the new target, or (target, metrics) (below) in order, each transforms the last one's target SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, DQN, PQN, PPO, APO critic_loss(agent_state, ext_state, batch, ctx) a term added to the critic loss, or (term, metrics) summed SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, DQN, PQN, PPO, APO actor_loss(agent_state, ext_state, batch, ctx) a term added to the actor loss, or (term, metrics) summed SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, PPO, APO, APG, UDRL action(agent_state, ext_state, obs, rng, ctx) an action, or None to defer the last non-None wins SAC with an expert policy (below) eval_action(agent_state, ext_state, obs, rng, ctx) an action, or None the last non-None wins no agent yet transform_action(actions, a_expert) the executed action, from the policy's and the expert's the first one acts SAC with an expert policy, in collection, its losses and evaluation post_update(agent_state, ext_state, ctx) (agent_state, ext_state) in order every agent, after each update eval_metrics(agent_state, ext_state, rng, ctx) a dict of metrics merged every agent, at each evaluation

Each phase the stack folds is one ExtensionStack method, fold_<phase> (fold_init runs init_state then pretrain), and an agent calls it once where the phase applies; SAC's action pipeline dispatches action and transform_action itself. Each agent lists the phases it folds in supported_extension_phases. An extension implementing any other phase is rejected when the agent is built, instead of being silently ignored. DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and its multi-task variant fold only the loop's phases (pretrain, post_update, eval_metrics).

init_state and pretrain run on a fresh run only. A resumed run's state already carries the extension's state and whatever pretraining produced.

docs.title: Logging what a phase computes
docs.text:
on_target, critic_loss and actor_loss may return (value, metrics) instead of their value: metrics is a dict of scalars named <extension>/<metric>, logged at each evaluation with the agent's own training metrics, and like them the last update's or, for PPO, APO, PQN and UDRL, the mean over the update's epochs, minibatches or steps. They are not differentiated: the agent returns them beside its loss, as it returns its own metrics. Returning the value alone logs nothing. Two extensions logging the same name raise when the agent is traced.

def on_target(self, agent_state, ext_state, batch, target, ctx):
    wins = ...  # where the expert's next action scores higher
    return jnp.where(wins, expert_target, target), {"ibrl/expert_wins": wins.mean()}

eval_metrics stays the place for what can be read off the agent state at an evaluation (a schedule, a counter kept in the extension's state).

docs.title: What a phase receives
docs.text:
ctx is an ExtensionContext:

  • ctx.step: the collector's timestep, traced. Use it in jnp.where, not in a Python if.
  • ctx.rng: a key for this call.
  • ctx.total_steps: the run's horizon, a plain Python int. Python-level decisions (a schedule's length) can use it at trace time. On a resumed run it is the whole run's horizon, so schedules continue rather than restart.

batch is a dictionary. PHASE_BATCH_KEYS in extensions/base.py lists the keys each agent puts in it, and tests/extensions/test_phase_contract.py checks every agent against that list:

Phase Agents Keys reward PPO observations, raw_observations, actions (the rollout's) on_target every agent folding it observations, next_observations, rewards, gamma SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, DQN, PQN actions, dones, reward_scale PQN, PPO, APO terminated, truncated PPO, APO gae, values critic_loss every agent folding it observations, targets SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, PPO, APO critic_params, critic_state SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, DQN, PQN actions DQN, PQN q_state actor_loss every agent folding it actor_params SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, PPO, APO, UDRL, APG actor_state, observations, raw_observations, pi_mean SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, APO a_expert SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG critic_state UDRL actions APG rollout, returns

What the keys mean: gamma is None for the average-reward agents, ASAC and APO. dones marks where the target cut the bootstrap. targets is the target on_target returned, held constant. The critic and actor parameters (critic_params, q_state, actor_params) are the ones being differentiated. raw_observations is None in a replay agent's run without an expert, whose replay does not keep them. An agent may add keys of its own (SAC's on_target batch carries rng_key, the target's own key); read its fold call in train_<AGENT>.py before relying on one.

docs.title: A worked example
docs.text:
This extension clips the TD target to [low, high] for the first part of the run, then lets it go. It counts the updates it was active for and logs the count at each evaluation. It touches four phases: init_state for its counter, on_target for the clip, post_update to count, and eval_metrics to report.

from dataclasses import dataclass

import jax.numpy as jnp

from ajax import TD3
from ajax.extensions import Extension
from ajax.logging.wandb_logging import LoggingConfig


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClippedTarget(Extension):
    """Clips the TD target to [low, high] for the first `fraction` of the
    run, and counts the updates it was active for."""

    low: float
    high: float
    fraction: float = 0.5
    name: str = "clipped-target"

    def active(self, ctx):
        # ctx.step is traced (the collector's timestep); ctx.total_steps
        # is a plain int, the run's horizon.
        return ctx.step < self.fraction * ctx.total_steps

    def init_state(self, agent_state, rng):
        return jnp.asarray(0, jnp.int32)

    def on_target(self, agent_state, ext_state, batch, target, ctx):
        clipped = jnp.clip(target, self.low, self.high)
        return jnp.where(self.active(ctx), clipped, target)

    def post_update(self, agent_state, ext_state, ctx):
        return agent_state, ext_state + self.active(ctx).astype(jnp.int32)

    def eval_metrics(self, agent_state, ext_state, rng, ctx):
        # A float: between evaluations the logger fills metrics with NaN.
        return {"ClippedTarget/active updates": ext_state.astype(jnp.float32)}


agent = TD3(
    "Pendulum-v1",
    learning_starts=200,
    extensions=(ClippedTarget(low=-50.0, high=0.0),),
)
logging = LoggingConfig(config={}, log_frequency=500, use_wandb=False)
state, evaluations = agent.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=2000, logging_config=logging)
print(state.ext_state[0])                              # [800 800]
print(evaluations["ClippedTarget/active updates"])     # [[301. 800. 800. 800.] ...]

Reading it part by part:

  • Fields. low, high and fraction are the extension's settings. name labels it in error messages. The dataclass is frozen, so the agent can pass it to jax.jit as a static argument.
  • State. init_state returns the counter. The agent stores it at state.ext_state[0], the first extension's slot, with a leading seed axis like every other leaf. That is why print(state.ext_state[0]) shows one count per seed.
  • on_target receives the target the agent computed and returns a new one. It must not change the agent state or its own state; the phases that can (pretrain, post_update) return both. On the replay agents the result is held constant (stop_gradient) before the critic regresses on it.
  • post_update runs after every update. Updates start at learning_starts (timestep 200) and the clip is active while the timestep is below 1,000, so each seed counts the 800 updates from timestep 200 to
  • The first evaluation, at timestep 500, reads 301.
  • eval_metrics adds a key to every evaluation. With a LoggingConfig, train returns it per seed and per evaluation, and W&B or TensorBoard record it when one is enabled.

docs.title: Reading the batch, and raising when a key is missing
docs.text:
A phase that reads the batch takes what it needs and raises when it is not there. This critic-loss term is an L2 penalty on the critic's parameters, as DDPG put on its critic (Lillicrap et al., 2016). It reads critic_params, which the actor-critic agents pass; DQN and PQN pass their Q-network as q_state instead, so on them it raises when training traces the fold:

from dataclasses import dataclass

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

from ajax import DQN, TD3
from ajax.extensions import Extension


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CriticWeightDecay(Extension):
    """coef * the sum of the critic's squared parameters, added to its loss."""

    coef: float = 1e-4
    name: str = "critic-weight-decay"

    def critic_loss(self, agent_state, ext_state, batch, ctx):
        params = batch.get("critic_params")
        if params is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "CriticWeightDecay needs the differentiated critic parameters"
                " ('critic_params') in the critic-loss batch; DQN and PQN pass"
                " their Q-network as 'q_state' instead."
            )
        return self.coef * sum(jnp.sum(jnp.square(p)) for p in jax.tree.leaves(params))


TD3("Pendulum-v1", learning_starts=200, extensions=(CriticWeightDecay(),)).train(
    seed=0, n_timesteps=400
)  # trains, with the term in its critic loss

try:
    DQN("CartPole-v1", learning_starts=200, extensions=(CriticWeightDecay(),)).train(
        seed=0, n_timesteps=400
    )
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)  # CriticWeightDecay needs the differentiated critic parameters ...

DQN folds critic_loss, so it accepts the extension at construction; the missing key shows when the fold is traced. Every shipped extension implementing on_target, critic_loss or actor_loss is checked to raise on an empty batch (tests/extensions/test_no_silent_noop.py).

docs.title: What an extension declares
docs.text:
An extension says what it needs with class attributes and methods the agent checks at construction, against what its algorithm has (capabilities) and what its code passes on (the phases it folds, the context it binds, its batches and replay fields; ajax.extensions.capabilities):

Declaration What it says What the agent does requires (class attribute, a frozenset) and needs() the capabilities it needs beyond those its phases imply (on_target, critic_loss: critic; actor_loss: actor; action: off_policy; transform_action: continuous_actions) refuses it when its run lacks one (MissingCapability, naming each); needs() returns them all and may depend on the extension's options provides (class attribute) the capabilities it gives its stack adds them to the run's: MCPretrain provides phi_star, which its readers require context (class attribute) the agent-context keys it cannot work without refuses it when its extension_context, the keys its make_train binds, lacks one (NotWired) pretrain_context (class attribute) the ExtensionContext fields its pretrain reads (env_args, update, buffer) refuses it when its loop does not fill one: its pretrain_context (NotWired) batch_keys (class attribute) and reads() per phase, the batch keys it reads beyond those every agent folding the phase passes refuses it when PHASE_BATCH_KEYS lists none of them for the agent (NotWired) buffer_fields (class attribute, a frozenset) replay fields beyond the agent's own that the extension reads, such as raw_next_obs, the environment's own next observation stores them only when an extension declares them; rejects the ones it cannot store (SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC and AVG store raw_next_obs) expert_fields (class attribute) and experts() the fields holding an expert, written in env units, and the experts the extension calls itself reads every expert in expert_fields in agent units (ExtensionStack.with_experts); keeps the raw observations and expert flags in replay for a run with an expert; refuses a stateful expert (one with init_state) that experts() would call without its state reads_agent_expert_actions (class attribute) the extension reads the expert actions the agent stored, when its expert is the agent's expert_policy lets a stateful expert through for it, on an agent that stores those actions (stores_expert_actions: SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC, AVG, APO) reads_step_in_episode (class attribute) the extension reads each env's step within its episode SAC counts it only then (JSRLCurriculum reads it) action_slot (class attribute) where in SAC's action pipeline an action override applies: "pre_warmup" or "post_warmup" SAC dispatches action only to extensions with a slot, and only with an expert_policy

EDGEExploration does not require phi_star: it reads phi* when MCPretrain ran and the live critic otherwise. Its value gates require a Q critic (its needs() depends on its gate).

These checks run when the agent is built:

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar

from ajax import PQN, SAC, TD3
from ajax.extensions import Extension


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ActorNudge(Extension):
    """A term on the actor's loss (a stand-in: it adds nothing)."""

    name: str = "actor-nudge"

    def actor_loss(self, agent_state, ext_state, batch, ctx):
        return 0.0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NextObservationReader(Extension):
    """Reads the environment's own next observation from replay."""

    name: str = "next-observation-reader"
    buffer_fields: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"raw_next_obs"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PhiStarReader(Extension):
    """Reads the frozen expert critic phi*, which only MCPretrain fits."""

    name: str = "phi-star-reader"
    requires: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"phi_star"})


for build in (
    lambda: PQN("CartPole-v1", extensions=(ActorNudge(),)),  # PQN has no actor
    lambda: TD3("Pendulum-v1", extensions=(NextObservationReader(),)),  # SAC stores it
    lambda: SAC("Pendulum-v1", extensions=(PhiStarReader(),)),  # no MCPretrain
):
    try:
        build()
    except ValueError as error:
        print(error)
# PQN cannot run ActorNudge ('actor-nudge'), which needs actor (a policy network trained by gradient).
# TD3 has what its extensions need, but does not pass it on yet: NextObservationReader ('next-observation-reader'): TD3 stores no ['raw_next_obs'] yet.
# SAC cannot run PhiStarReader ('phi-star-reader'), which needs phi_star (add MCPretrain(expert_policy=...), which fits phi*, to the extensions).

If the agent you target does not fold a phase you need, adding the fold to that agent is a change of its own, made in the agent's update, and the agent still must not know about your extension. One more limit: SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC and PPO built with memory= reject every extension when training starts; APG takes both.

docs.title: Taking context from the agent: bind_to_agent
docs.text:
Some extensions need what the agent builds: its environment, optimiser, replay buffer or discount. The agent hands this context to every extension through ExtensionStack.bind_to_agent(**context). Each extension's bind_to_agent returns a new frozen instance holding what it needs and ignores the rest. The default returns the extension unchanged.

import dataclasses
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

import jax.numpy as jnp

from ajax import SAC
from ajax.extensions import Extension
from ajax.logging.wandb_logging import LoggingConfig


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EffectiveHorizon(Extension):
    """Logs 1 / (1 - gamma), the agent's effective planning horizon."""

    gamma: Optional[float] = None  # filled by bind_to_agent unless given
    name: str = "effective-horizon"

    def bind_to_agent(self, **agent_context):
        gamma = agent_context.get("gamma")
        if self.gamma is not None or gamma is None:
            return self  # a value the user passed wins
        return dataclasses.replace(self, gamma=gamma)

    def eval_metrics(self, agent_state, ext_state, rng, ctx):
        if self.gamma is None:
            raise ValueError("EffectiveHorizon needs gamma: pass it, or use an agent that binds it")
        return {"Debug/effective horizon": jnp.asarray(1.0 / (1.0 - self.gamma))}


agent = SAC("Pendulum-v1", gamma=0.95, learning_starts=200, extensions=(EffectiveHorizon(),))
logging = LoggingConfig(config={}, log_frequency=500, use_wandb=False)
_, evaluations = agent.train(seed=0, n_timesteps=1000, logging_config=logging)
print(evaluations["Debug/effective horizon"])  # [[20. 20.]]

Five agents call bind_to_agent, when training starts:

  • SAC passes env_args, actor_optimizer_args, network_args, critic_optimizer_args, num_critics, buffer, gamma, reward_scale, use_train_frac, augment_obs_with_expert_action, augment_obs_with_expert_state, expert_state_aug_dim, extensions (the whole stack), expert_policy, recurrent, update_value_fn and update_target_fn.
  • TD3, REDQ and APO pass env_args, actor_optimizer_args and expert_policy, which CloningPretrain needs.
  • DreamerV3 passes env_args, agent_config, gamma and total_timesteps.

Follow the shipped extensions' pattern. Keep a value the user passed explicitly, as MCPretrain and PhiRefresh do. And raise with a clear message when the context you need is missing, as PhiRefresh and CloningPretrain do on an agent that did not bind it, rather than running with None. On an agent that binds nothing, EffectiveHorizon above raises the same way.

docs.title: Randomness
docs.text:
init_state and eval_metrics give each extension a key of its own, the rng argument. The other phases pass one ctx to every extension of the stack, so two extensions drawing from ctx.rng in the same phase draw the same numbers: split it with a constant of your own (jax.random.fold_in) when that matters. SAC's action pipeline passes the same key as rng to every action extension too.

Each fold's key is one no other fold gets and one the agent draws nothing else on (tests/extensions/test_phase_contract.py checks both on every agent). When you add a fold to an agent, take its key as an extra entry of a split the agent already makes: key, rng, ext_key = jax.random.split(k, 3) where the agent used key, rng = jax.random.split(k). Under JAX's default partitionable threefry the first two keys are unchanged, so the agent's own random stream stays the same with or without extensions.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A loss term needs the differentiated parameters. critic_loss and actor_loss run inside the agent's value_and_grad. A term computed from agent_state.critic_state.params has no gradient. Use the parameters the batch passes (critic_params, actor_params, or q_state for DQN and PQN). The probes plant this exact mistake and catch it, and the phase contract checks that a term moves the network it names, and only that one.
  • Integer metrics. Between evaluations the logger fills eval_metrics with NaN of the metric's dtype. An integer cannot hold NaN: it becomes 0, which reads as a real value. Return floats.
  • State on self. A Python attribute is read once, when the program is traced, and never again. Whatever must change during training belongs in init_state's pytree.
  • on_target cannot pass a gradient. The target is held constant. To change what the critic learns through a gradient, use critic_loss.
  • Shapes. A replay agent's target has a batch axis; a rollout agent's has time and environment axes. Read the shapes from the agent's fold call, or stay shape-agnostic as ClippedTarget does.

docs.title: Shipping it
docs.text:
1. Put the class in src/ajax/extensions/<topic>.py, next to related ones: expert.py (learning from an expert), exploration.py, target_mods.py (target modifiers), pretrain.py, instrumentation.py (measurements), ensemble.py. ensemble.py's KernelRepulsion, a single critic_loss term with its paper's citation, is a good model.
  2. Test it in tests/extensions/: the feature does what its paper says (a metric meets its closed form, a term moves the loss the right way, a target shifts by the expected amount on a hand-built batch).
  3. Give it the rows the generic tests ask for, which fail until it has them: a builder in EXTENSIONS of tests/agents/test_option_smoke.py (every extension of ajax.extensions is stacked into an agent that folds it and trained briefly), and, if it implements on_target, critic_loss or actor_loss, a row in BUILD of tests/extensions/test_no_silent_noop.py.
  4. If it adds a learning behaviour, add a probe case in tests/probing/test_extensions.py and plant the faults it should catch (see Testing).
  5. Document it in the user guide's Extensions page, with the paper it comes from.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Ajax is on PyPI as ajax-rl and imports as ajax. It needs Python 3.12 or newer.

pip install ajax-rl

Brax and MuJoCo Playground environments need an extra: "ajax-rl[playground]" installs both, "ajax-rl[brax]" Brax alone. pip installs main from the repository:

pip install "ajax-rl @ git+https://github.com/YannBerthelot/Ajax.git"

pip does not read uv.lock, so it takes the newest versions that pyproject.toml allows. A weekly CI job tests those too, and another the oldest versions allowed (Dependencies and releases).

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
uv installs Ajax from source:

git clone https://github.com/YannBerthelot/Ajax.git
cd Ajax
uv sync

uv sync creates .venv with the versions in uv.lock, which CI tests. Prefix commands with uv run, or activate the environment with source .venv/bin/activate. To check the install:

uv run python -c "import ajax; print(ajax.__version__)"

docs.title: CPU or GPU
docs.text:
Ajax installs JAX for the CPU. CUDA comes only from its cuda extra (Linux only); without it, JAX runs on the CPU even on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU. To use the GPU:

uv sync --extra cuda

A project that depends on Ajax asks for ajax-rl[cuda] instead.

To keep a run on the CPU on a machine with a GPU, set JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu. The repository's make targets go further and hide the GPU from CUDA as well, so tests never compete with an experiment running on it:

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu uv run python my_script.py

Performance says when each device pays off.

docs.title: Dependency groups
docs.text:
uv sync installs the runtime and two groups by default. The others are opt-in.

Group Default What it adds dev yes pytest, coverage, pre-commit, ruff, mypy, the probing environments the tests train on, and the playground extra wandb yes the wandb extra (below) plane no TargetGym, for the Plane3DCircle scenario of the speed benchmark (benchmarks/perf_bench.py) docs no MkDocs and its plugins, to build this site 
uv sync --group plane         # add an opt-in group
uv sync --no-default-groups   # the runtime alone

The docs group builds the site without the runtime (uv sync --only-group docs): the API pages are read from the source, not imported.

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
Extra What it adds cuda JAX with CUDA, on Linux (above) brax Brax, for Brax environments such as "ant" playground MuJoCo Playground and Brax, for Playground environments such as "CartpoleBalance" compare the adastop package, whose confidence sequence ajax.compare.estimate uses; AdaStop itself needs no extra reproduction Hugging Face Hub, pandas and pyarrow, for ajax.reproduction.load (Reproduction) wandb Weights & Biases, for logging with use_wandb=True; the default wandb group installs it 
uv sync --extra compare

Brax and MuJoCo Playground come only with their extras: a project that uses their environments asks for ajax-rl[playground], or ajax-rl[brax] for Brax alone. Without them, building a Brax or Playground environment raises an error that names the extra. The dev group installs both, so uv sync in this repository has them.

The compare extra takes adastop from a commit of its main branch, named in [tool.uv.sources], until a release includes the confidence sequence. pip does not read that table: with pip, install adastop from that commit yourself.

docs.title: Using Ajax from another project
docs.text:
Ajax and every runtime dependency, gymnax 1.0.1 included, come from PyPI:

[project]
dependencies = ["ajax-rl"]  # "ajax-rl[cuda]" for CUDA, "ajax-rl[playground]" for Brax and Playground envs

[tool.uv.sources]
ajax-rl = { git = "https://github.com/YannBerthelot/Ajax.git" }  # optional: main instead of a release

A project that declared ajax from git or a path renames it ajax-rl; the import stays import ajax.

uv resolves that project's own versions within Ajax's bounds, not those of Ajax's uv.lock.

docs.title: The compile cache
docs.text:
import ajax turns on JAX's persistent compile cache, in ~/.cache/ajax/jax_compile_cache. A second process that runs the same program loads it from disk instead of compiling it again. Two environment variables control it:

Variable Effect AJAX_JAX_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR puts the cache somewhere else AJAX_NO_COMPILE_CACHE=1 turns the cache off and leaves the disk untouched

Performance explains what it saves and when it does not apply.

docs.title: Weights & Biases
docs.text: A LoggingConfig logs to Weights & Biases unless you pass use_wandb=False. Log in once with uv run wandb login before the first run that uses it. Runs that keep their results in memory, as in the quickstart, need no account.

docs.title: Working on Ajax
docs.text: After uv sync, run uv run pre-commit install once, so ruff and mypy check every commit. make docs builds this site as CI does (uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict: a broken link or a docstring naming a parameter the code does not have fails it), and make docs-serve serves it at http://127.0.0.1:8000, rebuilt on save. Contributing covers the rest.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page trains an agent, reads its results, runs the trained policy and saves it. Each example runs on a laptop CPU in under a minute, compilation included.

docs.title: Train an agent
docs.text:
An agent takes an environment id and its hyperparameters; train runs it. Here PPO learns CartPole with three seeds at once:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from ajax import PPO
from ajax.logging.wandb_logging import LoggingConfig

agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_envs=8, n_steps=128)  # 1,024 steps per rollout
# Evaluate every 4,096 steps; use_wandb=False keeps the results in memory only.
logging = LoggingConfig(config={}, log_frequency=4_096, use_wandb=False)
state, evaluations = agent.train(
    seed=[1, 2, 3], n_timesteps=32_768, logging_config=logging
)

steps = evaluations["timestep"][0]  # [ 4096  8192 ... 32768]
returns = evaluations["Eval/episodic mean reward"]  # shape (3, 8): seeds x evaluations
print(returns.mean(axis=0))

plt.plot(steps, returns.mean(axis=0))
plt.fill_between(steps, returns.min(axis=0), returns.max(axis=0), alpha=0.3)
plt.xlabel("environment steps")
plt.ylabel("evaluation return")
plt.savefig("cartpole.png")

What happened:

  • PPO("CartPole-v1", ...) looked the id up in gymnax and built 8 copies of the environment, which step in parallel inside each seed.
  • train compiled the whole run, environment included, into one program and ran the three seeds side by side with jax.vmap.
  • Every 4,096 steps it evaluated the policy on 10 test episodes (num_episode_test) and stored the mean return.

evaluations maps every logged name to an array with one row per seed and one column per evaluation. Without a logging_config, train does not evaluate at all and returns (state, None). Training an agent has the details.

docs.title: Continuous actions
docs.text:
The same pattern works for every agent. SAC on Pendulum:

from ajax import SAC
from ajax.logging.wandb_logging import LoggingConfig

# SAC waits learning_starts steps (10,000 by default) before its first update;
# this short demonstration starts after 1,000.
agent = SAC("Pendulum-v1", learning_starts=1_000)
logging = LoggingConfig(config={}, log_frequency=1_000, use_wandb=False)
state, evaluations = agent.train(seed=[1, 2], n_timesteps=3_000, logging_config=logging)
print(evaluations["Eval/episodic mean reward"])

Three thousand steps show the mechanics, not a trained pendulum: give SAC tens of thousands of steps for that. The algorithm pages help pick an agent and list each one's defaults.

docs.title: Use the trained policy
docs.text:
Every array in state has a seed axis first. Take one seed's actor and ask it for actions:

import gymnax
import jax

from ajax import PPO
from ajax.environments.interaction import get_pi

agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_envs=8, n_steps=128)
state, _ = agent.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=16_384)

actor = jax.tree.map(lambda x: x[0], state.actor_state)  # seed 0

env, params = gymnax.make("CartPole-v1")
key = jax.random.PRNGKey(0)
obs, env_state = env.reset(key, params)
episode_return, done = 0.0, False
while not done:
    pi, _ = get_pi(actor, actor.params, obs[None])  # a batch of one observation
    action = pi.mode()[0]  # the most likely action
    key, step_key = jax.random.split(key)
    obs, env_state, reward, terminated, truncated, _ = env.step(
        step_key, env_state, action, params
    )
    episode_return += float(reward)
    done = bool(terminated or truncated)
print(episode_return)

get_pi returns the policy's action distribution. It applies the agent's own observation normalisation when the agent keeps one (a replay agent's normalize_observations=True). If you trained an agent that normalises in the environment (PPO, APO, PQN, UDRL), normalise the observation the same way first: see Environments.

For continuous actions, take pi.mean() instead of pi.mode(). It is in the agent's units, [-1, 1]: map it onto the environment's bounds before stepping, as training and evaluation do, with agent_action_to_env(pi.mean(), env, params)[0] from ajax.environments.utils (Pendulum's torque spans [-2, 2]).

docs.title: Save and resume
docs.text:
save_checkpoint writes a state to disk. restore_into loads it into the state of a fresh agent, which train then continues:

import os
import tempfile

from ajax import PPO
from ajax.checkpoint import restore_into, save_checkpoint

seeds = [0, 1]
agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_envs=8, n_steps=128)
state, _ = agent.train(seed=seeds, n_timesteps=8_192)
path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "ppo_cartpole.pkl")
save_checkpoint(state, path)

# Later, in another process: the same agent, and a 0-step run as the skeleton.
agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_envs=8, n_steps=128)
skeleton, _ = agent.train(seed=seeds, n_timesteps=0)
state = restore_into(skeleton, path)
state, _ = agent.train(seed=seeds, n_timesteps=8_192, initial_state=state)
print(state.collector_state.timestep)  # [18432 18432]: PPO adds a rollout per call

Checkpoints and resuming explains what a resume keeps.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Environments: gymnax, Brax and MuJoCo Playground ids, your own environments, normalisation and time limits.
  • Networks and the PID policy: layer sizes, activations, encoders, and a policy that is a PID controller.
  • Memory: GRU, LSTM, transformer and Mamba blocks for partially observed tasks.
  • Extensions: learn from an expert, change the critic's target, measure the critic.
  • Logging: Weights & Biases and TensorBoard.

docs.title: Why Ajax
docs.text:
Stable-Baselines3 (SB3) is a PyTorch library of reinforcement-learning agents, with more agents in sb3-contrib. SBX is its JAX version. PureJaxRL is a set of single-file JAX implementations. Ajax is built around four things:

  1. End to end on the accelerator: the environment and the training loop compile into one JAX program, as in PureJaxRL and the other end-to-end JAX libraries.
  2. Average-reward agents: ASAC and APO, for tasks that never end.
  3. Expert-guided agents: agents that learn from a controller you already have.
  4. World models: DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2, in the same compiled program as the environment.

This page shows each one, compares the libraries and says when another library fits better. The examples run on a laptop CPU in under a minute each, except the world-model one.

docs.title: End to end on the accelerator
docs.text:
train compiles the whole run into one JAX program: the environment's steps, the replay buffer or rollout, the updates and the evaluations. The seeds run side by side in that same program, through jax.vmap. The loop does not come back to Python between two steps, so the program can run on a GPU the way it runs on a CPU, without a round trip to the host at each step. This is PureJaxRL's approach, and every Ajax agent trains this way except TDMPC2MultiTask, which learns offline from a dataset and evaluates its tasks from Python between compiled chunks of updates. It needs an environment written in JAX: gymnax, Brax, MuJoCo Playground or TargetGym. Logging and the critic pre-training extensions do call back to the host, to hand over their records or print progress.

import jax

from ajax import PPO

print(jax.default_backend())  # "cpu" here; "gpu" when JAX finds one
# 8 seeds, each with 8 copies of CartPole, compiled and run as one program.
agent = PPO("CartPole-v1", n_envs=8, n_steps=128)
state, _ = agent.train(seed=list(range(8)), n_timesteps=16_384)
print(state.collector_state.timestep)  # one count per seed

The same script runs on a GPU when JAX is installed with CUDA support and finds one (Installation). This section describes how the program is built, not a measured gain: Ajax's tests and per-agent benchmark run on the CPU, and no measurement compares a run on a GPU with the same run on a CPU. Performance has the costs that were measured: compilation, seeds, each agent's speed on a CPU.

docs.title: Average-reward agents
docs.text:
Most agents maximise a discounted return: a reward k steps ahead counts gamma**k times as much as one now. For a task that never ends, such as holding a setpoint or running a plant, the discount is not part of the problem; it only shortens how far ahead the agent looks. An average-reward agent maximises the reward per step over the long run instead, and has no discount factor. Ajax has two, each following its paper: ASAC (Adamczyk et al., 2025), SAC for this criterion, and APO (Ma et al., 2021), PPO for it. Each keeps its estimate of the reward per step on the state.

from ajax import APO, ASAC

# On-policy: PPO's clipped update on the reward minus the reward per step.
apo = APO("Pendulum-v1", n_envs=4, n_steps=256)
state, _ = apo.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=4_096)
print(state.average_reward)  # one estimate per seed

# Off-policy: soft actor-critic on the same criterion.
asac = ASAC("Pendulum-v1", learning_starts=1_000)
state, _ = asac.train(seed=[0, 1], n_timesteps=2_000)
print(state.theta)  # its reward-rate estimate, entropy term included

These budgets show the calls; Pendulum needs far more steps to be solved.

docs.title: Expert-guided agents
docs.text:
Often a controller already exists for the task: a tuned PID, a model predictive controller, an earlier policy. In Ajax an expert is a JAX function from observations to actions (or a stateful one, such as a PID carrying its integral, which gets its state back at every step), and an agent can learn from it instead of starting from scratch. The expert reads the environment's raw observations and answers in the environment's action units; the agent converts its answers to its own units, [-1, 1].

SAC uses it the most: it fills the replay buffer with the expert's experience, lets the expert act during warm-up, and takes the expert extensions: online behaviour cloning, residual policies, JSRL hand-over, IBRL targets and EDGE exploration, among others. SAC, TD3, REDQ and APO can clone the expert before training (CloningPretrain), and SAC, TD3, REDQ, ASAC and APO can add an imitation term to the actor's loss (ImitationLoss). SAC, TD3, REDQ, APO and AVG, given expert_policy=, also log the expert's own return at each evaluation, so the curves show whether the agent has overtaken it. Expert guidance covers every option.

import jax.numpy as jnp

from ajax import SAC, TD3
from ajax.extensions.expert import ImitationLoss
from ajax.extensions.pretrain import CloningPretrain
from ajax.logging.wandb_logging import LoggingConfig


def pd_expert(obs):
    """A PD controller on Pendulum's raw observation [cos θ, sin θ, θ̇],
    answering a torque in the environment's units, [-2, 2]."""
    theta = jnp.arctan2(obs[..., 1], obs[..., 0])
    return jnp.clip(-(2.0 * theta + 0.5 * obs[..., 2]), -2.0, 2.0)[..., None]


# SAC writes 1,000 expert steps to its replay buffer before training.
sac = SAC("Pendulum-v1", expert_policy=pd_expert, expert_buffer_n_steps=1_000,
          learning_starts=1_000)
logging = LoggingConfig(config={}, log_frequency=1_000, use_wandb=False)
state, evaluations = sac.train(seed=0, n_timesteps=2_000, logging_config=logging)
print(evaluations["Eval/expert bias"])  # the agent's return minus the expert's

# TD3 clones the expert on 1,000 of its steps before training, then keeps
# pulling its actor towards the expert's actions with an extra loss term.
td3 = TD3("Pendulum-v1", learning_starts=1_000, extensions=(
    CloningPretrain(pd_expert, n_steps=1_000, epochs=2),
    ImitationLoss(pd_expert),
))
state, _ = td3.train(seed=0, n_timesteps=2_000)

docs.title: World models
docs.text:
A world-model agent learns a model of the environment, a network that predicts what happens next and what reward follows, and uses it to act. DreamerV3 learns its policy inside the model, from imagined trajectories; TD-MPC2 plans with the model at every step; TDMPC2MultiTask trains one model offline on the data of several tasks. Each follows the code that produced its paper's results: the deviations register lists where Ajax departs from it, and tests compare Ajax's components with it. DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 run in one compiled program with the environment, like the other agents; TDMPC2MultiTask steps no environment while it trains. World models explains them in plain words.

# doc: skip (about half a minute on a laptop CPU, compilation included)
from ajax import DreamerV3

# The smallest model and a low train ratio, for a first look on a CPU.
agent = DreamerV3("CartPole-v1", model_size="1m", n_envs=4, train_ratio=32,
                  batch_size=4, batch_length=16)
state, _ = agent.train(seed=0, n_timesteps=1_000)

Both agents are much heavier than the model-free ones: use a GPU for anything beyond a check.
