the offline trainer evaluates after its first update, then every eval_freq Offline-trainer protocol (eval_mode, 10 episodes per task, t0 at each episode's first step), every log_frequency updates of the run, the first after log_frequency updates; each evaluation from fresh initial states; normalised score mean(return / 10) (the DMC normalisation) The trainer protocol is the one behind the paper's training curves T17 TD-MPC2 MT Datasets mt30 / mt80 (replay of 240 single-task agents, random to expert) Self-generated: full training history of single-task Ajax runs on the playground versions of the 19 original mt30 DMC tasks Validates the mechanisms, not the paper's numbers E18 both dm_control (MuJoCo C) mujoco_playground MJX ports: reduced solver iterations, some sim_dt changes (e.g. reacher 0.005 vs 0.02), impl='jax' on CPU. QuadrupedRun / DogRun and the 11 custom TD-MPC2 tasks are unavailable Environment, not algorithm E19 both dm_control action repeat stops at the episode end brax EpisodeWrapper repeat continues after a termination None on DMC (never terminates) E20 both Fresh random initial state every episode Same: static reset mode resets freshly itself; dynamic mode uses the auto-reset, fresh on every backend since playground envs default to fresh_reset=True (#54). Only a playground env built with fresh_reset=False restarts from a cached first state in dynamic mode (warned) None with the default env stack E21 both — Golden checksums are CPU-only regression guards GPU nondeterminism (TF32, scatter-add order) D22 DreamerV3 Two-hot bins symexp(jnp.linspace(-20, 0, 128)) evaluated in float32 inside the jitted step; expectation p_m·b_m + Σ (p_i·b_i + p_j·b_j) over mirror pairs, which XLA fuses into multiply-adds under jit, so a zero-initialised head predicts a constant that depends on the compiled program (−0.17 to +0.16 on CPU), not the 0 of paper p.18 Bins: float32 rounding of the float64 values, computed once with numpy (the same constants eagerly, under jit and on every backend); expectation Σ (p_j − p_i)·b_j over mirror pairs, exactly 0 for uniform p also under jit Same expectation in exact arithmetic: bins within 1.3e-6 relative of the reference's; encode and loss bit-identical given the same bins; decode within 3·ε·E_p|b| (ε = float32 epsilon). Not negligible in training. Once the logits move, the reference's contracted pair sum adds noise of std ≈ 0.085 (max ≈ 0.3) to every reward, value and slow-critic prediction, plus a constant at zero logits that depends on the compiled program (−0.17 to +0.16); the noise fades as the outer bins lose mass (CartPole, 1m: value std 0.085, 0.052, ≈ 0.01 over the 2000-, 4000- and 6000-row windows). It slows the early decline of the actor's entropy (CartPole, 1m, 4000-row window: 0.51 with the reference's sum, 0.46 with Ajax's, measured in both codebases); with the same expectation on both sides (and the replay sampler seeded per run), the training statistics' seed ranges overlap the reference's in at least 52 of the 58 windows with updates (PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md, DreamerV3 reference comparison, round 3, for the exceptions). Ajax's form is exact only while the outer logits stay bitwise mirror-symmetric, which depends on the compiled program (a one-seed run and a three-seed vmapped run differ): a float32 fragility of the bins (±4.85e8, holding ≈ 1/255 of the mass early on) that both codebases share D23 DreamerV3 Kernel init 1.1368 · sqrt(1/fan_in) · TruncatedNormal(−2, 2) variance_scaling(outscale², 'fan_in', 'truncated_normal'), i.e. the exact factor 1/0.87962566 Same draws up to a constant factor: 4.16e-5 relative T24 TD-MPC2 Two-hot over torch.linspace(vmin, vmax, 101) (middle bin −1.5e-7, not 0), any vmin < vmax; target by the floor formula k = floor((x − vmin)/Δ); naive expectation Σ p_k·b_k; F.log_softmax Bins: float32 rounding of the float64 grid, mirrored (within 4.8e-7 of torch's); target by linear interpolation between the neighbouring bins; symmetric expectation as in D22; logits − logsumexp(logits); symmetric ranges only (vmax = −vmin, as in every TD-MPC2 config) Float32 rounding: weights within 1.1e-5 of the floor formula and closer to the exact ones (2e-6 vs 8.6e-6); decode within ε·(1 + 6·E_p|b|) in symlog space (≤ 4.8e-6); log-probabilities within 3·ε·(max|logits| + loss) T25 TD-MPC2 RunningScale: sort-and-interpolate _percentile; S.lerp_(v, τ), i.e. S + τ·(v − S) jnp.percentile (linear: the same formula); (1 − τ)·S + τ·v (optax.incremental_update) Float32 rounding (≤ 1e-6 relative over 30 updates, tested) T26 TD-MPC2 b67b21c replay capacity floor(min(buffer_size, steps) / T) episodes (buffer.py:40) ceil(min(buffer_size, total) / (T·n_envs)) rounds of n_envs episodes, plus one staging round that is written in place and never sampled; total = the run's env steps when the current train() call ends, so a resumed run (chunked training, or a checkpoint restored by a new agent) sizes its ring for the whole run and moves the carried episodes into it (EpisodeBuffer.adopt) Identical when buffer_size is a multiple of T·n_envs (DMC: 1e6 / 500 = 2000 episodes) and whenever the run never fills the buffer; otherwise at most one more round. A run trained in chunks replays exactly what the uninterrupted run does T28 TD-MPC2 One update per env step after the seed-phase burst (online_trainer.py:105-112); config.yaml has no update-to-data option updates_per_step r (default 1): max(1, round(n_envs·r)) updates per stepping tick after the burst, which stays seed_steps updates; in the episodic mode (T29) max(1, round(m·r)) on a tick that stepped m > 0 envs Opt-in generalisation; r = 1 is the reference exactly (and T7 for n_envs > 1) T29 TD-MPC2 Latest code's episodic mode (eece801, as at e9f5932): single env; finished episodes added to a row storage of min(buffer_size, steps) rows; SliceSampler(strict_length=True): uniform episode among those of ≥ H+1 rows, uniform offset; seed phase and one update per env step counted in env steps; every other part of the agent at its latest version Opt-in (episodic=True), grafted onto the paper-era agent (every §2 choice above kept, e.g. Q dropout in the TD target); dynamic-reset row collector: per-env rings of ceil(min(buffer_size, total) / n_envs) rows written in lockstep (the running episode's rows included; total = the run's rows when the current train() call ends, the reference's clamp to the run, so a resumed run moves the carried rows into its own rings, EpisodicBuffer.adopt), an overwritten episode keeps its stored tail as in the reference; seed phase max(S div n, T) ticks (held rows included, ≈ S·k/(k+1) env steps for k-step episodes), then one update per env stepped in the tick (none until an episode of ≥ H+1 rows is stored); n_timesteps counts rows Same targets, losses, planning and sampling distribution; the seed phase is shorter by the episode ends it contains. Validated on a terminating chain whose values are known (test_tdmpc2_episodic.py) D26 DreamerV3 when.Ratio keeps prev in float64: prev += repeats / r The exact closed form 1 + ⌊(t − t0)·r⌋ on the absolute tick (r the exact fraction of train_ratio / (B·T)) Identical whenever 1/r is exact in float64 (every reference configuration: r = 2^k); otherwise the reference's rounding sometimes runs an update one transition late, and Ajax is at most one update ahead (tested) D27 DreamerV3 Replay capacity in items (5e6), FIFO over the items of all workers Per-env rings of C = min(ceil(replay_capacity / n_envs), rows per env of the run) rows, overwritten in lockstep Never binds in the paper protocols (DMC: 250K rows ≪ 5e6), in one run or split into resumed calls (a resumed run grows a run-clamped ring to its total length); when it binds, every env drops its oldest row together and L − 1 fewer items per env are kept than rows

docs.title: DreamerV3 implementation reference: revised / Nature recipe, vector observations
docs.text: This document merges three verified component specs (world model, actor-critic, training) into one reference. It includes every correction and missing item from the adversarial verifiers, and a re-check of the disputed points against the sources. It is meant to replace the paper and the code for the implementer.

docs.title: Sources and pinned versions
docs.text:
Source Identifier Role Paper Hafner, Pasukonis, Ba, Lillicrap, "Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models", arXiv:2301.04104v2 (revised version, matches the Nature 2025 paper). https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.04104v2 Primary algorithm description. Page numbers below are v2 PDF pages. Official code (pinned) danijar/dreamerv3 @ e3f0224 ("Fix Atari frame maxpooling on reset (#213)"). https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3/tree/e3f02248693a79dc8b0ebd62c93683888ddaccfe The "Spec (exact)" column describes this code unless marked otherwise. The world-model, actor-critic and config code at HEAD comes from the f8817c4 rewrite (2024-12-07). Later commits (55c8c67, ec19f16, cd026ac, bfcdfc1, b65cf81, cdf5709, e3f0224) touch only the API, logging, Docker/README, the atari100k task name, driver stop plumbing and Atari envs. None of them changes the algorithm. Paper-era revised code 2411f7d (2024-04-15) The code that produced the paper's Table 2 protocol. Used for version notes. Post-paper fixes before f8817c4 1a532a7 (2024-04-28): removed the unused flags compute_lr, winit_scale and scale_by_actent, and renamed debug_outer to outer. 03bc307 (2024-05-08): one-hot encodes integer vector obs. 29eb964 (2024-05-15): fixes the first prevact in the replay context. Version notes. DreamerV3 v1 code 8fa35f8 (2023) v1-vs-revised notes only. External dependency elements package (>= 3.19.1) provides elements.when.Ratio at HEAD. It is not vendored. Its semantics are taken from 2411f7d:embodied/core/when.py:26-42, the code it was moved from.

Reference sources: the paper PDF above and the official repository at the pinned commit. Code references path:line are relative to that repository.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Dimensions. d = model dimension, which is also the MLP width ("units") and the RSSM "hidden" width. D = 8d is the deterministic state width, g = 8 is the number of GRU blocks, S = 32 is the number of categorical latents and C = d/16 is the number of classes per latent. B = 16 is the batch size, T = 64 the number of trained steps per sequence, K the number of imagination starts per row (K = T) and H = 15 the imagination horizon. N = B·K = 1024 is the number of imagined trajectories.
  • Recommended Ajax configuration. It uses d = 256 (12M preset): D = 2048, C = 16, feature width 10d = 2560. See the Hyperparameter defaults and Open questions sections.
  • Notation. sg = stop_gradient. symlog(x) = sign(x)·log(1 + abs(x)) and symexp(x) = sign(x)·(exp(abs(x)) − 1). Norms are written ‖·‖. Table cells avoid the pipe character, so absolute values are written abs(·).
  • Code references are relative to the repo root at e3f0224 unless prefixed with a commit, e.g. 2411f7d:dreamerv3/nets.py:321.
  • "Paper vs code" labels. agree; conflict (paper and code differ); code_only (the paper is silent); partial (some sub-points agree, others are code_only or conflict).
  • Version note. Gives differences at 2411f7d (paper era) and, where useful, v1 (8fa35f8). "Same" means algorithmically identical.
  • Where the paper and HEAD conflict, the "Spec (exact)" cell gives HEAD and flags the conflict. The recommended Ajax default is in the final table, and the choice is listed under Open questions.

docs.title: Merge decisions and re-checks (traceability)
docs.text:
1. All verifier corrections are applied, and the verifiers' missing items are integrated:
  2. sliding windows that cross episodes;
  3. asynchronous write-back and parameter lag;
  4. integer observations in the paper-era code;
  5. weight-layout differences;
  6. straight-through routing;
  7. report windows;
  8. eviction retry;
  9. DMC preset history;
  10. LR warmup labelled code-only;
  11. RMSNorm precision history.
  12. Re-checked in the source and decided:
  13. replay_context = 0. The world-model spec said the official code "reuses the last carry of the previous unrelated batch, not a clean zero start". The training spec said it is a zero-state start. The source shows a zero start. Replay.sample always calls _annotate_batch(..., is_first=True), which sets is_first[:, 0] = True (embodied/core/replay.py:126, :284-286). RSSM._observe then masks deter, stoch and prevact to 0 wherever is_first holds (dreamerv3/rssm.py:75-80). The old carry is passed in but zeroed immediately, so the world-model spec's note is wrong. This item is corrected.
  14. Asynchronous outs and params. The delayed write-back (pending_outs) and the acting-parameter lag of about two driver iterations (pending_sync holds the pre-update non-donated allo, swapped only after the next policy call) are confirmed at embodied/jax/agent.py:237-247, :264-289.
  15. The first training batch is prefetched before the 1024-item gate. Confirmed: train.py:64 builds the stream at setup, Prefetch starts its worker in __iter__ (streams.py:44-48, :70-77), and Replay.sample waits only for len(sampler) >= 1 (replay.py:121-124).
  16. No 1/2 factor in the symlog MSE in either code version. At 2411f7d TransformedMseDist.log_prob = −Σ(pred − symlog(y))², and at HEAD outs.MSE.loss = (pred − sg(symlog(y)))². The conflict with paper Eq. 8 holds for both versions.
  17. Gradient-routing label. The paper's ablation (Ablations text p.10, Fig. 6b p.9, Fig. 18 caption: "additional reward and value gradients further improve performance") says that value gradients shape the representation by default. In the code, imagination features are stop-gradiented, so the replay critic (repval_grad=True) is the only path for value gradients into the world model. The training verifier's "agree (implicit)" therefore supersedes the world-model verifier's "code_only" for repval.
  18. dyn-loss gradient reach (new correction found in the merge). The world-model spec said "dyn trains only the prior net". In the code, prior = _prior(feat['deter']) uses a deter that is not stop-gradiented (rssm.py:123), so dyn also trains the core and everything upstream of h_t. This matches paper p.4: "The dynamics loss trains the sequence model". Corrected in 2.14 and in the routing matrix (4.2).
  19. Removed note: "AGC slows zero-initialised tensors". A constant per-tensor clip factor cancels in g / sqrt(EMA(g²)) when eps = 1e-20. At the first RMS step u = sign(g).
  20. LaProp beta2. The paper (p.18) says beta2 = 0.99 and describes it as "its default parameters". Both code versions use 0.999. The defaults of the LaProp reference itself were not verified here (no literature fetch), so this stays open.

docs.title: Version map: algorithmic differences, paper-era (2411f7d) to HEAD (e3f0224)
docs.text:
Each item is detailed in its own row below. This is only a summary.

Aspect 2411f7d (paper era) HEAD e3f0224 dmc_proprio preset size12m, train_ratio 512, env.dmc.repeat 2, run.steps 3e5 agent steps (6e5 env steps). Matches Table 2. size1m (code only), train_ratio 1024, repeat 1, run.steps 1.1e6 Discrete actor distribution 'onehot' with 1% unimix (matches the paper) 'categorical' with no unimix Start-state reward/continue in imagination from replay data: reward_t and hard 1 − is_terminal_t model predictions (r̂_0 unused, ĉ_0 ≈ 0.997 enters the weight) Vector decoder output outscale 0.1 (Dist default; config outscale reached only imgout) 1.0 Symlog MSE tolerance: errors² < 1e-8 zeroed; mode() returns symexp(pred) no tolerance; pred() returns the symlog-space value RMSNorm statistics computed in the input dtype (bf16), upcast only for fp16 always computed in f32 Integer vector obs cast to f32 and symlogged (2411f7d); then one-hot and symlog of everything (03bc307) one-hot, not symlogged First prevact in the replay context bug: taken from the previous unrelated batch's carry (fixed by 29eb964 on 2024-05-15) data[action][:, K−1] Slow critic separate module, f32, hard copy after the first optimizer step copy at creation, compute dtype. Equivalent in effect. Policy mean/std nonlinearities computed after the cast to f32 tanh/sigmoid on bf16 Linear outputs, then cast to f32 Stored stoch int32 argmax indices f32 one-hot. Equivalent. Encoder key order / decoder input order obs-space order / concat(deter, stoch) sorted keys / concat(stoch, deter). Layout only. CNN (out of scope) stride-2 convs, mults (1,2,3,4,4), debug_outer (first conv stride 1) conv + 2×2 max-pool, mults (2,3,4,4)

docs.title: 1. Shared building blocks (used by world model, actor and critic)
docs.text:
These are the modular primitives worth implementing once and sharing. They are also reusable for TD-MPC2 where applicable: the symlog, two-hot and RMSNorm-MLP blocks.

Item Spec (exact) Paper ref Code ref Paper vs code Version note 1.1 Linear Linear(units). Kernel W has shape (in, prod(units)) and bias b has shape (prod(units),). The bias is always present (bias=True), even when RMSNorm follows, and is zero-initialised. y = x @ W.astype(x.dtype) + b.astype(x.dtype), reshaped to (..., units). units may be a tuple: heads emit (shape) or (shape, classes). The input must be in the compute dtype (bf16). Linear calls ensure_dtypes(x) but discards the return value, so only the forward* dtype assert runs. The custom_vjp backward (cotangent) assert is active only where the returned value is used, i.e. Head.__call__. none embodied/jax/nets.py:230-251; ensure_dtypes :102-117 (call sites :241, :268, :300, :375 discard the result); embodied/jax/heads.py:88 code_only 2411f7d: Linear also took norm/act kwargs and applied Linear → Norm → act internally (2411f7d nets.py:594-635). Same composition. v1 (8fa35f8 nets.py:570): no bias when a norm follows (bias and norm == 'none'). 1.2 BlockLinear (block-diagonal dense) BlockLinear(U, g). Input x has shape (..., I) with I % g == 0 and U % g == 0. Kernel shape (g, I/g, U/g); bias shape (U,), zero-initialised. y = einsum('...ki,kio->...ko', x.reshape(..., g, I/g), W).reshape(..., U) + b. Output block k depends only on input block k. Init fan_in = (I/g)·g = I, the TOTAL input width, because compute_fans treats the leading g axis like a conv receptive field. Std[W] ≈ 1/sqrt(I) is therefore sqrt(g) ≈ 2.83× smaller than a per-block fan-in would give. Only the forward dtype assert runs (see 1.1). p.18 Networks: "GRU with block-diagonal recurrent weights of 8 blocks" embodied/jax/nets.py:254-281; fans :187-197 agree on the block structure; fan convention code_only 2411f7d: block_fans=False (config default) gives the same total fan (2411f7d nets.py:873-884). It also padded I to a multiple of g, which never triggers for the RSSM. 1.3 RMSNorm, SiLU and the hidden block RMSNorm over the last axis. x32 = f32(x); y = x32 · rsqrt(mean(x32², axis=−1, keepdims) + 1e-4) · scale. The learned scale (F,) is initialised to ones and stored in f32. There is no shift for 'rms'. The output is cast back to the input dtype (bf16). Activation: silu(x) = x·sigmoid(x). Every hidden layer is Linear → RMSNorm → SiLU (norm after the linear, before the activation, with the Linear bias kept). A LayerNorm ('layer') variant exists in the code but no config uses it. Table 4 p.21 "Activation: RMSNorm + SiLU"; p.20 "Block GRU, RMSNorm normalization, SiLu activation" embodied/jax/nets.py:361-409 (eps default :364; rms :382-386; scale init ones :401-405), :26-39 (act); dreamerv3/configs.yaml:91-101 (act silu, norm rms) agree; eps code_only 2411f7d computed the RMS in the input dtype (bf16), upcasting only for float16 (2411f7d nets.py:753-758). HEAD always uses f32. Both use eps 1e-4. v1 used LayerNorm. 1.4 MLP and MLPHead nn.MLP(layers, units) casts the input to bf16, flattens it to (N, F), applies layers × [Linear(units) → RMSNorm → SiLU] and reshapes back. MLPHead(space, output, layers, units, outscale) = MLP, then a Head (final Linear with outscale), then the output distribution. outscale reaches only the final head Linear; hidden layers always use outscale 1. DictHead builds one Head per key of a dict space. p.18 Networks (MLP sizes per module) embodied/jax/nets.py:565-587 (MLP); embodied/jax/heads.py:16-41 (MLPHead), :26-34 (outscale routed to Head only), :44-62 (DictHead), :65-94 (Head) agree 2411f7d: same composition (Dist module per output). 1.5 Weight initialisation Every Linear, BlockLinear and Conv kernel: W = outscale · 1.1368 · sqrt(1/fan_in) · TruncatedNormal(lower=−2, upper=2). The truncated normal has unit sigma before truncation and is sampled in f32. 1.1368 ≈ 1/0.8796 restores Std[W] ≈ 1/sqrt(fan_in). The config winit: trunc_normal_in parses to Initializer('trunc_normal', fan='in', scale=1.0). compute_fans: rank 0 gives (1, 1); rank 1 (n,) gives (1, n); rank 2 (in, out) gives (in, out); rank ≥ 3 gives (shape[−2]·prod(shape[:−2]), shape[−1]·prod(shape[:−2])). So a BlockLinear (g, I/g, U/g) gets fan_in = I, and a conv HWIO gets fan_in = H·W·I. Biases are zeros and never scaled by outscale. Norm scales are ones. All parameters are stored in f32. outscale per final layer: RSSM obslogit/priorlogit 1.0; vector decoder heads 1.0; reward head 0.0 (zero kernel and zero bias, so uniform softmax and a prediction of exactly 0); continue head 1.0; policy head 0.01 (both the mean and stddev Linears, or the logits Linear); value head 0.0. The slow value net starts as an exact copy of the value net (3.18). The RSSM initial state is zeros, not learned (2.2). p.6 "initialize the output weight matrix of the reward predictor and critic to zeros"; p.18 "output weights of twohot distributions are initialized to zero". No general init scheme in the paper. embodied/jax/nets.py:42-49 (name parsing), :144-197 (Initializer; trunc_normal :168-170; compute_fans :187-197), :250-251 (Linear._scaled_winit); embodied/jax/heads.py:26-34; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:91, 94-101 agree on zero twohot outputs; everything else code_only 2411f7d winit 'normal' is the same truncated normal × 1.1368 × sqrt(1/fan_in) with fan 'in' and block_fans False, so the fans are the same. Exception: the 2411f7d vector decoder output layer used outscale 0.1. Each vector head was Dist(shape, dist=vecdist) with no outscale passed, so the Dist default of 0.1 applied; the config outscale 1.0 reached only 'imgout' (2411f7d nets.py:321, :353, :408). HEAD passes outscale=1.0 to every vector head (rssm.py:304-305), so the HEAD decoder output kernel starts 10× larger. v1: fan 'avg'. 1.6 symlog / symexp symlog(x) = sign(x)·log1p(abs(x)) and symexp(x) = sign(x)·(exp(abs(x)) − 1). Symlog of vector observations is computed in f32 (obs are float32) before the bf16 cast. Eq. 9 p.7 embodied/jax/nets.py:59-64, :494-497 agree Same. 1.7 DictConcat (input concatenation) DictConcat(spaces, fdims=1, squish): keys are sorted alphabetically. Availability mask per sample and per key (not per element): available(x) = (x != −inf for floats, x != −1 for signed ints) reduced with .all() over every feature dim. If any element of a key is unavailable, the whole vector for that key and sample is zeroed. The mask is applied before and again after encoding. Discrete keys become one_hot(int32(x), classes) in bf16 and are not squished. Continuous keys become squish(x) (symlog for the encoder, identity for actions), then bf16. Feature dims are flattened and the keys concatenated. none embodied/jax/nets.py:467-500 (sorted keys :471; masks :483-484, :497), :80-99 (available; .all() reduction :95-96) code_only 2411f7d concatenated encoder vector keys in obs-space order (2411f7d nets.py:238-240). This changes only the layout. 1.8 Categorical / OneHot with unimix, straight-through, KL, entropy Logits l of shape (..., S, C) are cast to f32. Unimix: p = 0.99·softmax(l) + 0.01/C, and l' = log(p). Sample (OneHot): idx ~ Categorical(l'); value = sg(one_hot(idx)) + p − sg(p), where p = softmax(l') is the mixed probability, so the straight-through gradient flows through the mixed softmax. Factorisation: Agg(OneHot, dims=1, sum) sums kl, entropy and logp over the S = 32 latent axis. KL(P‖Q) = Σ_S Σ_C softmax(l'_P)·(log_softmax(l'_P) − log_softmax(l'_Q)). Entropy = Σ_S −Σ_C p log p. Unimix is re-applied every time the distribution is built from logits, including after sg. Store raw logits. outs.Categorical(logits) without unimix (the HEAD discrete policy, 3.14) samples an int index with jax.random.categorical; logp = log_softmax(l)[a]. p.4 straight-through; p.5 "1% uniform and 99% neural network output"; p.18 Distributions; Table 4 "Latent unimix 1%" embodied/jax/outs.py:208-240 (Categorical; unimix :210-217; kl :236-240; entropy :230-234), :243-270 (OneHot; straight-through :265-270), :40-76 (Agg) agree 2411f7d: a tfp OneHotCategorical subclass with the same straight-through formula (2411f7d jaxutils.py:103-116), and Independent(..., 1) for the latent sum. Unimix was applied inside _logit, so the stored logit was already log(mixed probs). Mathematically identical. 1.9 Symexp two-hot distribution (reward and critic) Bins (n = 255): half = symexp(linspace(−20, 0, 128, f32)); bins = concat([half, −reverse(half[:−1])]). This equals symexp(linspace(−20, 20, 255)) with exact antisymmetry, bins[127] = 0, a step of 20/127 in symlog space, and a range of ±symexp(20) ≈ ±4.85e8. Loss for target y (f32, raw space, not symlogged): see Algorithm D. The interpolation is linear in raw space between neighbouring symexp-spaced bins. A target outside the range puts all its mass on the edge bin; an exact bin hit puts all its mass on that bin. Prediction: probs = softmax(logits) in f32, then the symmetric sum: p[m]·b[m] + Σ(reverse(p[:m]·b[:m]) + p[m+1:]·b[m+1:]) with m = 127. This pairs mirror bins from small to large magnitude, so uniform probs give exactly 0. There is no unsquash. Eq. 10-11 p.7 (B = symexp([−20 … +20])); Eq. 12 p.18 (twohot weights, k = Σ_j δ(b_j < x)); p.18 "summation order matters … positive and negative bins summed separately, from small to large" embodied/jax/heads.py:132-144 (bins); embodied/jax/outs.py:273-330 (pred :285-309, loss :311-330); dreamerv3/configs.yaml:98, :101 (bins 255) agree. The bin count is code_only. Eq. 12 and the code agree inside the range, including exact bin hits (Eq. 12 at x = b_{k+1} puts weight 1 on index k+1). The only difference is out-of-range targets: Eq. 12 is undefined for k = 0 or k = abs(B), while the code clips to the edge bin. 2411f7d emitted 256 logits and dropped the last for odd bins (2411f7d nets.py:432-438, :462-471). docs.title: Algorithm D: two-hot loss and prediction (raw-space interpolation)
docs.text:
def twohot_loss(logits, y, bins):                      # logits [..., n] f32, y [...] f32 raw
    n = len(bins)
    below = clip(sum(bins <= y[..., None], -1) - 1, 0, n - 1)
    above = clip(n - sum(bins > y[..., None], -1), 0, n - 1)
    equal = below == above
    d_below = where(equal, 1, abs(bins[below] - y))
    d_above = where(equal, 1, abs(bins[above] - y))
    w_below = d_above / (d_below + d_above)
    w_above = d_below / (d_below + d_above)
    target = w_below[..., None] * one_hot(below, n) + w_above[..., None] * one_hot(above, n)
    return -sum(target * (logits - logsumexp(logits, -1, keepdims=True)), -1)

def twohot_pred(logits, bins):                         # odd n, m = (n - 1) // 2
    p = softmax(logits)
    m = (len(bins) - 1) // 2
    pb = p * bins
    return pb[..., m] + sum(pb[..., :m][..., ::-1] + pb[..., m + 1:], -1)

docs.title: Algorithm A: block-GRU core (RSSM._core, dynlayers = 1)
docs.text:
def core(deter, stoch, action):     # deter [B, D] bf16, stoch [B, S, C] bf16 one-hot, action [B, A] bf16
    D, Hd, g = 8 * d, d, 8          # Hd = rssm.hidden
    z = stoch.reshape(B, S * C)
    a = action / sg(maximum(1, abs(action)))
    x0 = silu(rms(Linear(Hd)(deter)))          # 'dynin0'  (full deter: the only cross-block mixing)
    x1 = silu(rms(Linear(Hd)(z)))              # 'dynin1'
    x2 = silu(rms(Linear(Hd)(a)))              # 'dynin2'
    x = concat([x0, x1, x2], -1)               # [B, 3Hd]
    x = repeat(x[:, None, :], g, axis=1)       # [B, g, 3Hd]: same embedding for every block
    x = concat([deter.reshape(B, g, D // g), x], -1).reshape(B, g * (D // g + 3 * Hd))
    x = silu(rms(BlockLinear(D, g)(x)))        # 'dynhid0'; RMSNorm over the FULL D vector
    x = BlockLinear(3 * D, g)(x)               # 'dyngru'; no norm, no activation
    r, c, u = split(x.reshape(B, g, 3 * D // g), 3, axis=-1)   # per-block [r | c | u]
    r, c, u = (y.reshape(B, D) for y in (r, c, u))
    r = sigmoid(r)
    c = tanh(r * c)                            # reset gate scales the whole candidate pre-activation
    u = sigmoid(u - 1)                         # u weights the candidate; ~0.27 at init
    return u * c + (1 - u) * deter

docs.title: Algorithm B: one observe step (RSSM._observe), used both when training and when acting
docs.text:
def observe_step(carry, token_t, prevact_t, is_first_t):
    deter, stoch, prevact_t = where(is_first_t, 0, (carry.deter, carry.stoch, prevact_t))
    act = DictConcat(act_space)(prevact_t)     # one-hot for discrete, identity for continuous
    act = where(is_first_t, 0, act)            # mask again: one_hot(0) != 0
    deter = core(deter, stoch, act)            # h_t
    x = concat([deter, token_t], -1)
    x = silu(rms(Linear(d)(x)))                # 'obs0'
    logit = Linear(S * C, outscale=1.0)(x).reshape(S, C)   # 'obslogit', raw
    stoch = bf16(OneHot(logit, unimix=0.01).sample())      # straight-through sample
    return {deter, stoch}, entry={deter, stoch}, feat={deter, stoch, logit}

docs.title: Algorithm C: one imagine step (RSSM.imagine, single=True)
docs.text:
def imagine_step(carry, policy):
    a = policy(sg(carry))                      # pi(. | feat2tensor(sg(carry))).sample()
    deter = core(carry.deter, carry.stoch, DictConcat(act_space)(a))
    x = deter
    for i in range(2):
        x = silu(rms(Linear(d)(x)))            # 'prior0', 'prior1'
    logit = Linear(S * C, outscale=1.0)(x).reshape(S, C)   # 'priorlogit'
    stoch = bf16(OneHot(logit, unimix=0.01).sample())
    return {deter, stoch}, (feat={deter, stoch, logit}, action=a)

docs.title: Algorithm E: world-model part of the loss (Agent.loss, first half)
docs.text:
tokens = enc(obs)                                          # [B, T, d]
carry, entries, feat = rssm.observe(carry0, tokens, prevact, obs.is_first)   # scan, Algorithm B
prior = rssm.prior(feat.deter)                             # [B, T, S, C], parallel
dyn = max(KL(OneHot(sg(feat.logit)) || OneHot(prior)), 1.0)       # summed over S
rep = max(KL(OneHot(feat.logit) || OneHot(sg(prior))), 1.0)
recons = dec(concat(stoch_flat, deter))                    # one dist per obs key
losses[key] = recons[key].loss(sg(obs[key]))  for each vector key   # [B, T] each
x = feat2tensor(feat)                                      # concat(deter, stoch_flat), NOT sg
losses.rew = rewhead(x).loss(obs.reward)                   # two-hot NLL, raw reward
losses.con = conhead(x).loss(f32(~obs.is_terminal) * (1 - 1/333))
losses.dyn, losses.rep = dyn, rep                          # all [B, T]

docs.text: Item Spec (exact) Paper ref Code ref Paper vs code Version note 3.1 Imagination start states Imagination starts from every posterior state in the replayed batch. K = min(imag_last or T, T), and imag_last = 0, so K = T. With B = 16 and T = 64 that is B·T = 1024 start states. There is no subsampling. The replay sequence has 64 + 1 steps; the context step is dropped (5.8), leaving T = 64. Each start carry is the posterior entry {deter_t, stoch_t}, where stoch_t is the sampled one-hot posterior. Flatten batch-major: x[:, −K:].reshape(B·K, ...). The same ordering is used for the 'first' features and for reshaping the replay bootstrap to (B, K) (3.19). No start state is masked: terminal and is_last starts are still imagined, and are down-weighted only through the continuation weight (3.6). p.5 Critic learning ("Starting from representations of replayed inputs…"); Table 4 (B = 16, T = 64) dreamerv3/agent.py:189-191, :194-195; dreamerv3/rssm.py:56-59; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:10-11, :15, :104; dreamerv3/main.py:184-188 agree. Using all B·T states is code detail. 2411f7d: imag_start 'all' with imag_repeat 1 (2411f7d configs.yaml:132-133; agent.py:276-282), giving the same start set. batch_length was 65 including context, so T is also 64. 3.2 Horizon and trajectory layout H = imag_length = 15 imagined steps. Each trajectory has H + 1 = 16 states: index 0 is the posterior start state and indices 1..15 are imagined prior states. The paper's "prediction horizon T = 16" counts these 16 states. imgfeat[:, 0] = sg(posterior feat at t); imgfeat[:, i] = sg(state after i imagined steps). imgact[:, i] = the action sampled at state i, for i = 0..H, so imgact is aligned with imgfeat. imgact[:, H] ('lastact') is sampled at the last state only to fill the shape, and is never used because every loss slices [:, :−1]. Discrete: Categorical.sample gives an int index. Continuous: mean + std·N(0, 1), an unclipped float sample. The policy input is feat2tensor(sg(carry)) = concat(deter, flatten(stoch)) in the compute dtype. Then deter' = core(deter, stoch, onehot_or_float(a)); logit' = prior(deter'); stoch' ~ OneHot(logit', 0.01). The core's a / sg(max(1, abs(a))) acts as a forward-pass clip to [−1, 1] for continuous actions (2.3). For the loss, the policy is evaluated again on the stop-gradient features with identical parameters, so learning is exactly on-policy. For t ∈ [0, H): L_val[b, t] = sg(w_t)·(CE_twohot(v_ψ(s_t), sg(R_t)) + slowreg·CE_twohot(v_ψ(s_t), sg(E[v_slow(s_t)]))), with slowreg = 1.0. The regulariser target is the slow critic's scalar expectation (slowvalue.pred()), two-hot encoded. It is not a KL or cross-entropy to the slow critic's full distribution. Both terms are evaluated on the same stop-gradient imagined features. State H gets no loss (the pad is sliced off). Reduction: mean over H, then over (B, K), × β_val = 1.0. Eq. 5 p.5 (max-likelihood loss −Σ ln p_ψ(R^λ_t ∣ s_t)); p.6 (regularise toward an EMA of its own parameters); Table 4 (β_val = 1, critic EMA regulariser 1) dreamerv3/agent.py:417-422, :215, :240; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:86, :108 agree. The paper does not specify the form of the regulariser. The continuation weighting is code_only. 2411f7d: the same (agent.py:344-350), but the slow critic was computed in f32 (dtype 'float32', agent.py:77-78); HEAD uses the compute dtype. 3.18 Slow critic EMA SlowModel(rate 0.02, every 1). Init: on first use, the slow params are an exact copy of the online value params (_initonce; val(inp) is called before slowval(inp)). Update: once per train step, after the optimizer step: mix = rate if count % every == 0 else 0; θ_slow ← mix·θ + (1 − mix)·θ_slow; count += 1. That is an EMA decay of 0.98 every step. The slow params are not in the optimizer's module list, so they get no gradient. The slow critic is used only as a regularisation target (imagination and replay losses), never for bootstrapping or the advantage baseline (slowtar = False). p.6 Critic learning (EMA regulariser); Table 4 (critic EMA decay 0.98, regulariser 1) embodied/jax/utils.py:94-127 (update :113-119, _initonce :121-127); dreamerv3/agent.py:66-68, :74-78, :139-142; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:110 agree 2411f7d SlowUpdater: a separate module with its own random init, computed in f32. mix = clip(1·[updates == 0] + 0.02·[updates % 1 == 0], 0, 1), so a hard copy happens when updater() is first called, which is after the first optimizer step (29eb964:jaxutils.py:737-762; 2411f7d agent.py:77-83, :207-210). HEAD copies at creation and mixes 0.02 at the first update. Equivalent in effect, not by construction: both critics have zero-initialised output layers, so both slow critics predict exactly 0 at step 1, and the warmup gives lr = 0 at step 0, so θ_1 = θ_0. 3.19 Replay value loss (repval) Enabled by repval_loss = True, scale β_repval = 0.3. Inputs: the replay batch's posterior features repfeat, not stop-gradiented (repval_grad = True), so this loss also trains the encoder and RSSM (2.16). Uses real is_last, is_terminal and reward over the last K = T steps. Bootstrap: boot[b, t] = R^λ_0 of the imagination rollout that started at replay state (b, t), i.e. imag ret[:, 0].reshape(B, K): the imagined λ-return estimate of V(s_t) under the current policy, built from the online critic. Replay λ-return (Algorithm H) with γ = 1 − 1/333 fixed (independent of contdisc) and λ = 0.95: R_{T−1} := boot_{T−1}; for t = T−2..0: live = γ(1 − term_{t+1}), cont = λ(1 − last_{t+1}), R_t = r_{t+1} + live·((1 − cont)·boot_{t+1} + cont·R_{t+1}). At an episode end (last_{t+1}) there is no λ continuation: R_t = r_{t+1} + γ(1 − term_{t+1})·boot_{t+1}. r_{t+1} = obs['reward'][t+1]. Loss for t ∈ [0, T−1): L_repval[b, t] = (1 − is_last_t)·(CE_twohot(v_ψ(s_t), sg(R_t)) + 1.0·CE_twohot(v_ψ(s_t), sg(E[v_slow(s_t)]))). The weight is the hard mask ~is_last; terminal steps are also is_last, and the batch annotation marks the step before any mid-window is_first as is_last (5.3). There is no continuation product. The last replay index gets no loss. Reduction: mean over all (B, T−1) = (16, 63) entries including masked zeros, × 0.3. slowtar has no effect here, because tarval goes only into the unused val argument. p.6 Critic learning (replay critic loss β_repval = 0.3, using "the imagination returns R^λ_t at the start states of the imagination rollouts as on-policy value annotations for the replay trajectory to then compute λ-returns over the replay rewards"); Table 4 (0.3) dreamerv3/agent.py:218-235 (sg skip :220; boot :222), :449-479, :482-490; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:86, :109, :115-116 agree. The ~is_last mask, the explicit γ and the gradient flow into the world model are code details. The gradient flow is implied by the paper's ablation (2.16). 2411f7d: the same (replay_critic_loss True, replay_critic_grad True, replay_critic_bootstrap 'imag', return_lambda_replay 0.95; configs.yaml:104-106, :138; agent.py:352-373). 3.20 Order of operations within one train step Inside the loss (under nj.grad): (1) world-model forward on replay (posterior repfeat, dyn entries; Algorithm E). (2) Imagine H = 15 steps from all B·T posterior starts with the current policy, and detach the features. (3) Evaluate r̂, ĉ, policy, value and slow value on all H + 1 states. (4) Read the valnorm stats (no-op); compute tarval and the weight; compute R (λ-return); update retnorm with R, then read S; compute the advantage and the policy loss; update valnorm (no-op); compute the value loss. (5) repl_loss: bootstrap from R[:, 0], compute the replay λ-return and the repval loss. (6) Sum the scaled means and take the gradient. After the loss: (7) optimizer update, then the slow-critic EMA update, then latent write-back (5.9). Normaliser updates happen only when training = True. not stated dreamerv3/agent.py:137-154 (train), :156-245 (loss), :382-446 (imag_loss), :449-479 (repl_loss) code_only Same.

docs.title: Algorithm H: λ-return (shared by imagination and replay)
docs.text:
def lambda_return(last, term, rew, boot, disc, lam):     # all [N, L] f32; the code's unused 'val' arg dropped
    live = (1 - term)[:, 1:] * disc
    cont = (1 - last)[:, 1:] * lam
    interm = rew[:, 1:] + (1 - cont) * live * boot[:, 1:]
    R = [boot[:, -1]]
    for t in reversed(range(L - 1)):
        R.append(interm[:, t] + live[:, t] * cont[:, t] * R[-1])
    return stack(list(reversed(R))[:-1], 1)               # [N, L-1] = R_0 .. R_{L-2}
# imagination: last=0, term=1-c_hat, rew=r_hat, boot=v_online, disc=1 (contdisc), lam=0.95, L=H+1=16
# replay:      last=is_last, term=is_terminal, rew=reward, boot=imag_R0.reshape(B,K), disc=1-1/333, lam=0.95, L=T=64

docs.title: Algorithm F: imagination actor-critic loss (imag_loss)
docs.text:
# inputs on (N=B*K, H+1): act (sg), r_hat = rew.pred(), c_hat = con.prob(1), pi, v, v_slow (all on sg feats)
v_on   = v.pred()                                  # online critic expectation
disc   = 1.0                                       # contdisc=True
weight = cumprod(disc * c_hat, axis=1) / disc      # includes c_hat_0
R      = lambda_return(0, 1 - c_hat, r_hat, v_on, disc, 0.95)           # [N, H]
lo, hi = retnorm.update_then_read(sg(R))           # EMA(0.99) of P5 and P95, init 0, no debias
S      = max(1.0, hi - lo)
adv    = (R - v_on[:, :-1]) / S
logpi  = sum_k pi_k.logp(sg(act_k))[:, :-1]
ent    = sum_k pi_k.entropy()[:, :-1]
L_pol  = sg(weight[:, :-1]) * -(logpi * sg(adv) + 3e-4 * ent)
tar    = concat([R, zeros(N, 1)], 1)
L_val  = sg(weight[:, :-1]) * (v.loss(sg(tar)) + 1.0 * v.loss(sg(v_slow.pred())))[:, :-1]
losses.policy = L_pol.mean(1).reshape(B, K); losses.value = L_val.mean(1).reshape(B, K)

docs.title: Algorithm G: replay critic loss (repl_loss)
docs.text:
feat = repfeat                                    # NOT sg (repval_grad=True)
boot = R_imag[:, 0].reshape(B, K)                 # imagined lambda-return from each replay state
Rr   = lambda_return(obs.is_last, obs.is_terminal, obs.reward, boot, 1 - 1/333, 0.95)   # [B, T-1]
tar  = concat([Rr, zeros(B, 1)], 1)
L    = f32(~obs.is_last)[:, :-1] * (v(feat).loss(sg(tar)) + 1.0 * v(feat).loss(sg(v_slow(feat).pred())))[:, :-1]
losses.repval = L                                 # [B, T-1]; mean over all entries, x 0.3

docs.title: 4. Loss assembly, gradient routing and optimizer
docs.text: Item Spec (exact) Paper ref Code ref Paper vs code Version note 4.1 Total loss assembly, per-loss scales and reductions loss_scales = {rec: 1.0, rew: 1.0, con: 1.0, dyn: 1.0, rep: 0.1, policy: 1.0, value: 1.0, repval: 0.3}. 'rec' is replaced by one entry per decoder observation key, each with scale 1.0. Every term is an un-reduced tensor. World-model terms are asserted to have shape (B, T) = (16, 64): rec_key (summed squared error over the key's feature dims, 2.11), rew (two-hot NLL), con (soft-label Bernoulli NLL), dyn and rep (free-bits KL summed over latents). Imagination terms policy and value are computed on (B·K, H) = (1024, 15), then .mean(axis=1) and reshaped to (B, K) = (16, 64). repval has shape (B, T−1) = (16, 63), masked by (1 − is_last). TOTAL: L = Σ_k scale_k · mean_over_all_elements(loss_k). It is a mean, not divided by the sum of weights, so weighted-out or masked entries still count in the denominator. World-model terms are not masked at episode boundaries; the RSSM handles resets through is_first. The world-model and actor-critic losses form one f32 scalar, differentiated w.r.t. all modules [dyn, enc, dec, rew, con, pol, val] and applied in one optimizer step. Eq. 2 p.4 (L = E[Σ_{t=1..T}(β_pred L_pred + β_dyn L_dyn + β_rep L_rep)]); Eq. 5/6 (sums over t); Table 4 (β_pred = 1, β_dyn = 1, β_rep = 0.1, β_val = 1, β_repval = 0.3, β_pol = 1) dreamerv3/agent.py:80-83 (scales, rec expanded per key), :184-186 (shape assert), :215 (imagination reshape), :219-235 (repval), :237-240 (sum of scaled means), :74-78 (single optimizer); dreamerv3/configs.yaml:86 conflict in reduction form, while the scale values agree. The paper sums over t; the code takes means over B × T and over H. A sum would make the world-model terms 64× and the actor-critic terms 15× larger, which changes their relative weighting. Global rescaling is otherwise absorbed by LaProp (eps 1e-20) except through AGC thresholds. Reproduce the code's means. 2411f7d: scales {dec_cnn 1, dec_mlp 1 (per vector key), reward 1, cont 1, dyn 1, rep 0.1, actor 1, critic 1, replay_critic 0.3} with the same mean reduction (agent.py:414-415), written Σ_k mean(scale_k · loss_k): each element is scaled before the mean (the same value up to float32 rounding). v1: separate model, actor and critic optimizers. 4.2 Gradient routing inside the single optimizer (summary) See the routing matrix below; details in 2.16 and 3.4. reward_grad = True; the continue and decoder inputs are not sg; repval_grad = True (the replay critic trains enc and dyn); ac_grads = False (imagination starts and imagined feats are sg, so policy and value losses update only pol and val). Inside imagine, the policy sees sg(carry). After the optimizer step: slowval ← 0.02·val + 0.98·slowval (3.18). The retnorm percentile EMA is updated inside the loss forward pass (training = True), once per step. p.4 (end-to-end world model); Eq. 6 (sg advantage); Ablations p.10, Fig. 6b, Fig. 18 (reward and value gradients shape the representation); Table 4 (critic EMA decay 0.98, regulariser 1) dreamerv3/agent.py:139-142, :172, :196, :219-220; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:88, :110, :114-116; embodied/jax/utils.py:94-127 agree (implicit for repval, see 2.16) 2411f7d: replay_critic_grad True, reward_grad True, ac_grads 'none', slow fraction 0.02 every 1. Same. 4.3 Optimizer: one LaProp chain over ALL trainable modules One optimizer instance over modules [dyn, enc, dec, rew, con, pol, val]: world model, actor and critic in one param tree, one scalar loss, one update per train step. Not optimised: slowval (EMA copy of val) and the retnorm, valnorm and advnorm statistics. Per step: (L, grads) = value_and_grad of L w.r.t. the f32 params (loss asserted f32 with shape ()); on multiple devices grads = pmean over the data axes. updates = chain(grads), with the chain in this exact order: (1) clip_by_agc(0.3, pmin = 1e-3) per tensor (4.4); (2) scale_by_rms(beta2 = 0.999, eps = 1e-20), bias-corrected (4.5); (3) scale_by_momentum(beta1 = 0.9, nesterov = False), bias-corrected (4.6); (4) add_decayed_weights only if wd > 0 (wd = 0); (5) optax.scale_by_learning_rate(schedule), i.e. × −lr_k (4.7). params ← params + updates. Optimizer state is f32. The config key opt.momentum = True is accepted by _make_opt but ignored: momentum is always appended. See Algorithm I. p.18 Optimizer; Table 4 (LR 4e-5, AGC(0.3), LaProp(ε = 1e-20)); p.20 "Previous Dreamer generations" (AGC, LaProp = RMSProp followed by momentum) dreamerv3/agent.py:74-78, :342-379 (_make_opt; chain :358-360); embodied/jax/opt.py:16-81 (f32 scalar assert :37-38; pmean :52-54; update :60-63); dreamerv3/configs.yaml:87 agree, apart from beta2 (4.5) 2411f7d: the same single optimizer (separate_lrs False) in dreamerv3/jaxutils.py, with an optional globclip (0.0 = off) before AGC. Identical maths. 4.4 Adaptive gradient clipping (AGC), per TENSOR For every parameter leaf p with gradient g (each kernel, bias and norm scale is its own tensor): u = ‖vec(g)‖₂, n = ‖vec(p)‖₂ (current, pre-update params), upper = 0.3·max(1e-3, n), g ← g / max(1, u/upper). Applied to the raw gradient of the summed loss, before RMS normalisation. This is not NFNet unit-wise AGC: there are no per-row norms, and the norm runs over the whole flattened tensor, including 3-D BlockLinear kernels. Zero-initialised tensors (all biases, the zero output kernels of the reward and value heads) have n = 0, so their gradient norm is capped at 3e-4 until they grow. This cap does not slow those tensors: a constant per-tensor factor cancels in the following g / sqrt(EMA(g²)) with eps = 1e-20, and at the first RMS step u = sign(g) whatever the clip. As ‖p‖ grows the cap loosens, which makes normalised updates temporarily larger while the EMA catches up. pmin = 1e-3 is a hard-coded default at HEAD. p.18 ("clips per-tensor gradients if they exceed 30% of the L2 norm of the weight matrix they correspond to, with its default ε = 10⁻³") embodied/jax/opt.py:109-123; dreamerv3/agent.py:358; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:87 (agc 0.3) agree 2411f7d jaxutils.scale_by_agc: identical formula, pmin configurable (1e-3). 4.5 LaProp normaliser (RMS step), beta2 conflict State: step (int32, init 0) and nu (f32 zeros). step ← step + 1; nu ← β₂·nu + (1 − β₂)·g² (g is the AGC-clipped gradient); nu_hat = nu / (1 − β₂^step); u = g / (sqrt(nu_hat) + eps), with eps added after the sqrt. Code: β₂ = 0.999, eps = 1e-20. With such a small eps the update is invariant to a global rescaling of the loss. p.18: "LaProp optimizer with ε = 10⁻²⁰ and its default parameters β₁ = 0.9 and β₂ = 0.99" (verified on PDF p.18) embodied/jax/opt.py:126-143; dreamerv3/agent.py:348, :359; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:87 (beta2 0.999) conflict: the paper says 0.99, the code 0.999 2411f7d: {scaler rms, beta2 0.999, eps 1e-20}, the same as HEAD. So the published curves were produced with 0.999. float32 caveat (observed running 29eb964 in M6: one step of 195 learning rates, from g ≈ 2e-18): the term that underflows is the increment (1 − β₂)·g². Below the smallest normal float32 (1.18e-38), i.e. for 4.6 LaProp momentum step Its own step counter (int32) and mu (f32 zeros). step ← step + 1; mu ← β₁·mu + (1 − β₁)·u, where u is the RMS-normalised update from 4.5; output mu_hat = mu / (1 − β₁^step). β₁ = 0.9, nesterov = False. Momentum acts on the normalised update (LaProp), not on the raw gradient (Adam). p.18 ("LaProp normalizes gradients by RMSProp and then smoothes them by momentum"), β₁ = 0.9 embodied/jax/opt.py:146-164; dreamerv3/agent.py:360 agree Identical in 1a532a7 jaxutils.scale_by_momentum. 4.7 Learning rate and warmup schedule lr = 4e-5. schedule 'const', anneal 0, warmup 1000 updates: ramp = optax.linear_schedule(0, lr, 1000); sched = join_schedules([ramp, constant(lr)], [1000]); applied through optax.scale_by_learning_rate (sign flipped). With the optax count k = 0, 1, 2, … (read before increment): lr_k = 4e-5 · k/1000 for k < 1000, then 4e-5. The first update uses lr = 0, so it is a no-op on the params, but the moments still accumulate. No decay afterwards. The warmup covers the actor and critic too, since they share the optimizer. The unused 'linear' and 'cosine' options decay to 0.1·lr over (anneal − warmup) steps. docs.text:
"RSSM" is the code module dyn: core, prior MLP and posterior obs layers. The straight-through mark (ST) means the gradient reaches the posterior logits through z_t.

Loss (scale) enc RSSM core RSSM prior MLP RSSM posterior layers dec rew con pol val slowval rec per key (1.0) yes yes no yes (ST) yes no no no no no rew (1.0) yes yes no yes (ST) no yes no no no no con (1.0) yes yes no yes (ST) no no yes no no no dyn (1.0) yes, via h_t and earlier steps yes yes via earlier z through h_t no no no no no no rep (0.1) yes yes no yes no no no no no no policy (1.0) no no no no no no no yes no no value (1.0) no no no no no no no no yes no repval (0.3) yes yes no yes (ST) no no no no yes no (EMA after step) 0.02·val + 0.98·slowval

docs.title: Algorithm I: one optimizer update (shared by all modules)
docs.text:
def opt_update(params, grads, state):                 # all f32
    k = state.count                                   # 0, 1, 2, ...
    g = {name: gi / max(1.0, norm(gi) / (0.3 * max(1e-3, norm(params[name]))))
         for name, gi in grads.items()}               # AGC per tensor
    state.t_rms += 1
    state.nu = 0.999 * state.nu + 0.001 * g**2
    u = g / (sqrt(state.nu / (1 - 0.999**state.t_rms)) + 1e-20)
    state.t_mom += 1
    state.mu = 0.9 * state.mu + 0.1 * u
    m = state.mu / (1 - 0.9**state.t_mom)
    lr = 4e-5 * min(k / 1000, 1.0)                    # first update: lr = 0
    state.count += 1
    return params - lr * m, state
# then: slowval = 0.02 * val + 0.98 * slowval

docs.title: 5. Replay buffer and replay context
docs.text: Item Spec (exact) Paper ref Code ref Paper vs code Version note 5.1 Storage layout and capacity There is one append-only stream per env worker. Episodes are concatenated in the stream, and boundaries exist only as the is_first / is_last flags. Each stored step t contains: obs_t (vector keys, reward_t, is_first_t, is_last_t, is_terminal_t); the action a_t sampled after observing obs_t, zeroed by the driver if is_last_t; the policy outputs 'dyn/deter' = h_t (f32[D]) and 'dyn/stoch' = z_t (f32[32, C] one-hot) (5.7); and 'stepid' (uint8[20] = a 16-byte chunk UUID plus a 4-byte big-endian index). Storage is in chunks of 1024 steps linked by succ. An item is a start position. When step n of a worker is added and the worker's stream holds at least length steps, the item starting at n − length + 1 is inserted. Every step becomes the start of exactly one item (stride-1 overlapping windows). length = consec_train·batch_length + replay_context = 1·64 + 1 = 65. capacity = 5e6 items (not episodes). When full, the oldest item is evicted FIFO, and chunk memory is freed by refcount. A capacity check asserts batch_size·length ≤ capacity. p.18 "Experience replay"; Table 4 (replay capacity 5e6); p.20 ("Larger capacity, online queue, storing and updating latent states") embodied/core/replay.py:77-118 (add), :171-191 (insert/remove FIFO), :193-214 (getseq across chunks); embodied/core/chunk.py:41-62; dreamerv3/main.py:183-209; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:39-46 agree 2411f7d: replay length = batch_length = 65 (context included), same item semantics (1a532a7 embodied/replay/replay.py). 5.2 Sliding windows cross episode and chunk boundaries Items are the 65-step windows ending at each insert in a worker's continuous stream. They are not aligned to episodes: windows freely cross episode boundaries and chunk boundaries. A mid-sequence is_first is the normal case, and the RSSM resets the carry there (2.2). Do not restrict sampling to within-episode windows. p.18 (not explicit) embodied/core/replay.py:108-118 code_only (the paper is silent) Same at 2411f7d. 5.3 Training batch sampling and annotation B = 16 rows, sampled independently and with replacement. For each row in 'train' mode: if the online queue is non-empty, pop its oldest item (5.4); otherwise draw uniformly over all current items (Uniform selector: rng.integers(0, len(keys))). Gather 65 contiguous steps into arrays [16, 65, ...]. Annotate: is_first[:, 0] = True; is_last = is_last OR roll(is_first, −1), with the last column of the rolled array set to False. This marks the step before any mid-window is_first as last, which also covers abandoned episodes. The Consec stream (consec = 1, prefix = replay_context = 1, strict) emits the whole [16, 65] window with consec = 0 for every step. A Prefetch thread (amount = 1) prepares the next batch (6.3). With replay_context = 1, is_first[:, 0] = True has no effect on training, because index 0 is only context and its obs are dropped. It matters when replay_context = 0 (5.11). p.18: "each minibatch is formed first from non-overlapping online trajectories and then filled up with uniformly sampled trajectories from the replay buffer" embodied/core/replay.py:121-127 (sample), :151-169 (_sample), :255-275 (assemble), :277-292 (annotate); embodied/core/selectors.py:29-57; embodied/core/streams.py:89-140 (Consec), :32-86 (Prefetch); dreamerv3/main.py:261-272; embodied/jax/agent.py:326-337 agree 1a532a7 replay.dataset: same sampling and annotation; there the report dataset also popped the online queue (HEAD: train mode only). 5.4 Online queue replay.online = True. Each worker has a counter lengths[w], the number of steps it has previously added (incremented after each add). When step n (0-indexed) inserts an item (n ≥ 64) and lengths[w] % 65 == 0, i.e. n = 65, 130, …, the newly inserted item (start n − 64 = 1, 66, 131, …) is appended to a FIFO deque. This yields non-overlapping consecutive 65-step windows of the freshest data. The queue is popped only by 'train' sampling (report never pops) and is unbounded. With 16 envs it gains 16/65 ≈ 0.246 items per vector step, against 16·(train_ratio/1024)·16 rows sampled per vector step. At RR 512 that is 128 rows per vector step, so about 0.2% of rows are online (about 3% at RR 32). p.18 ("uniform replay buffer with an online queue") embodied/core/replay.py:39-42, :108-118, :158-160 agree Same push rule at 2411f7d and 1a532a7 (embodied/replay/replay.py:140-144). 5.5 Non-uniform selectors (present but disabled) fracs {uniform 1.0, priority 0.0, recency 0.0}. A Mixture is built only if fracs.uniform < 1. Prioritized(exponent 0.8, initial inf, zero_on_sample True, maxfrac 0.5, branching 16) and Recency(1/(age + 1)^1.0, branching 16) exist in the code. HEAD's agent never writes priorities (agent.py:151-152 is commented out). Implement uniform only. p.18 ("we opt for uniform replay"); Table 4 caption (no prioritised replay) dreamerv3/configs.yaml:42-45; dreamerv3/main.py:197-207; embodied/core/selectors.py:60-229; dreamerv3/agent.py:151-152 agree 2411f7d wrote priorities when fracs.priority > 0 (priosignal 'model' = rep + dyn + reconstruction loss per step). Off by default. 5.6 Eviction handling (sampling retry, partial write-back) If a popped online item or a uniformly drawn item points to an evicted chunk (KeyError in _getseq), _sample silently retries: the next queue item, or a fresh uniform draw. Latent write-back for rows whose chunk was evicted is skipped. If a successor chunk is missing, the write can stop after a partial update. none embodied/core/replay.py:156-169, :141-149, :216-235 code_only Same. 5.7 Replay context: storing latents at collection replay_context = 1. At every policy step, the RSSM posterior entry for each env, entry_t = {deter: h_t, stoch: z_t}, is returned as outs {'dyn/deter', 'dyn/stoch'} and stored with transition t. For vector obs the enc and dec entries are empty. entry_t is the state after filtering obs_t: h_t = core(h_{t−1}, z_{t−1}, a_{t−1}) (with is_first masking), and z_t is a sample (not the mode) from OneHot(logits, 0.01). Agent.ext_space adds the replay keys consec (int32), stepid (uint8[20]), dyn/deter (f32[D]) and dyn/stoch (f32[32, C]). A memory-efficient lossless equivalent is z as int32 class indices [32] and h in bf16. p.18 ("We store latent states into the replay buffer during data collection to initialize the world model on replayed trajectories") dreamerv3/agent.py:89-99 (ext_space), :115-135; dreamerv3/rssm.py:39-43 (entry_space), :75-92; embodied/core/driver.py:70-80 agree 1a532a7 and 2411f7d stored stoch as int32 argmax indices and one-hot encoded them at train time (algorithmically identical). 5.8 Replay context: RSSM initialisation at the start of a training sequence Data per row has T + K = 64 + 1 = 65 steps. _apply_replay_context with K = 1 takes the 'replay' branch whenever data['consec'][:, 0] == 0, which is always the case with consec_train = 1. carry = stored entries at index K − 1 = 0 (dyn.truncate takes entries[:, :K][:, −1]): (h_0, z_0) from the buffer, a constant with no gradient. obs = data[:, 1:65]; prevact = data[action][:, 0:64] (actions at indices 0..63 = a_{t−1} for each obs_t, so the first trained step consumes a_0); stepid = stepid[:, 1:]. The training scan then computes h_1 = core(h_0, z_0, a_0), unless is_first_1 holds (then the state and action are zeroed). Step 0 contributes no loss. Stored latents come from older params and are used as-is. See Algorithm J. p.18 ("…to initialize the world model on replayed trajectories") dreamerv3/agent.py:137-140, :312-340; dreamerv3/rssm.py:51-54 (truncate); dreamerv3/main.py:187; embodied/jax/agent.py:420, :447-457 agree 29eb964 (2024-05-15, after 2411f7d) fixed a bug: the first prevact came from the train carry, i.e. the last action of the previous, unrelated batch, instead of data[:, K − 1]. HEAD has the fix (rep_prevact = data[:, K−1:−1]). So the paper-era code 2411f7d still had the bug. 5.9 Latent write-back after each update train returns outs['replay'] = {stepid [B, T, 20] (indices 1..64), 'dyn/deter' [B, T, D], 'dyn/stoch' [B, T, 32, C]}. These are the posterior entries of the training forward pass: pre-update params, sampled posteriors, after replay-context initialisation. replay.update: for each row i, decode (chunk UUID, index) from stepid[i, 0] and overwrite the latents of the 64 consecutive steps, crossing chunk boundaries via succ. Rows whose chunk was evicted are skipped (5.6). The context step (index 0) is not overwritten by this row. Report passes never write back. Each step is refreshed roughly train_ratio times over its life. Asynchrony in the reference: the jax Agent wrapper returns the outs of the previous train call (pending_outs is fetched asynchronously). So the first update writes nothing back, update k's latents reach the buffer only after update k + 1 has run, and the final update's latents are never written. A synchronous Ajax implementation that writes back immediately is a faithful simplification (Open questions). p.18 ("and write the fresh latent states of the training rollout back into the buffer") dreamerv3/agent.py:143-150; embodied/run/train.py:76-79; embodied/core/replay.py:130-149, :216-235; embodied/jax/agent.py:286-289 agree (the delay is code_only infrastructure) Same at 2411f7d, including the delayed outs (2411f7d:dreamerv3/jaxagent.py:188-191). 5.10 Train carry threading and consec_train carry_train = (enc {}, dyn {deter, stoch} zeros, dec {}, prevact zeros) from init_train(B) is threaded through successive train calls. train returns (the final enc/dyn/dec carry of the trained window, computed with pre-update params; data[act][:, −1]). It is consumed only when consec_train > 1. In that case one sampled sequence of length consec·T + K is split into chunks [kT, kT + T + K) with consec = k. For k ≥ 1 the 'normal' branch uses the threaded carry, whose state corresponds to index K − 1 of chunk k, with obs/prevact = data[:, K:] / data[act][:, K−1:−1]. Gradients never cross chunk boundaries. Default consec_train = 1, so the threaded carry is always overridden by the replay context, and this machinery can be omitted. not described embodied/run/train.py:67, :76; dreamerv3/agent.py:109-110, :137-154, :312-340; embodied/core/streams.py:89-140; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:13-15 code_only 2411f7d: the carry was passed similarly; long-sequence splitting was replay.dataset(length) in 1a532a7. 5.11 replay_context = 0 behaviour (resolved in the merge) With replay_context = 0, _apply_replay_context returns early. The carry passed in is the previous train call's carry and prevact = concat(carry prevact, data[act][:, :−1]). However, Replay.sample always sets is_first[:, 0] = True, and _observe masks deter, stoch and prevact to zero wherever is_first holds. So the sequence starts from h_0 = core(0, 0, 0): a zero-state (DreamerV2-style) start, not a reuse of unrelated state. Use this as the fallback if Ajax's replay cannot store latents: run with replay_context = 0 and force is_first at index 0. p.18 (the paper describes only the stored-latent version) embodied/core/replay.py:126, :284-286; dreamerv3/rssm.py:75-80; dreamerv3/agent.py:316-320 code_only This corrects the world-model extractor's note, which claimed the previous batch's carry is reused.

docs.title: Algorithm J: one training step with the replay context (consec_train = 1)
docs.text:
# data: dict of [B, 65, ...] incl. obs keys, action, reward, is_first/last/terminal, dyn/deter, dyn/stoch, stepid
carry0  = dict(deter=bf16(data['dyn/deter'][:, 0]), stoch=bf16(data['dyn/stoch'][:, 0]))   # constants, no grad
obs     = {k: data[k][:, 1:] for k in obs_keys}            # [B, 64]
prevact = {k: data[k][:, 0:64] for k in act_keys}          # a_{t-1} for each obs_t
(loss, aux), grads = value_and_grad(total_loss)(params, carry0, obs, prevact)   # Algorithms E, F, G
params, opt_state = opt_update(params, grads, opt_state)   # Algorithm I
slowval = 0.02 * params.val + 0.98 * slowval
replay.update(stepid=data['stepid'][:, 1:],                # write back fresh posteriors for indices 1..64
              deter=aux.entries.deter, stoch=aux.entries.stoch)   # computed with the PRE-update params

docs.title: 6. Training loop, scheduling and infrastructure
docs.text: Item Spec (exact) Paper ref Code ref Paper vs code Version note 6.1 Train-ratio semantics and update scheduling step counts agent transitions summed over all env workers: each env contributes 1 per vector step, and action repeat is not counted. batch_steps = B·T = 16·64 = 1024 (context step excluded). should_train = Ratio(train_ratio / 1024), where Ratio(r)(step) is: if prev is None, set prev = step and return 1; otherwise repeats = floor((step − prev)·r), prev += repeats/r, return repeats. It is evaluated after every single transition. The per-transition callback order is step += 1, then replay.add, then trainfn, so updates interleave with the per-env adds inside a vector step. Gradient updates per agent step = train_ratio/1024; per env frame = train_ratio/(1024·repeat). For B = 16 and T = 64: RR 32 gives 1/32 updates per agent step (Atari, repeat 4: 1 update per 128 frames, about 1.56M updates over 200M frames); RR 64 gives 1/16; RR 128 gives 1/8; RR 256 gives 1/4; RR 512 gives 1/2 (DMC proprio: 250K agent steps × 0.5 = about 125K updates); RR 1024 gives 1. The logged replay stat 'replay_ratio' = 65·samples/inserts = (65/64)·train_ratio. The separate 'parallel' script enforces the ratio with SamplesPerInsert instead (train_ratio/batch_length samples per inserted step, tolerance 4·B, minsize B·65). p.18: replay ratio = "fraction of time steps trained on per time step collected from the environment, without action repeat. Dividing the replay ratio by the time steps in a minibatch and by action repeat yields the ratio of gradient steps to env steps" (Atari example: RR 32, repeat 4, 16 × 64 gives 1 step per 128 env steps, 1.5M over 200M) embodied/run/train.py:24-25, :59-62, :70-81; Ratio: 2411f7d:embodied/core/when.py:26-42 (HEAD imports elements.when.Ratio from the external elements package, not vendored); embodied/core/replay.py:70; embodied/run/parallel.py:242-245 agree 2411f7d: batch_steps = B·(batch_length − replay_context) = 16·(65 − 1) = 1024, identical. 6.2 Learning starts, prefill and exploration No random-action prefill and no exploration schedule. The randomly initialised actor acts from step 0 (continuous: mean ≈ 0, std ≈ 0.893). The gate: trainfn returns early until len(replay) (items) ≥ B·T = 1024. A worker yields items only after 65 steps, so with N lock-stepped envs there are N·(s − 64) items after s steps per env. With N = 16 the first update happens at s = 128, i.e. 2048 total transitions. That first eligible Ratio call returns 1 (one update); afterwards accrual is normal, with no catch-up for the prefill period. Prefetch subtlety (reference only): the train stream's Prefetch worker starts when the stream is created at setup and calls replay.sample immediately. replay.sample waits only until len(sampler) ≥ 1, not for the 1024-item gate. So the first training batch is drawn as soon as about 1 to 16 items exist (about 65 steps per env), uniformly with replacement from the earliest items, with heavy duplication. The online queue is usually still empty at that point, because the first per-worker push is at n = 65; this part is race-dependent. When training starts (2048 transitions), each worker has pushed exactly one queue item (n = 65; n = 130 is not reached), so the second batch, sampled right after the first is dequeued, is exactly the 16 online windows starting at index 1. In general batch k + 1 is sampled when batch k is dequeued, before update k runs. not specified embodied/run/train.py:64 (stream built at setup), :70-73 (gate), :93-95; embodied/jax/agent.py:337 (Prefetch); embodied/core/streams.py:44-48, :50-53, :70-77; embodied/core/replay.py:114, :121-124; 2411f7d:embodied/core/when.py:33-42 code_only 2411f7d: training started when len(replay) ≥ batch_size (16 items) and step ≥ train_fill (0), with expl_until 0 (no explore mode), so the first update came after about 65 steps per env. 6.3 Asynchrony and staleness in the reference loop (engineering, not algorithmic) (a) Acting params: only keys matching '^(enc|dyn|dec|pol)/' are copied to the policy. A train call sets pending_sync to its pre-update non-donated params (allo), but only if no sync is already pending; otherwise allo is deleted. The swap happens only after the next policy call has already run on the old params. Let θ_v be the params after all updates of driver iteration v. Policy call π_{v+1} then acts with θ_{v−2} while the trainer is at θ_v, so the acting params lag by about two driver iterations of updates (about 16 updates at RR 512 with 16 envs). (b) Batch prefetch (amount 1) samples the next batch before the current update and its latent write-back (6.2). (c) Delayed outs: both metrics and outs['replay'] are returned one train call late (5.9). None of this changes the algorithm in expectation. A synchronous Ajax loop (act with the current params, sample after the write-back, write back immediately) is a faithful simplification, but it will not reproduce the reference bit-for-bit. not in paper embodied/jax/agent.py:143-147, :229-247 (policy then swap), :264-289 (allo / pending_sync / pending_outs); embodied/jax/transform.py:78-89; embodied/core/streams.py:32-86; embodied/core/driver.py:70-80; dreamerv3/agent.py:85-87 code_only 2411f7d: policy keys '/(enc|dyn|actor)/' with a similar delayed sync, and the same delayed outs (2411f7d jaxagent.py:188-191). 6.4 Report / diagnostics stream (not part of learning) report_length 32. The report stream samples from the train replay, whose items are 65 steps long, in 'report' mode: it never pops the online queue and is not counted in the sample stats. Annotation (is_first[:, 0] = True, is_last OR next is_first) is applied to the full 65-step window. Consec(length 32, prefix 1, strict False) then slices [:, 0:33], so report windows are the first 33 steps of a 65-step train item. consec_report 1, report_batches 1, run every report_every = 300 s. It runs the loss with training = False: no normaliser updates, no param update, no latent write-back. For image keys it also makes open-loop prediction videos. Optional for Ajax. not in paper embodied/run/train.py:65, :68, :99-104; dreamerv3/main.py:261-270 (strict only for train); embodied/core/streams.py:126-133; dreamerv3/agent.py:247-310; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:12, :14, :53, :58 code_only 2411f7d: batch_length_eval 33, eval_every 180 s. 6.5 RNG seeding Param init seed = [config.seed, 0]. Policy seed per call = default_rng([config.seed, n_actions]).integers(0, 2³² − 1, (2,), uint32). Train seed per batch = the same construction with the counter n_batches. That counter is shared by the train and report Prefetch streams (both go through agent.stream), so train-batch seeds depend on how many report batches were prefetched. The replay Uniform selector rng = np.random.default_rng(0), not derived from config.seed (Replay(seed = 0) default; main.py never passes a seed); the Mixture rng also uses seed 0. XLA deterministic ops are enabled. Ajax: seed the replay sampler from config.seed and document the deviation (Open questions). not in paper embodied/jax/agent.py:332-335 (shared n_batches), :405-408, :418-419; embodied/run/train.py:64-65; embodied/core/replay.py:16-25; embodied/core/selectors.py:31-34, :202-212; embodied/jax/internal.py:45-47 code_only —

docs.title: Algorithm K: reference training loop (synchronous simplification recommended for Ajax)
docs.text:
step = 0
ratio = Ratio(train_ratio / (B * T))                  # 512 / 1024 = 0.5 for the DMC-proprio paper setting
obs = envs.reset()                                    # N = 16 envs; is_first=True, reward=0
carry = init_policy(N)                                # zeros; prevact zeros
while step < total_agent_steps:                       # 250K agent steps = 500K env steps at repeat 2
    carry, act, entries = policy(params, carry, obs)  # Algorithm B on the (N,) batch, then sample pi
    act_env = clip(act, -1, 1)                        # ClipAction then NormalizeAction
    act_store = where(obs.is_last, 0, act)            # driver zeroes actions at is_last
    for w in range(N):                                # per transition
        step += 1
        replay.add(w, {**obs[w], 'action': act_store[w], 'dyn/deter': entries.deter[w],
                       'dyn/stoch': entries.stoch[w]})
        if len(replay) >= B * T:                      # items, 1024
            for _ in range(ratio(step)):
                train_step(replay.sample(B))          # Algorithm J; online-queue pops first
    obs = envs.step(act_env, reset=obs.is_last)       # is_last envs are reset; next obs is_first

docs.title: 7. Acting, environment protocol, benchmark configurations and sanity targets
docs.text: Item Spec (exact) Paper ref Code ref Paper vs code Version note 7.1 Act-time computation (collection policy) Batched over N envs per vector step. carry = (enc {}, dyn {deter [N, D] bf16, stoch [N, 32, C] bf16}, dec {}, prevact). reset = obs['is_first']. tokens = enc(obs) (symlog vector obs, then the 3-layer MLP). RSSM._observe (Algorithm B): deter, stoch and prevact are masked to 0 where reset; prevact is one-hot encoded (discrete) and masked again; h_t = core(...); posterior logits from concat(h_t, tokens); z_t sampled from OneHot(logits, 0.01). feat = concat(h_t, flatten(z_t)). a_t ~ π(· ∣ feat), SAMPLED. New carry = (..., {deter: h_t, stoch: z_t}, ..., a_t as the raw sample). The decoder is not run at act time. Outputs: actions to the env, entries to the replay (5.7). The carried prevact is the raw sample even at is_last steps (the driver zeroes only the stored and sent action). This is harmless, because the next obs is is_first and masking zeroes it. Eq. 1 p.4; p.5 ("For environment interaction, we select actions by sampling from the actor network without lookahead planning") dreamerv3/agent.py:101-107, :115-135; dreamerv3/rssm.py:61-92, :135-159; embodied/jax/agent.py:219-261; embodied/core/driver.py:56-83 agree 1a532a7 policy: the same filter and sample. 7.2 is_first resets and episode protocol (driver) The initial acts are zeros with reset = True for all envs. env.step({..., reset: True}) returns the first obs (is_first = True, reward = 0, is_terminal = False). After each policy call, actions for envs with is_last are multiplied by 0, so a zero action is stored in the replay at the is_last step. reset = True is sent at the next step, whose obs is is_first of a new episode in the same worker stream. RSSM masking is described in 2.2. is_terminal = (dm_env discount == 0) and is False on first steps. DMC time-limit ends give is_last = True and is_terminal = False. not detailed embodied/core/driver.py:35-40, :70-80; dreamerv3/rssm.py:75-80; embodied/jax/nets.py:67-77; embodied/envs/from_dm.py:51-78 code_only 1a532a7 nets.RSSM.observe: jaxutils.reset((deter, stoch, action), reset) before _gru. Same. 7.3 Eval mode Agent.policy ignores its mode argument. 'train', 'eval' and 'report' all sample the actor (no mean or argmax action) and sample posteriors. The default 'train' script logs episode/score from the training envs (stochastic policy, 16 envs). train_eval adds eval envs (eval_envs 4, eval_eps 1 per eval) using the same sampling policy and a separate eval replay of capacity size/10. not specified dreamerv3/agent.py:115, :126; embodied/run/train.py:93; embodied/run/train_eval.py:126-134; embodied/run/eval_only.py:64; dreamerv3/main.py:186; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:56-57 code_only 1a532a7 Agent.policy also ignored mode (always sample). 7.4 Action handling at the env boundary Continuous ('bounded_normal', 3.13): sample a = μ + σ·ε in f32, not squashed. Env side: wrap_env applies NormalizeAction (maps [−1, 1] to [low, high]) and then ClipAction (outermost, clips to [−1, 1]) to every continuous key. The replay stores the UNCLIPPED sample. RSSM input: a / sg(max(1, abs(a))). Discrete ('categorical' at HEAD, 3.14): Categorical(logits).sample gives an int index, with no unimix at HEAD; it is one-hot (bf16) for the RSSM. p.18 (actor unimix, discrete only) embodied/jax/heads.py:101-110, :146-155; embodied/jax/outs.py:161-186, :208-241; dreamerv3/configs.yaml:100-103; dreamerv3/main.py:249-258; embodied/core/wrappers.py:76-110; dreamerv3/rssm.py:137 conflict for discrete actions only (unimix). The continuous parameterisation is code_only. 2411f7d: discrete 'onehot' with unimix 0.01 (straight-through one-hot, argmax index sent to the env); continuous 'normal' with the same maths as bounded_normal (1a532a7 nets.py:486-493). 7.5 DMC proprio environment protocol Paper protocol: 18 tasks (all 20 visual-control tasks minus quadruped walk/run), action repeat 2, 500K env steps (= 250K agent steps), 16 env instances, replay ratio 512 (0.5 updates per agent step, 0.25 per env step, about 125K updates in total), 12M model, about 0.3 A100 GPU-days. Observation: every key of the dm_control observation dict becomes its own vector input ('/' → '_'), float64 → float32 (UnifyDtypes), symlogged in the encoder. Action space [−1, 1].
