docs.title: Shared building blocks
docs.text:
• BlockLinear init uses fan_in = the full input width I, not the per-block width I/g, because compute_fans multiplies the per-block fan by g. A per-block fan-in makes the GRU weights sqrt(8) ≈ 2.83× too large at init.
  • Every hidden Linear keeps its bias, even when RMSNorm follows. RMSNorm: eps 1e-4, statistics in f32, learnable scale only (no shift), output cast back to the activation dtype.
  • outscale applies only to the final head Linear; hidden layers always use 1.0. Policy 0.01 (mean and std Linears), reward 0.0, value 0.0, continue 1.0, RSSM logits 1.0, vector decoder 1.0 (HEAD) or 0.1 (2411f7d). Biases are always zero-initialised.
  • Two-hot: 255 bins built from a mirrored half for exact antisymmetry. Interpolation is linear in raw space between symexp-spaced bins, and targets are not symlogged. The expectation must use the symmetric pairwise sum, or the reward and value predictions are not exactly 0 at init. Targets must be f32.
  • Unimix (1%) is re-applied every time a categorical is built from logits, including inside both KL terms after the sg and when sampling. The straight-through estimator uses the mixed probabilities: sample = sg(onehot) + p_mix − sg(p_mix). Store raw logits.
  • DictConcat availability masking is all-or-nothing per key and per sample. Keys are sorted alphabetically. Discrete keys are one-hot encoded and never symlogged.
  • bf16 compute: Linear outputs, the RSSM carry and the GRU maths are bf16. Norm statistics, distributions, losses, returns and normalisers are f32. An all-f32 Ajax implementation changes numerics only. Note that if Ajax computes in f32, storing replay latents as bf16 is no longer lossless.

docs.title: World model
docs.text:
• Core: the RMSNorm after dynhid0 runs over the full D vector, not per block, and dyngru has no norm and no activation. GRU convention: deter' = u·cand + (1 − u)·deter, with u = sigmoid(u_pre − 1) and cand = tanh(sigmoid(r_pre)·cand_pre). The per-block gate layout is [r, c, u] within each block's 3D/g chunk; this matters only for official-weight compatibility.
  • is_first: zero deter, stoch and the previous action before the core, and zero the action again after one-hot encoding. h at an episode start is core(0, 0, 0). There is no learned initial state in the revised recipe. World-model losses at is_first steps are not masked.
  • KL: free bits clamp max(Σ_latents KL, 1.0) per (b, t), not per latent, and both dyn and rep are clamped. Both are KL(post ‖ prior); the sg goes on post for dyn and on prior for rep. The prior is computed from the same h_t that conditioned the posterior, in parallel after the scan, and h_t is not stop-gradiented, so dyn also trains the core and everything upstream (merge correction, 2.14).
  • Decoder: the input order is concat(stoch_flat, deter), while reward, continue, actor and critic use concat(deter, stoch_flat). The loss per key is the sum of squared errors over the feature dims against symlog(target), with no ½. Each obs key is its own loss term (scale 1), mean-reduced over (B, T).
  • Encoder: symlog only continuous keys. The tokens are the output of the 3rd Linear → RMSNorm → SiLU block, with no extra projection.
  • Action input to the dynamics is a / sg(max(1, abs(a))). The replay stores the unclipped policy sample; env clipping happens in a wrapper.
  • Stoch is sampled, not the mode, when acting, training and imagining.
  • Continue target = 0.997·(1 − is_terminal), a soft label. Truncations (is_last without is_terminal) are not zero targets. Never use is_last for this target.
  • Reward target = raw reward of the step that entered x_t (0 at is_first), not squashed.
  • Unused rssm.py class defaults (gelu, deter 4096, hidden 2048, classes 32) must not leak in. Use silu and the size-preset values.

docs.title: Actor-critic
docs.text:
• Targets and advantages bootstrap from the ONLINE critic (slowtar = False overrides the function default True). The slow critic is only a regulariser: two-hot cross-entropy toward its scalar mean, weight 1.0, in both the imagination and replay critic losses.
  • λ-return at step t uses r̂, ĉ and v of the NEXT state s_{t+1}, and r̂_0 is unused. Paper Eq. 5 literally indexes v_t; follow the code. lambda_return's val argument is never used.
  • The continuation weight w_t = Π_{i≤t} ĉ_i includes ĉ_0 of the start state. Slice weight[:, :−1] to align it with R_0..R_{H−1}. With contdisc the imagination recursion uses disc = 1. The replay recursion always uses γ = 1 − 1/333 with hard flags.
  • Return normaliser: update the EMAs of P5 and P95 first, then compute S = max(1, hi − lo) for the same batch. lo and hi start at 0 with no debias. Percentiles use linear interpolation over the flattened (B·K·H) = 15360 imagined returns, with no mask and no weights. Divide the advantage by S and do not subtract the offset.
  • Reinforce for both action types: log_prob of sg(sampled action). Continuous: Normal(tanh(μ), 0.9·sigmoid(s + 2) + 0.1), unsquashed samples and log-probs, no tanh-Jacobian term, entropy of the unsquashed Normal.
  • Imagined features are stop-gradiented (start feat via ac_grads = False, imagined feats always), so the actor and imagination critic never update the world model. The replay critic (repval) is not stop-gradiented and trains enc/dyn with scale 0.3. Its mask is ~is_last at the trained state, with no continuation product. Episode boundaries are cut by cont = λ(1 − is_last_{t+1}) and live = γ(1 − is_terminal_{t+1}).
  • Batch-major flattening of imagination starts (b major, t minor) is required for boot = R_imag[:, 0].reshape(B, K) to line up with the replay rows.
  • Reductions are means, not sums. Policy and value: mean over H, then over B·K. repval: mean over B·(T − 1). Weighted-out and masked entries still count in the denominator. The final states (imagination index H, replay index T − 1) receive no loss.
  • Normaliser EMA updates happen inside the loss forward pass and must be skipped in evaluation and report passes.
  • The policy samples stochastically in every mode; there is no deterministic eval action in the reference.

docs.title: Optimizer and loss assembly
docs.text:
• Optimizer order: AGC per tensor (0.3·max(1e-3, ‖p‖)) on the raw gradients, then RMS (β₂ 0.999, eps 1e-20 after the sqrt, bias-corrected), then momentum on the normalised update (β₁ 0.9, bias-corrected, its own step counter), then −lr. One optimizer covers all modules; the slow-critic EMA runs after the step.
  • The LR warms up linearly from 0 over 1000 updates, so the first update has lr = 0 (a no-op on the params, but the moments accumulate). This is code-only; the paper says "no annealing".
  • The AGC cap on zero-initialised tensors (gradient norm ≤ 3e-4 while ‖p‖ = 0) does not slow them: a constant clip factor cancels in the RMS normalisation.
  • Total loss = Σ scale·mean(term). Each vector obs key is its own rec term with weight 1. The loss must be an f32 scalar.

docs.title: Replay, replay context and loop
docs.text:
• Replay windows: an item at every start index (stride 1), length 65 = 64 trained steps + 1 context step. Windows cross episode and chunk boundaries. Do not restrict them to within-episode windows; the RSSM handles boundaries through is_first masking.
  • Batch annotation: is_first[:, 0] = True, and is_last = is_last OR (next step is_first), with the last column excluded. The repval mask relies on this.
  • Context alignment: the carry comes from the latent stored at index 0. The first trained obs is index 1. prevact for obs index t is the action stored at index t − 1 (data[act][:, 0:64]). Step 0 contributes no loss and is not overwritten by the write-back.
  • Stored per step: obs_t; a_t, the action chosen after seeing obs_t (zero if is_last_t); h_t and z_t, the posterior after filtering obs_t. After every update, write back the training-pass posteriors (pre-update params) for indices 1..64.
  • Online queue: per worker, push the item whose insertion happens at step n with n % 65 == 0 (starts 1, 66, 131, …). Train sampling pops it FIFO before uniform sampling; report sampling never pops.
  • The train-ratio clock counts agent transitions over all envs (not env frames). Updates per agent step = RR/(16·64). Evaluate after every transition. The first eligible call does exactly one update. Training starts once ≥ 1024 items exist (2048 transitions with 16 envs). There is no random prefill.
  • Capacity never binds for DMC proprio: 250K agent transitions ≪ 5e6 items, so FIFO eviction and the eviction retry never trigger there. A preallocated per-env ring of about 15.7K steps × 16 envs holds the entire run.
  • Memory for stored latents at 12M: D + 32·C = 2560 floats per step (10 KB in f32). Lossless compact storage is stoch as uint8 class indices [32] (C = 16 < 256) plus deter in bf16 (lossless only when compute is bf16), about 4.1 KB per step, or about 1 GB for 250K steps.
  • Functional, on-device replay design for Ajax (pure-JAX):
  • Per-env ring buffers [N_env, L_cap] with flags.
  • Valid starts are positions with 64 later steps in the same env stream.
  • Draw a uniform start index, gather 65 steps, and scatter the latent write-back at (env, start + 1 .. start + 64).
  • Emulate the online queue with a per-env pointer to the next unconsumed non-overlapping window (starts 1, 66, …), consumed before uniform draws.
  • Engineering staleness in the reference (acting params about two driver iterations stale, one-batch prefetch, outs and write-back delayed by one train call, replay RNG fixed at seed 0) is not algorithmic. A synchronous Ajax loop is a faithful simplification; document it as a deviation.
  • Scores: the reference reports training-episode returns of the stochastic policy. Paper Table 11's "Task mean" and "Task median" rows are swapped. Use mean ≈ 754 and median ≈ 871 at 500K env steps as the DMC-proprio sanity target, and mean ≈ 675 / median ≈ 790 at 250K env steps from the bundled curves.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
Each question gives the recommended default in the final table in bold. The user's call is needed where marked.

Resolved since: the user's answers are the fidelity rule of DESIGN.md §0 and the choices in deviations.md §1 and §3, which win over the recommendations below (notably 6 and 7, where Ajax follows 2411f7d).

  1. DMC-proprio protocol (user call). The paper (Table 2) and 2411f7d use size12m, replay ratio 512, action repeat 2, 16 envs and 500K env steps. 2411f7d actually ran 3e5 agent steps = 600K env steps. HEAD (since f8817c4, Dec 2024) uses size1m, ratio 1024, repeat 1 and 1.1M env steps. This choice fixes every network width. Reproducing Table 11 needs the paper / 2411f7d setting. Recommended: paper (12M / 512 / repeat 2 / 500K).
  2. LaProp β₂ (user call). The paper text says 0.99 ("its default parameters"); both code versions use 0.999, which produced the published curves. The LaProp reference's own defaults were not verified here (no literature fetch). Recommended: 0.999, with 0.99 as a config option.
  3. Symlog MSE ½ factor. Paper Eq. 8 has ½; both code versions have none, so the code's reconstruction gradient is 2× the paper formula's. Recommended: code (no ½).
  4. Continue head target. The paper uses a binary c_t with γ applied in the return; both code versions use the soft label 0.997·(1 − terminal) with γ folded in (contdisc = True). The returns are equivalent in expectation. Recommended: code (contdisc = True).
  5. Discrete actor unimix. The paper (p.18, Table 4) and 2411f7d use 1%; HEAD's 'categorical' head drops it. This does not affect DMC, only discrete-action tasks. Recommended: 1% (paper), as a head option.
  6. Start-state continuation and reward in imagination. HEAD uses the predicted ĉ_0 (≈ 0.997) in the weight. 2411f7d used the replay flag 1 − is_terminal (hard, without the 0.997 factor) and the replayed reward. The effect is a constant factor of about 0.997 on all actor-critic weights, plus different handling of terminal start states. The paper is silent. Recommended: HEAD.
  7. Vector decoder output outscale. HEAD uses 1.0; 2411f7d (paper era) effectively used 0.1, a 10× init difference. The paper is silent. Recommended: HEAD 1.0, unless strict paper-era fidelity is preferred.
  8. Table 3 12M recurrent units. The paper prints 1024, which contradicts its own 8d rule; both code versions use 2048. Recommended: 2048 (treat as a typo).
  9. Replay context in Ajax (user call). The replay context needs a replay that stores per-step latents (2560 floats per step at 12M) and supports write-back by step id. If Ajax's on-device replay cannot provide this, the deviation must be chosen. The clean fallback is the official replay_context = 0 behaviour, which is a zero-state start (is_first forced at index 0; see 5.11), not a reuse of stale state. Burn-in is another option. Recommended: implement it (it is part of the paper).
  10. Compute dtype (user call). The reference uses bf16 compute with f32 params, norms, distributions and losses. Should Ajax replicate bf16 (GPU-oriented) or default to f32 for CPU benchmarks and reproducibility? Recommended: a dtype option; f32 default for CPU tests, bf16 on GPU.
  11. Asynchrony. Should Ajax reproduce the reference's acting-param lag (about two driver iterations), one-batch prefetch, one-call-delayed write-back and early first batch? The paper does not specify these. Recommended: synchronous, documented as a deviation.
  12. Replay sampler seed. The reference fixes it to 0, independent of config.seed. Recommended: derive it from config.seed (documented deviation).
  13. What Table 11 scores measure. The paper does not say whether they are training-episode returns of the stochastic policy (what the default train script logs) or separate evaluation episodes, and the code has no deterministic eval mode. Recommended: log training-episode returns as the primary metric, plus optional sampled-policy eval episodes.
  14. Replay windows crossing episode boundaries. The code does this; the paper is silent. Recommended: follow the code.
  15. elements.when.Ratio at HEAD comes from the external elements package, which is not available locally. Its semantics are taken from the 2411f7d code it was moved from, so a later change in that package cannot be ruled out. Low risk.
  16. Online queue in a functional replay. The paper lists it as a component. A per-env "next non-overlapping window" pointer reproduces it. Its effect is small (about 0.2% of rows at RR 512 after the start-up batches). Recommended: implement it, behind a flag.

docs.title: Shared building blocks for DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 in Ajax
docs.text:
This spec lists the modular blocks that DreamerV3 (D3) and TD-MPC2 (T2) need. Each block is designed once, as a pure-functional JAX function or a flax.linen module, with a parameterisation that reproduces both references exactly. For each block it gives:

  • the math;
  • the single signature that covers both papers;
  • which paper uses which variant;
  • unit tests pinned against the reference formulas.

It also flags false friends: blocks that look shared but differ in a way that matters.

Status: the pre-implementation spec (M0), kept as the design record. The code follows DESIGN.md §3 (what was built, and where), §4.2-4.3 and deviations.md, which win where they differ from this file. The departures: - Names and layout: no src/ajax/blocks/ package and none of the proposed TwoHotSpec, twohot_*, PercentileScaleConfig or mppi_plan APIs. The shared blocks are ajax.distributional (symlog, symexp, TwoHot), ajax.normalizers (ReturnNormalizer, RunningScale) and ajax.networks.blocks (linear, NormedMLP); the rest is agent-local. - B4: NormedMLP(layers, units, act, norm, norm_eps, kernel_init, dropout) has no output layer (compose it with linear) and no dtype (Ajax computes in f32, D4). - B5: DreamerV3's initialiser is flax variance_scaling (trunc_normal_fan_in), not the literal 1.1368, so its draws match the reference's to 4.16e-5 relative, not exactly (D23); TD-MPC2's is the "normal(0.02)" initializer. - B1 test 4 and B9's dropout rows were wrong about the references: see the notes there. - B13, B14, B19: the planner (agents/TDMPC2/planner.py) takes its random draws as an explicit PlanNoise (draw_plan_noise), scans over the iterations and unrolls the H-step rollouts in Python, and draws the elite with sample_elite, the paper-era inverse CDF of one uniform (np.random.choice), not jax.random.categorical (DESIGN.md §4.3, deviations.md §2). There is no shared rollout helper: DreamerV3's observe and imagine steps are their own scans.

docs.title: 0. Sources and conventions
docs.text:
• D3 spec: dreamerv3_spec.md (this directory), cited as D3§x.y. It pins danijar/dreamerv3 @ e3f0224 (paper-era 2411f7d) and arXiv:2301.04104v2.
  • T2 spec: tdmpc2_spec.md (this directory), cited as T2§x.y. It pins nicklashansen/tdmpc2 @ e9f5932 (HEAD) and 5f6fade (PE), and arXiv:2310.16828v2.
  • Re-checked against the reference code (both official repositories at the commits pinned in the two specs):
  • D3: embodied/jax/{outs,heads,nets,opt,utils}.py and dreamerv3/agent.py:480-488 (lambda_return).
  • T2: tdmpc2/common/{math,scale,init,layers}.py, tdmpc2/tdmpc2.py:208-230 (update_pi) and common/world_model.py:186-216 (Q).
  • Pinned numbers. Every number in the test lists below was computed by the reference translations shipped with the block tests (tests/world_models/reference_impls.py), which contains literal translations of the reference functions: D3 is already JAX, and T2's torch code is translated to numpy line for line. The environment was Ajax's locked one: jax 0.7.2, flax 0.10.7, optax 0.2.6. Unless stated otherwise, the tolerance is rtol 1e-6 in f32.
  • Ajax conventions this spec assumes (from CLAUDE.md and the codebase):
  • flax.linen modules plus pure functions.
  • Hyperparameters live in frozen dataclasses.
  • No per-feature kwargs on agents: optional behaviour is an Extension.
  • Tests ship with every block.
  • Existing pieces this spec reuses or warns against: LoadedTrainState.soft_update (optax.incremental_update), networks.MultiCritic (nn.vmap ensemble), networks.memory._mask_reset, PQN compute_q_lambda_targets, SAC SquashedNormal, networks.utils.get_adam_tx, buffers.utils.get_buffer (flashbax).

docs.title: B1. symlog / symexp
docs.text:
Math. - symlog(x) = sign(x)·log1p(abs(x)) - symexp(x) = sign(x)·expm1(abs(x))

The two are mutual inverses, odd functions, with symlog'(0) = 1.

Signature. symlog(x) -> x, symexp(x) -> x. Elementwise, dtype-preserving, pure.

Variants. D3 uses log1p/expm1 (nets.py:59-64; D3§1.6). T2 uses log(1 + abs(x)) and exp(abs(x)) − 1 (math.py:42-55; T2§1.14). These agree to rounding, so use log1p/expm1.

False friend: what each paper symlogs. - D3 symlogs continuous vector observations (encoder, in f32 before the bf16 cast) and decoder targets (symlog-MSE). It also builds the two-hot bins with symexp. D3 does not symlog two-hot targets. - T2 symlogs only inside two-hot (reward and Q targets). It never symlogs observations or latents (T2§1.4, T2§1.14).

Tests. 1. symlog([−1000, −1, −0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 1000]) = [−6.908755, −0.6931472, −0.4054651, 0, 0.4054651, 0.6931472, 6.908755]. 2. symexp(symlog(x)) == x at rtol 1e-6 on that vector. 3. Oddness: symlog(−x) == −symlog(x) exactly. 4. grad(symlog)(0.0) == 1.0, and grad(symexp)(0.0) == 1.0. Wrong: at exactly 0 both references give 0 (sign(0) = 0); the slope is 1 only next to 0 (test_symlog_gradient_matches_reference). 5. bf16 in gives bf16 out.

docs.title: B2. Two-hot discrete regression (encode, decode, soft-CE, head)
Math (generic, any sorted bins b_0 < … < b_{K−1})
docs.text:
Encode a target y (after transform): - below = clip(#{b ≤ y} − 1, 0, K−1) - above = clip(K − #{b > y}, 0, K−1) - If below == above, put weight 1 on that bin. This covers out-of-range targets, which go to the edge bin. - Otherwise: w_below = abs(b_above − y)/(b_above − b_below) and w_above = 1 − w_below.

This is Dreamer's TwoHot.loss algorithm (outs.py:311-330). For uniformly spaced bins it equals T2's floor formula exactly: k = floor((y − vmin)/δ), o = frac, t[k] = 1 − o, t[k+1] = o (math.py:58-71). An exact bin hit puts weight 1 on that bin in both.

Soft-CE: −Σ_k encode(sg(y))_k · log_softmax(logits)_k. D3 writes this as logits − logsumexp; T2 as F.log_softmax. They are the same.

Decode: - p = softmax(logits). - m = (K−1)/2 (K odd). - E = p_m·b_m + Σ_{i<m} (p_i·b_i reversed + p_{m+1+i}·b_{m+1+i}). This is the symmetric sum, which gives exactly 0 for uniform p. - Return inverse_transform(E).

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TwoHotSpec:
    bins: tuple[float, ...]           # sorted, odd K, antisymmetric, bins[K//2] == 0, in INTERPOLATION space
    transform: Literal["identity", "symlog"]   # applied to targets before encoding; inverse applied after expectation

def twohot_encode(y, spec) -> f32[..., K]
def twohot_decode(logits, spec) -> f32[...]
def twohot_ce(logits, y, spec) -> f32[...]          # target stop-gradiented inside
class TwoHotHead(nn.Module): spec; out_kernel_init (zeros by default)   # Linear(K), logits in f32

def dreamer_twohot_spec(K=255, limit=20.0):          # half = symexp(linspace(-limit, 0, (K+1)//2)); bins = concat(half, -half[:-1][::-1])
    return TwoHotSpec(bins, "identity")
def tdmpc2_twohot_spec(K=101, vmin=-10.0, vmax=10.0): # mirrored linspace(vmin, 0, (K+1)//2), transform symlog
    return TwoHotSpec(bins, "symlog")

Build both bin sets by mirroring a half, so that bins[K//2] == 0 and antisymmetry hold exactly.

docs.text:
D3 (D3§1.9, Algorithm D; heads.py:132-144; outs.py:273-330) T2 (T2§1.15-1.17; math.py:5-9, 58-83) Bins 255, symexp(linspace(−20, 20)) in raw space; range ±4.85e8 101, linspace(−10, 10) in symlog space; step 0.2; raw range ±22025 Target transform none (raw reward or return) symlog, then clamp to [−10, 10] Interpolation linear in raw space linear in symlog space Decode E_p[raw bins], symmetric sum symexp(E_p[symlog bins]), naive sum Head init zero kernel and bias (reward and value) zero final weight (reward and every Q member), bias 0 Users reward head, critic (imagination and replay losses) reward head, Q ensemble, TD targets, planner

Deviation: use the symmetric sum for T2 as well. In symlog space the difference from T2's naive sum is ≤ 1e-6. Mirrored bins differ from torch.linspace by at most 1 ulp.

docs.title: False friends
docs.text:
1. Interpolation space. For y = 1.0, D3's bin pair (131, 132) = (0.8775, 1.1977) gets upper weight 0.3827 with raw-space interpolation. Symlog-space interpolation on the same pair would give 0.4015. The targets differ even on identical bins.
  2. Decode order. symexp(E[b]) ≠ E[symexp(b)]. Do not "simplify" one into the other.
  3. Range. T2 saturates at abs(y) ≈ 22025. That is harmless for DMC (abs(Q) ≤ 200 at γ = 0.99), but not for large-return tasks.
  4. K must be ≥ 2. T2's num_bins ∈ {0, 1} modes are broken (T2§1.18), so do not port them.

docs.title: B3. Percentile scale normaliser (D3 retnorm vs T2 RunningScale)
Math (unified)
docs.text:
r ← (1 − τ)·r + τ·g(P_hi(x) − P_lo(x)), then S = max(floor, r). Here:

  • P is jnp.percentile(method="linear") over all elements of sg(f32(x)).
  • The update happens before the read, so the current batch already counts.
  • There is no debias.

docs.text:

    clamp_before_ema: bool          # g = max(floor, .) if True else identity
    init: float                      # initial r

@struct.dataclass
class PercentileScaleState: r: f32[]   # (+ optional lo/hi EMAs for logging only)

def percentile_scale_update(state, x, cfg) -> state
def percentile_scale(state, cfg) -> f32[]       # max(floor, r)

Because the EMA is linear and both start at 0, this is exactly the EMA of hi − lo. scalar value Checkpointed yes (ninjax variable) no (resets to 1 on reload)

docs.title: False friend
docs.text:
The papers describe the same thing ("EMA of the 5 to 95 percentile range, floored at 1"). The configurations still differ:

  • T2 clamps before the EMA; D3 clamps after.
  • D3 starts at 0; T2 starts at 1.
  • They normalise different quantities over different data.

Tests (pinned). Feed batches x_i = arange(256)·s, with s ∈ {0.001, 0.01, 1, 10}. The 5-95 ranges are 0.2295, 2.295, 229.5 and 2295.

after batch 1 after batch 2 after batch 3 after batch 4 D3 S 1.0 1.0 2.3199697 25.246771 T2 S 1.0 1.01295 3.2978203 26.214842

Also, after batch 4 the D3 lo/hi EMAs are 1.4025983 and 26.649368.

Further case D3 S T2 S Constant range 50, after 100 updates 31.698427 32.064415 Ranges alternating 0 and 3, after 2000 updates 1.50753 2.00502

The alternating case pins down clamp-before vs clamp-after.

docs.title: B4. NormedMLP (Linear, then Dropout, then Norm, then Act, plus an optional output layer)
Math (per hidden layer i)
docs.text:
h ← act(Norm(Dropout_{p·[i==0]}(h W_i + b_i))). The bias is always present. Dropout is the inverted kind and is active only when not deterministic.

Output layer, one of: - none (the trunk output is the result); - plain Linear; - Linear, then Norm, then out_act (T2's encoder and dynamics end with LayerNorm then SimNorm).

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
class NormedMLP(nn.Module):
    hidden: Sequence[int]
    out: int | tuple | None = None       # None -> no output layer (D3 encoder tokens)
    out_norm_act: Callable | None = None # None -> plain Linear output; e.g. simnorm -> Linear->Norm->SimNorm
    norm: Literal["rms", "layer", "none"] = "rms"
    norm_eps: float = 1e-4
    act: Callable = jax.nn.silu
    dropout: float = 0.0                 # first hidden layer only
    kernel_init: Initializer = dreamer_trunc_normal()
    out_kernel_init: Initializer = dreamer_trunc_normal(outscale=1.0)
    dtype: Any = jnp.float32             # compute dtype (bf16 for D3 on GPU)
    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, deterministic: bool = True): ...

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• D3 (D3§1.1-1.4; nets.py:230-251, 361-409, 565-587):
  • norm="rms", norm_eps=1e-4, act=silu, dropout=0.
  • RMSNorm: f32 statistics, learnable scale only (no shift), output cast back to the compute dtype.
  • Flax mapping: nn.RMSNorm(epsilon=1e-4, dtype=compute_dtype). Verified 0.0 max abs difference from the D3 formula in both f32 and bf16.
  • The input is cast to the compute dtype, and leading dims are flattened, then restored.
  • Heads apply outscale to the output layer only.
  • T2 (T2§1.1-1.2; layers.py:94-133):
  • norm="layer", norm_eps=1e-5, act=jax.nn.mish.
  • dropout=0.01 only for Q members, on the first layer only.
  • Flax mapping: nn.LayerNorm(epsilon=1e-5, use_fast_variance=False), with learnable γ and β.
  • The output layer is plain Linear for reward, Q and π, and Linear → LN → SimNorm for the encoder and dynamics.

Configurations used (d = 256 at D3 12M; mlp = 512, enc = 256 and L = 512 at T2 5M):

Network hidden out other D3 encoder [d]×3 None — D3 reward / continue head [d]×1 head — D3 policy / value [d]×3 head — D3 decoder [d]×3 per-key heads — D3 RSSM prior [d]×2 S·C — D3 RSSM posterior [d]×1 S·C — T2 encoder [enc]×max(n−1, 1) L out_norm_act = simnorm T2 dynamics [mlp]×2 L out_norm_act = simnorm T2 reward / Q [mlp]×2 101 Q: dropout 0.01 T2 π [mlp]×2 2A —

docs.title: False friends
docs.text:
1. Flax defaults are wrong for both papers.
  2. nn.LayerNorm defaults to eps 1e-6 with fast variance E[x²] − E[x]². With mean-1000 inputs that gives a max error of 2.2e-2, against 3.9e-5 with use_fast_variance=False.
  3. nn.RMSNorm defaults to eps 1e-6, and with dtype=None a bf16 input gives an f32 output.
  4. D3 has no shift on RMSNorm. Do not use LayerNorm with eps 1e-4 for D3. The D3 'layer' implementation exists in the code but is unused.
  5. Dropout sits before the norm in T2. It is not after the activation.
  6. Ajax's existing Encoder and parse_architecture add an optional output LayerNorm or L2 norm and use an orthogonal init. Neither paper does this, so do not reuse them.

Expression Expected RMSNorm([1, 2, 3, 4]), eps 1e-4 [0.36514595, 0.7302919, 1.0954379, 1.4605838] LayerNorm([1, 2, 3, 4]), eps 1e-5 [−1.3416355, −0.44721183, 0.44721183, 1.3416355] silu(1), silu(−1) 0.7310586, −0.2689414 mish(1), mish(−1) 0.8650984, −0.3034015

def dreamer_trunc_normal(outscale=1.0):   # W = outscale * 1.1368 * sqrt(1/fan_in) * TruncNormal(-2, 2) (unit sigma), f32
def normal_init(std=0.02, outscale=1.0)   # T2: W = outscale * N(0, std^2)
# fan_in: rank2 (in,out) -> in;  rank>=3 -> shape[-2]*prod(shape[:-2])  (D3 compute_fans == flax variance_scaling in_axis=-2)
# biases: zeros (both); norm scale: ones (both); LN shift: zeros (T2); T2 task embedding: U(-0.02, 0.02) (Ajax uniform_init)

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• D3 (D3§1.5; nets.py:144-197): trunc-normal fan-in for every Linear, BlockLinear and Conv. Output outscales:
Output layer outscale reward 0 value 0 policy (mean, std or logits) 0.01 continue 1 RSSM logits 1 decoder 1 at HEAD; 0.1 at 2411f7d

The slow critic starts as an exact copy of the critic. - T2 (T2§1.13; init.py): - N(0, 0.02) for all Linears. Torch trunc_normal_(std=.02, a=-2, b=2) has absolute bounds of ±100σ, so it is effectively untruncated. - Zero final weight for the reward head and for every Q member. - π, encoder, dynamics and termination heads are not zeroed. - Each Q member gets its own key. - The target Q is cloned after the zeroing.

docs.text:
1. jax.nn.initializers.truncated_normal(0.02) is wrong for T2. It truncates at ±2σ = ±0.04 with no std correction (std 0.0176 in jax 0.7.2). Use normal(0.02), which gives std 0.02.
  2. flax lecun_normal is D3's distribution up to a constant. Flax's 1/0.87962566 = 1.1368472 differs from D3's literal 1.1368 by 4.2e-5 relative (max abs difference 5.9e-6 at the same key). Use a 3-line custom initialiser with the literal constant so parity tests are exact. (Not built: Ajax uses flax's constant, D23.)
  3. Ajax parse_layer defaults to orthogonal(1.0). Neither paper uses it.

  2. BlockLinear kernel (8, 1024, 256): fan_in = 8192 and std ≈ 0.011048.

  4. The zeroed heads have all-zero kernel and bias. Every two-hot head then decodes to 0.

docs.title: B6. BlockLinear (D3 only)
docs.text:
Math. Kernel W has shape (g, I/g, U/g) and the bias has shape (U,). The output is y = einsum('...ki,kio->...ko', x.reshape(..., g, I/g), W).reshape(..., U) + b. Init fan_in = I, the full width (B5). Used in the GRU core: dynhid0 with U = D and dyngru with U = 3D (D§2.4).

Signature. BlockLinear(features: int, blocks: int) (agent-local in agents/DreamerV3/networks.py, DESIGN.md §3). The kernel init is fixed to B5's fan-in truncated normal at outscale 1: the reference's RSSM builds dyn0 and dyncore with BlockLinear's default outscale (29eb964 nets.py:161-166), and its only other BlockLinear, the image decoder's space0, is out of scope. f32 only (D4).

Tests. 1. The Jacobian block (output k, input j) is zero for j ≠ k. 2. The result equals a dense layer with a block-diagonal kernel. 3. 12M shapes: dynhid (8, 1024, 256); dyngru (8, 256, 768). 4. Init std as in B5.

docs.title: B7. Grouped softmax: SimNorm (T2) vs categorical latents (D3), a false friend
docs.text:
Shared primitive. grouped_softmax(x, group) = softmax(x.reshape(..., D/group, group), -1).reshape(..., D).

  • T2 SimNorm (T2§1.3; layers.py:74-91): group V = 8, τ = 1, deterministic. Placed after the LayerNorm at the end of the encoder and the dynamics. The probabilities are the latent: there is no sampling and no unimix. Paper Eq. 5 divides by τ, while the App. H prose describes the opposite. If τ is exposed, use Eq. 5.
  • D3 latent (D3§1.8): logits are reshaped to (S = 32, C = d/16). The probabilities get 1% unimix, and the latent is a sampled one-hot with straight-through gradients (B8).

They share the reshape and softmax and nothing else. Do not build D3 latents on SimNorm.

Tests. 1. simnorm(arange(16)/4, V = 8) gives the same 8-vector in each group: [0.04445499, 0.05708134, 0.07329389, 0.09411121, 0.12084118, 0.15516315, 0.19923344, 0.2558208]. 2. Each group sums to 1. 3. The output is invariant to adding a constant per group.

docs.title: B8. Unimix categorical, straight-through sample, KL and free bits (D3 only)
Math (D3§1.8, §2.14; outs.py:208-270)
docs.text:
• Unimix: p = (1 − u)·softmax(l) + u/C, and l' = log p, with u = 0.01.
  • Sample: idx ~ Cat(l'). The value is sg(onehot(idx)) + p − sg(p), so the gradient flows through the mixed p.
  • KL(P‖Q) = Σ_C softmax(l'_P)·(log_softmax(l'_P) − log_softmax(l'_Q)), summed over the S latents.
  • Unimix is re-applied after any sg. Store raw logits.
  • Free bits: max(KL_summed_over_S, 1.0) per (b, t).
  • dyn = KL(sg(post) ‖ prior) and rep = KL(post ‖ sg(prior)).

docs.title: B9. Q ensemble with random-pair reduction (T2 only; D3 has a single V critic plus a slow copy)
Math (T2§1.10-1.12, §3.14; world_model.py:186-216)
docs.text:
• Nq members (5 by default; 2 at 1M; 8 at 317M). Each member is NormedMLP([512, 512], 101, dropout = 0.01).
  • The members are vmapped over stacked params with the input broadcast, and each member gets its own dropout mask.
  • 'all' returns logits of shape (Nq, ..., K).
  • 'min' / 'avg': one permutation(Nq)[:2] per call, shared across the whole batch and horizon. Decode each head (B2), then take the min or the mean of the decoded scalars.

docs.title: B10. EMA target / slow network
docs.text:
Math. θ_tgt ← rate·θ + (1 − rate)·θ_tgt over all leaves, including norm scales and biases. Initialise with an exact copy.

Signature. ema_update(target, online, rate) = optax.incremental_update(online, target, rate). This is Ajax's existing LoadedTrainState.soft_update; reuse it.

docs.title: Math (time-major, rlax convention)
docs.text:
Index t is the transition t → t+1: - G_{T−1} = r_{T−1} + d_{T−1}·v_{T−1} - G_t = r_t + d_t·[(1 − λ_t)·v_t + λ_t·G_{t+1}]

Here v_t = V(s_{t+1}) is the bootstrap at the arrival state, d_t is the per-step discount times continuation (soft allowed), and λ_t is the per-step λ times "not cut".

Signature. lambda_returns(rew, disc, boot, lam) -> G with all inputs [T, ...] f32, as a reverse lax.scan with carry init boot[−1]. lam may be a scalar or [T, ...].

docs.title: Mapping from D3's lambda_return (agent.py:480-488)
docs.text:
D3's arrays have length L and the outputs are R_0..R_{L−2}. Set: - rew_t := rew[t+1] - disc_t := disc·(1 − term[t+1]) - lam_t := λ·(1 − last[t+1]) - boot_t := boot[t+1]

Uses: - D3 imagination: disc = 1 (contdisc), term = 1 − ĉ (soft), last = 0, boot = online v, λ = 0.95. - D3 replay: disc = 1 − 1/333, term/last = the replay flags, boot = imag R_0 reshaped to (B, K). - T2 one-step TD target: y = r + γ(1 − term)·Q̄min(h(s')). This is λ = 0 with T = 1. The bootstrap state is the encoded next obs (T2§2.3). - T2 planner value: Σ γ^t r̂_t + γ^H·Q_avg. This is λ = 1 with disc = γ.

Both T2 uses are degenerate cases. Use the block or inline them; neither needs it.

docs.title: False friends
docs.text:
1. D3 indexing. Step t uses r̂, ĉ and v of the next state, and the continuation weight w_t = Π_{i≤t} ĉ_i includes ĉ_0. The weight is computed outside this block.
  2. Ajax PQN compute_q_lambda_targets has the same recursion, but it casts done flags to bool, which breaks the soft ĉ. It also takes terminated and truncated separately. Do not reuse it for D3 as is.

docs.title: B12. Gaussian policy heads (shared primitives, separate heads; a false friend)
Shared primitives
docs.text:
def diag_gaussian_logpdf(x, mean, std) -> per-dim
def diag_gaussian_entropy(std) = 0.5*log(2*pi*e*std^2) per-dim
def reparam_sample(key, mean, std) = mean + std * eps
def tanh_squash_logdet(u, eps=1e-6) = sum(log(relu(1 - tanh(u)^2) + eps))   # T2 form (NOT distrax's exact log-det)

docs.title: D3 'bounded_normal' (D3§3.13; heads.py:146-155)
docs.text:
• μ = tanh(m) and σ = 0.9·sigmoid(s + 2) + 0.1, so σ ∈ (0.1, 1).
  • Normal(μ, σ) is not squashed: samples are unbounded, the log-prob is the plain Normal logpdf of the unclipped sample, and there is no Jacobian term.
  • The entropy is that of the unsquashed Normal, summed over dims.
  • The gradient estimator is REINFORCE on sg(action).
  • The env clips the action, the replay stores it unclipped, and the RSSM divides the action by max(1, abs(a)).
  • Both output Linears use outscale 0.01.

docs.title: T2 policy prior (T2§1.8-1.9, §2.12)
docs.text:
• log σ = −10 + 6·(tanh(raw) + 1), so log σ ∈ (−10, 2).
  • a = tanh(μ + σ·ε), with reparameterised gradients.
  • lp_g = Σ(−½ε² − log σ − ½ln2π). The log-prob subtracts tanh_squash_logdet(u, 1e-6).
  • The entropy bonus is scaled by n, the number of valid action dims. PE and HEAD differ here (T2 open question).
  • Planning and TD targets always use the sample. Acting with mpc = false in eval uses tanh(μ).
  • The last layer is N(0, 0.02) and is not zeroed.

docs.title: False friends
docs.text:
1. D3 is not a SAC-style tanh-Gaussian. Do not reuse Ajax's SquashedNormal for D3.
  2. T2's Jacobian uses +1e-6 inside the log. Ajax's SquashedNormal uses the exact stable log-det. At saturation (abs(u) > 7) T2's version is flat (log 1e-6), while the exact one has slope ±2. This changes PE gradients.
  3. The bounds are on different quantities. D3 bounds σ with a sigmoid and a +2 offset. T2 bounds log σ with a tanh.

docs.title: Tests (pinned)
docs.text:
1. D3: σ at raw 0 = 0.8927173; entropy per dim at init = 1.3054532; logpdf of an out-of-[−1, 1] sample is finite and has no Jacobian term.
  2. T2: log_std(0) = −4, log_std(+∞) = 2, log_std(−∞) = −10.
  3. T2 worked example. Inputs: ε = [0.5, −1], μ = [0.1, −0.2], raw = [0, 1].
Quantity Value log σ [−4, 0.5695648] u [0.10915782, −1.9674977] a [0.10872632, −0.9616578] lp_g 0.967558 Σ squash log-det −2.5992928 HEAD lp 3.5668507 HEAD scaled_entropy ≈ −n·lp_g −1.935116 PE log_pi = n·(Σ(−½ε² − log σ) − ½ln2π) − squash 6.372286

docs.title: Math (T2§3.1-3.24, pseudocode 3.C)
docs.text:
• Warm start. μ ← shift(prev_mean) (last row 0; zeros if t0). σ ← max_std. σ is never warm-started.
  • The P = 24 π-trajectories are fixed for all iterations but re-scored every iteration.
  • Each iteration (6, or 8 if A ≥ 20):
  • Sample the N − P Gaussian candidates and clip them to [−1, 1] before evaluation.
  • V = nan_to_num(value_fn(·)).
  • Take the top-E elites from the current iteration only.
  • score = softmax(0.5·(eV − max eV)). The temperature multiplies.
  • μ = Σ s·eA / (Σs + 1e-9).
  • σ = sqrt(Σ s·(eA − μ_new)² / (Σs + 1e-9)), the biased std around the new mean, clipped to [0.05, 2].
  • Mask μ and σ for MT after the clip.
  • Final action. Pick k ~ Cat(score) and take a = eA[0, k]. Add σ[0]·N(0, I) if not eval. Clip to [−1, 1]. Store prev_mean = μ (not the executed action).

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MPPIConfig: horizon=3; iterations=6; num_samples=512; num_pi_trajs=24; num_elites=64
                  min_std=0.05; max_std=2.0; temperature=0.5
def mppi_plan(key, value_fn, pi_actions | None, prev_mean, t0, eval_mode, cfg, action_mask=None)
    -> (action[A], new_prev_mean[H,A], aux{score, mean, std})
# value_fn(key, actions[H,N,A]) -> V[N]  (caller closes over z, networks; T2: Σγ^t r̂(z_t,a_t) + γ^H Q_avg(z_H, π(z_H)))

All shapes are static. Use lax.fori_loop, lax.top_k and jax.random.categorical(log score). (Built otherwise: see the status note at the top.) Per-env t0 and prev_mean come from the actor state (vmapped over envs; T2§3.A).

docs.title: Tests (pinned)
docs.text:
1. Update step. Inputs: H = 2, E = 3, A = 1, eV = [1, 2, 4], eA[0] = [0, .5, 1], eA[1] = [−1, 0, .2].
  2. score = [0.14024438, 0.2312239, 0.6285317]
  3. μ = [0.74414366, −0.01453803]
  4. σ = [0.3641262, 0.4064164]
  5. Warm start shifts only μ, and the last row is 0. σ resets to 2. t0 gives zeros.
  6. The π columns are unchanged across iterations.
  7. Candidates lie in [−1, 1].
  8. eval_mode removes only the final noise.
  9. Sanity: with V = −‖a − a‖², μ converges toward a.
  10. Under jit and vmap over envs, the result equals the per-env loop.

docs.title: B14. Latent rollout scan (both)
docs.text:
Signature. rollout(step_fn, carry0, length, xs=None, policy=None, key=None) -> (carry_T, outs[T]), a time-major lax.scan. It takes either given inputs (xs) or a policy callable sampled per step with split keys.

Uses: - D3: observe (posterior step with is_first masking, Algorithm B); imagine (the policy sees sg(carry); prior straight-through sample, Algorithm C), with H = 15. - T2: consistency rollout with buffer actions over H = 3; π-trajectory rollout (P = 24); planner value rollout. The T2 dynamics are deterministic.

Tests. 1. The scan equals a Python loop. 2. With a linear step function, the result matches the closed form. 3. Keys are split per step: no repeated noise. 4. Gradient flows through the carry unless the caller applies sg.

docs.title: B15. RSSM block-GRU core and observe/imagine steps (D3 only)
Math
docs.text:
The core follows D3 Algorithm A: - x0, x1, x2 = SiLU(RMS(Linear_d(·))) of deter, the flattened stoch, and a / sg(max(1, abs(a))). - Concatenate per block with each block's deter slice, then BlockLinear(D) → RMS over the full D → SiLU. - BlockLinear(3D) with no norm and no activation. The per-block layout is [r | c | u]. - r = σ(r), c = tanh(r·c) (the reset gate scales the whole candidate), u = σ(u − 1). - h' = u·c + (1 − u)·h.

Observe and imagine steps follow Algorithms B and C, including the double masking of is_first (zero deter, stoch and prevact before the core, and zero the encoded action again after one-hot). The initial state is zeros, not learned.

docs.title: Shared sub-blocks
docs.text: NormedMLP (B4), BlockLinear (B6), unimix straight-through (B8), rollout (B14), and Ajax memory._mask_reset for is_first zeroing (zero fresh carry).

docs.title: False friend: Ajax MemoryCell("gru")
docs.text:
Ajax's MemoryCell("gru") (flax GRUCell) is a different cell: - the reset gate applies only to the recurrent term; - there is no −1 update bias; - it is dense, not block-diagonal; - it has no norm or hidden layer.

Do not reuse it. T2 has no recurrence: the latent is re-encoded every env step.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
1. With the dyngru kernel and bias zeroed: u = σ(−1) = 0.2689414 exactly, and h' = 0.7310586·h.
  2. is_first gives h = core(0, 0, 0) regardless of the carry and the previous action. A one-hot of action index 0 is masked.
  3. Block structure: output block k depends on other blocks only through x0.
  4. Shapes and parameter counts at 12M (d = 256, S = 32, C = 16, A = 6). These are derived from the reference layer shapes, not from a reference run.
  5. dynin0 524,800; dynin1 131,584; dynin2 2,048; dynhid0 2,101,248; dyngru 1,579,008; core total 4,338,688.
  6. Prior MLP 722,432; posterior 721,920.

docs.title: B16. Bernoulli head (D3 continue; T2 termination as an Extension)
docs.text:
Math. loss(l, c) = −[c·log σ(l) + (1 − c)·log σ(−l)]. Soft labels are allowed.

Variants. - D3 (D3§2.13): target c = 0.997·(1 − is_terminal), a soft label; never is_last. Imagination uses σ(l) as ĉ (γ folded in). - T2 HEAD episodic (T2§1.7, §2.7, §3.11): off by default, so it belongs in an Extension. It is a hard 0/1 label, BCE-mean on the predicted z_1..z_H. Planning thresholds it at 0.5 and treats termination as absorbing.

Tests. 1. l = 0 gives log 2 = 0.6931472 for any c. 2. At c = 0.997 the minimum is at l = logit(0.997) = 5.8061385, where loss = 0.0204229 and the gradient ≈ 0.

docs.title: Builders (shared optax primitives)
docs.text:
def clip_by_agc_per_tensor(clip=0.3, pmin=1e-3)   # custom: g * 1/max(1, ||g|| / (clip*max(pmin, ||p||))) per LEAF
def laprop_agc(lr=4e-5, warmup=1000, agc=0.3, pmin=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-20):
    sched = optax.join_schedules([optax.linear_schedule(0., lr, warmup), optax.constant_schedule(lr)], [warmup])
    return optax.chain(clip_by_agc_per_tensor(agc, pmin),
                       optax.scale_by_rms(decay=beta2, eps=eps, eps_in_sqrt=False, bias_correction=True),
                       optax.ema(decay=beta1, debias=True),          # == D3 scale_by_momentum
                       optax.scale_by_learning_rate(sched))
def adam_grouped(lr=3e-4, lr_scales={"encoder": 0.3}, label_fn=..., clip_norm=20.0, eps=1e-8):
    return optax.chain(optax.clip_by_global_norm(clip_norm),        # ONE global norm over all groups
                       optax.multi_transform({g: optax.adam(lr * s, eps=eps) for g, s in ...}, label_fn))

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
• D3 (D3§4.3-4.7; opt.py:109-164): one optimiser over all modules. The order is AGC, then RMS, then momentum, then the lr. The first update has lr = 0 (warmup).
  • T2 (T2§2.9-2.14):
  • World model: adam_grouped(3e-4, {encoder: 0.3}), eps 1e-8, global clip 20.
  • π: a separate chain(clip_by_global_norm(20), adam(3e-4, eps=1e-5)).
  • Torch's clip coefficient adds +1e-6 to the norm; this is negligible.

docs.title: False friends
docs.text:
1. optax.adaptive_grad_clip is NFNet unit-wise AGC. Example with p = I₂ and g = [[3, 0], [0, 0.1]]:
  2. D3 per-tensor AGC gives [[0.42402855, 0], [0, 0.01413429]].
  3. optax gives [[0.3, 0], [0, 0.1]].
  4. Its axis argument cannot express "whole tensor" for a tree with mixed ranks, so a custom transform is needed.
  5. Ajax get_adam_tx defaults to eps 1e-5 and has no param groups. T2's world-model Adam needs eps 1e-8. Its π Adam needs 1e-5.
  6. Order of clip and groups. In T2 the global clip must come before multi_transform. Clipping per group is wrong.
  7. β₂. The D3 paper says 0.99 and the code says 0.999 (D3 OQ 2). Keep it as a config value.

docs.title: Tests (pinned)
docs.text:
1. The laprop_agc chain equals the D3 reference transforms (copied from opt.py) to max abs difference 2.1e-14 over 5 steps on a {(5, 3), (3,), (2, 4, 3)} tree.
  2. The first update is all zeros (lr_0 = 0).
  3. AGC: p = ones(2, 2), g = 3·ones gives 0.3·ones (cap 0.6). p = 0, g = [3, 4] gives [1.8e-4, 2.4e-4]. Include the unit-wise counterexample above.
  4. T2 grouped Adam: g_enc = 30 and g_rest = 40 are globally clipped to 12 and 16. The first-step updates are −8.99994e-5 (encoder) and −2.99998e-4 (rest).
  5. Scale invariance (D3): multiplying the loss by 1000 leaves the LaProp updates unchanged (eps 1e-20).

docs.title: B18. Sequence replay (shared ring buffer, per-algorithm window predicate)
Design (pure-JAX, on device)
docs.text:
• Storage. Per-env ring buffers [N_env, cap] of step rows {obs…, action, reward, is_first, is_last, is_terminal, (+ latent fields)}, a per-env write pointer and a per-env "committed" pointer.
  • Sampling returns (batch, (env_idx, start_idx)). The indices are required for D3's latent write-back. Validity is a predicate over the window flags.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text: D3 (D3§5; replay.py) T2 (T2§2.1, §4.6-4.9) Window 65 steps (64 trained + 1 context), stride-1 starts H+1 = 4 rows Episode boundaries windows cross them (mid-window is_first is normal) windows never cross them (valid iff no is_first in rows 1..H) Sampling uniform over items, with replacement; online queue of non-overlapping fresh windows popped first (train only) uniform over episodes, then start (= uniform over valid windows for fixed-length episodes) Annotation is_first[:, 0] = 1; is_last ∨= roll(is_first, −1), last column excluded none Freshness everything inserted is sampleable only completed episodes are sampleable Extra fields stored deter/stoch per step, written back after each update (indices 1..64) none Capacity 5e6 items 1e6 transitions (b67b21c: 2000 episodes × 501 rows)

docs.title: False friends
docs.text:
1. Action alignment.
  2. D3 row t = (x_t, r_t received on entering x_t, a_t chosen after x_t). prevact for row t is the action stored at row t − 1.
  3. T2 row k = (o_k, a_{k−1}, r_{k−1}), the action that led into o_k, with a placeholder at row 0.
  4. Rewards align the same way; actions are shifted by one. Pick one storage convention and derive the other in the sampler.
  5. Ajax's collector writes SARS′ Transitions under gymnax auto-reset. Each step is (obs, action, reward, terminated, truncated, next_obs), with next_obs = the final obs on done. So an episode has T rows, and the terminal obs exists only as next_obs.
  6. T2 maps cleanly onto this: a window is H consecutive transitions with no done among the first H−1, with obs[0..H] = obs_t..obs_{t+H−1} plus next_obs_{t+H−1}.
  7. D3 does not map cleanly. It needs the terminal obs as its own row (is_last, plus is_terminal if terminal) so that the RSSM filters it and the reward and continue heads train on it. That is T+1 rows per episode, which breaks per-env lockstep. See Q1.
  8. Ajax get_buffer(sequence_length=…) (flashbax trajectory buffer) gives stride-1, episode-crossing windows like D3's. However, it returns no indices (so no write-back), has no online queue, and has no episode-validity filter.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
1. D3 annotation. Flags is_first = [0, 0, 1, 0], is_last = [0, 0, 0, 0] become is_first = [1, 0, 1, 0] and is_last = [0, 1, 0, 0].
  2. T2 validity. No sampled window contains is_first after row 0. Over 10⁵ draws, a chi-square test is uniform over valid starts. In a buffer with one completed episode and one running episode, no sample comes from the running one.
  3. Alignment round trip. Ajax Transitions → T2 slice gives obs[H] == next_obs of the last transition.
  4. Write-back. Values written at the returned (env, idx) are read back on the next sample of the same window.
  5. Ring wrap-around keeps the per-env order.

docs.title: B19. Small shared utilities and non-shared look-alikes
docs.text:
• Discount from horizon.
  • D3: γ = 1 − 1/333 = 0.996997.
  • T2: γ(T) = clip(1 − 5/T, 0.95, 0.995), giving {T = 100: 0.95, 500: 0.99, 1000: 0.995, 50: 0.95}.
  • Signature: discount_from_horizon(h, lo=None, hi=None), with h = 333 (D3) or h = T/5 (T2).
  • Mixed precision.
  • D3: bf16 compute, with f32 params, norm statistics, distributions, losses, returns and normalisers.
  • T2: f32 (HEAD uses TF32 matmuls).
  • Every module takes dtype. Distribution, loss and normaliser code upcasts to f32. Parity tests set jax_default_matmul_precision="highest".
  • Categorical pick. jax.random.categorical replaces T2's Gumbel-max and np.random.choice, and D3's sampling. (Not for T2's elite: sample_elite keeps the inverse CDF.)
  • Not shared (look-alikes):
  • MSE losses:
    • D3 symlog-MSE decoder: (pred − symlog(y))², summed over feature dims, no ½, mean over (B, T).
    • T2 consistency loss: plain MSE, mean over batch and latent dim, no symlog, weighted by ρ^t and divided by H.
  • Temporal weights: D3 uses cumprod(ĉ) including ĉ_0; T2 uses ρ^t = 0.5^t.
  • Loss reductions: D3 takes means over (B, T) and H. T2 uses Σ_t ρ^t·mean_B, divided by H (or H·Nq for values).

docs.title: Open questions for the user (shared-block scope)
docs.text:
Resolved since: (1) the row collector's hold tick, i.e. option (a) (DESIGN.md §5.2); (2) a round of episodes becomes sampleable when its held tick passes (§4.4); (3) no blocks/ package, blocks promoted on their second consumer (§3); (4) f32 only (D4).

  1. D3 replay rows under Ajax's auto-reset environments. This blocks B18 for D3. The options:
  2. (a) An explicit-reset env wrapper, as in the embodied driver. After an is_last step, the next step call ignores the action and emits the reset obs with is_first = 1 and reward 0. This gives one row per vector step, keeps lockstep and reproduces the reference stream exactly, including the train-ratio clock counting reset steps.
  3. (b) Keep auto-reset, and write 2 rows on done steps with per-env write pointers.
  4. (c) Store transitions, and synthesise the terminal row at sample time.

Recommended: (a). It is the reference's own data stream and the simplest correct option. 2. T2 "only completed episodes are sampleable". Should we implement a per-env committed pointer (recommended; cheap, exact) or accept per-step visibility as a documented deviation? 3. Package location and retrofitting. The proposal is a new src/ajax/blocks/ package with transforms, twohot, normalizers, layers, distributions, ensemble, returns, planning, rssm, optim and replay. Should existing Ajax code be retrofitted onto these blocks now, or left alone? The candidates are PQN q-lambda → B11, soft_update → B10 (already identical) and get_adam_tx → B17. 4. bf16 support (D3 OQ 10). Should the blocks support a bf16 compute dtype from day one (recommended), or start f32-only?

Recommendations that do not need a user decision: - Use the symmetric two-hot sum for both algorithms (B2). - Use the literal-constant D3 initialiser (B5). Not built: D23. - Use normal(0.02), not truncated_normal(0.02), for T2 (B5). - Use a custom per-tensor AGC (B17).

docs.title: TD-MPC2: implementation reference (merged and verified)
docs.text: This document gives the Ajax (JAX) implementer one place to work from instead of the paper and the code. Each row merges the extractor's spec with the adversarial verifier's corrections and the items the verifier found missing. Re-checks made during the merge are logged in §0.5.
